title: Sr Manager, Real Estate and Workplace
description:
About ALSO.

We’re ALSO, an electric mobility company originally conceived as a part of Rivian. We’re a passionate team of builders, dreamers, doers and innovators, focused on creating entirely new (not to mention, innovative and delightful) vertically integrated, small EVs designed to meet the global mobility challenges of today and tomorrow. Our mission is to inspire everyone to ride ALSO—replacing many local car, truck and SUV miles with ones on vehicles that are more affordable, more enjoyable and 10-50x more efficient.



ALSO is seeking an execution-driven Sr Manager, Real Estate & Workplace, to lead workplace strategy, projects, programs, and teams based in our Palo Alto HQ for a global multi-site portfolio spanning office, R&D labs, commercial hubs, and retail.


This role owns team leadership, strategic planning, critical project execution, and executive-level representation alongside the Director, partnering daily with IT, Engineering, Purchasing, Finance, Legal, Insurance, People, and cross functional key stakeholders. Success requires ability to prioritize in a fast-paced environment, drive R&D projects to execution, disciplined governance, financial rigor, 3rd party management, and the ability to anticipate space and workplace service needs (ie, mail, logistics, culinary, janitorial, and moves). Onsite 3-5 days/week, with off-hours availability for time-sensitive and critical issues.



What You Will Do 

Team & Program Leadership

 - Lead the Real Estate & Workplace team (operations, facilities, mail, logistics, culinary, janitorial) as deputy lead, balancing competing priorities with long-term focus.

 - Manage projects end to end, including portfolio administration, R&D lab build-outs, workplace programs, and occupancy data.

Strategic Space Planning & Occupancy Analysis

 - Own headcount and occupancy analysis, turning hiring plans and growth into space strategy, capacity models, and scenarios.

 - Drive long-range workplace strategy and partner with Finance and Analytics on forecasting and tradeoff recommendations to leadership.

Vendor, Contract & Budget Management

 - Manage vendors, consultants, landlords, and GCs with negotiation and financial accountability.

 - Own budget tracking, forecasting, and RFPs with Purchasing and Finance, and oversee lease transactions end to end with Legal and Risk.

Cross-Functional Partnership

 - Act as the connective tissue across IT, Engineering, Purchasing, Finance, Legal/Compliance, Analytics, and G&A.

 - Support Executive Assistants on space, logistics, and events, and communicate credibly with landlords, brokers, executives, and building inspectors.

Technical R&D Project Delivery & Operations

 - Coordinate lab infrastructure and equipment installs with Engineering and vendors.

 - Partner with the IT and EHS & Security Manager on life-safety and compliance, and serve as a point of contact for after-hours facilities emergencies.

Process Governance & Data Enablement

 - Implement standard PM frameworks, ticketing, and KPI/milestone dashboards.

 - Adopt new technology and AI-assisted tools to streamline workflows as the portfolio grows.



What You Will Bring 

 - 7+ years of progressive real estate, workplace, or facilities operations experience, with demonstrated growth from individual execution into a leadership scope.

 - Track record leading teams and operating as a trusted second-in-command.

 - Comfortable partnering across IT, Engineering, Finance, Legal, and Purchasing, and communicating credibly from AHJs to executives.

 - Working knowledge of commercial leases, vendor contracts, and budget/financial management.

 - Comfortable with ambiguity and fast-changing priorities; adaptable to new technology, software, and AI-assisted tools.

 - Familiarity with EHS, physical security concepts, and specialized lab/R&D infrastructure preferred (this role partners with a dedicated EHS & Security Manager rather than owning those programs directly).

 - Experience scaling high-tech, EV, or R&D lab environments strongly preferred.

 - Able to respond to occasional off-hours emergencies.



The salary for this position ranges from $200,000 - $220,000 per year, depending on experience, qualifications, and location.


Perks and Benefits

 - Robust health coverage. Excellent health, dental and vision insurance covered up to 100% by Also. with FSA & HSA options.

 - One Medical membership and dedicated insurance advocates.

 - Rich fertility and family building benefits with Progyny.

 - Flexible time off. 

 - 401(k) match.



Why ALSO.

We’re passionate about helping the world find a better way to get there—wherever it is you’re headed.

We’re located in the heart of Silicon Valley and have brought together a world-class team from some of the biggest brands in the technology, automotive, cycling, outdoor recreation and retail spaces. 

Together we’re working hands-on to imagine, design and build an entirely new solution to a global set of transportation challenges.

Drug Substance Engineering Internship Overview
Envision spending your summer working with energetic colleagues and inspirational leaders, all while gaining world-class experience in one of the most dynamic organizations in the pharmaceutical industry. This is a reality for AbbVie Interns.
Micronization of drug substance is a critical process in API manufacturing for ensuring downstream critical quality attributes. Micronization processes such as pin milling and jet milling leverage feed rate control to optimize the process performance, and while feed rate is well understood for many powder systems there is a gap in understanding the feed rate control of poorly flowing materials in micronization techniques.
The Drug Substance Engineering Intern within Product Development, Science, and Technology (PDS&T) will help establish a systematic approach to understand how the physical properties of powder systems impact their feeding performance in micronization processes.
Key responsibilities include:
Experimental studies to understand and characterize powder properties
Evaluate performance of micronization techniques (i.e. jet mill, pin mill) with various feed mechanisms
Analyze data and trends to identify signatures for process performance
Develop and verify computational models
Summarize and present findings in departmental and cross-functional settings

The Associate Director, Pricing is the International pricing lead for RINVOQ . The role sets RINVOQ's International pricing strategy and preserves the integrity of RINVOQ's price across its indications and markets. It turns pricing analysis into clear guidance, robust business cases and accurate financial assumptions, and supports Area and affiliate teams in achieving broad, timely and sustainable patient access that reflects the value of RINVOQ.
Key Responsibilities:
Pricing Strategy and Guidance:
Develop and maintain International pricing guidance for RINVOQ (price corridors and launch and re-pricing recommendations) in line with brand strategy, the Integrated Access Strategy (IAS) and corporate objectives.
Apply the Strategic Pricing Framework to define the price potential of new indications and formulations, and recommend indication and country launch sequencing that maximizes International value.
Develop contracting guidance and access models that address payer objections and affordability concerns while preserving the integrity of RINVOQ's price.
Monitor International pricing policy and competitor pricing, and flag risks and opportunities for RINVOQ early.
Business Cases and Pricing Governance:
Lead the development, review and challenge of RINVOQ pricing business cases from affiliates and Areas, ensuring each is analytically sound, compliant with International pricing governance and ready for decision.
Prepare and present business cases to the Executive Pricing Councils, with a clear recommendation, quantified financial impact, risks and mitigations.
PVTO and IRP Analysis:
Build and run price-volume trade-off (PVTO) analyses to evaluate price and access scenarios, breakeven volumes and the net revenue impact of pricing decisions at market and International level.
Assess International Reference Pricing (IRP) implications of every proposed price change, launch price and confidential agreement. Quantify cross-country spill-over and recommend the sequencing and price levels that preserve the integrity of RINVOQ's price across International markets.
Work with International Pricing analysts to design, run and interpret IRP, PVTO and launch-sequencing models, and turn the outputs into clear recommendations for senior stakeholders.
Plan and LRP:
Own the RINVOQ pricing assumptions in the annual Plan and Long Range Plan (LRP) process, including price evolution, launch timing, price erosion, IRP impact and risk and opportunity scenarios.
Collect, challenge and align pricing assumptions with Areas, affiliates and Finance, so that forecasts are consistent and explained.
Cross-Functional Partnership:
Area and affiliates (primary partners): help key markets turn International pricing guidance into local outcomes, covering price potential, negotiation strategy, scenarios, fallback positions and objection handling for national and sub-national negotiations.
Therapy Area teams (primary partners): make sure the pricing position is reflected in the RINVOQ IAS and brand strategy, and that indication priorities reflect price potential.
HTA: align price potential with the expected HTA outcome and value story and assess the price implications of HTA evidence and comparator choices.
Finance: reconcile pricing inputs with Plan, LRP and business case financials, and agree the net revenue impact of pricing decisions.
Act as the internal subject matter expert on RINVOQ pricing, IRP and pricing analytics.
Essential
Bachelor's degree in Finance, Economics, Health Economics, Statistics, Mathematics, Pharmacy or a related field.
At least 3 years' experience in pharmaceutical pricing, market access, health economics or commercial finance.
Strong quantitative and modelling skills, with experience building and interpreting pricing, forecasting or scenario models in Excel.
Working knowledge of International Reference Pricing and its impact on launch sequencing and price setting.
Ability to condense complex analysis into clear, concise recommendations for senior audiences. Excellent written and spoken English.
Able to influence without authority in a matrix organization, make sound calls on incomplete data, and challenge affiliate and Area proposals constructively.
Desired
Hands-on experience with pricing business cases for executive pricing committees, PVTO analysis and Plan/LRP pricing assumptions.
Knowledge of P&R systems in key markets, including Australia, Canada, China, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, Spain and the UK.
Understanding of HTA and health economic principles from a payer perspective.
Experience in immunology or another multi-indication specialty brand.

The Director Organizational Culture is responsible for leading the evolution of AbbVie’s culture transformation agenda. This leader will shape, amplify, and sustain a culture that enables meta-AbbVie, accelerates execution of the business strategy and strengthens organizational performance.
This role extends beyond traditional employee engagement, communications, or culture stewardship and is accountable for embedding culture into how the enterprise operates, makes decisions, develops leaders, deploys talent, rewards performance, collaborates, innovates, and delivers results. The role will translate AbbVie's cultural aspirations into practical expectations, mechanisms, and measures across business functions and geographies.
The successful candidate will serve as an architect and catalyst for enterprise-wide transformation. AbbVie’s Business Technology Solutions (BTS) Information Research (IR) organization is seeking an Engineer, Technology I to help deliver trusted, well-structured, AI-ready data products within ARCH, AbbVie’s R&D Convergence Hub. As part of the DELOS team — Data Exploration and Linked Outcome Solutions — this role helps build the reliable data foundations needed to advance analytics, reporting, knowledge graph capabilities, machine learning, and AI-enabled use cases across R&D.
In this role, you will independently design and develop data pipelines and curated data assets within assigned projects, applying established architecture, engineering patterns, and governance standards. You will collect, integrate, normalize, model, and document research data; implement quality checks; and support publication to the ARCH knowledge graph. Rather than developing AI models directly, you will prepare reliable, accessible, and appropriately governed data for analytics, data science, and AI-enabled use cases.
Working with R&D stakeholders, data scientists, machine learning engineers, platform teams, architects, and data owners, you will translate defined scientific and business requirements into dependable data solutions. You will perform routine and complex engineering tasks independently, understand project objectives and your contribution to them, adapt your approach when needed, and communicate progress, risks, and issues. You will collaborate with internal and contracted engineers on assigned work, seeking guidance on broader architecture decisions and escalating issues outside your scope.
Under the direction of the Associate Director – Data Strategy, AI & Knowledge Enablement, this role contributes to AbbVie’s R&D data transformation by delivering consistent, well-documented data solutions within agreed project scope and timelines. You will learn and apply new methods and technologies to help research partners use trusted data for scientific decision-making.
**This is a hybrid role based in Lake County, IL (Tue, Wed, Thu)
Responsibilities
Data Pipeline & Product Development: Independently design and develop pipelines and curated data assets for assigned scientific or business use cases. Collect, integrate, normalize, model, and transform data from databases, applications, APIs, licensed external sources, and other systems using established engineering patterns.
Reliable Project Delivery: Perform routine and complex engineering tasks competently and independently, producing reliable and consistent results within agreed timelines. Understand broader project objectives, organize assigned work, and adapt your approach when requirements or priorities change.
AI & Knowledge Graph Data Preparation: Clean, standardize, enrich, and structure data and documents for downstream analytics, machine learning, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and knowledge discovery. Organize metadata, support established chunking and embedding workflows, and prepare curated assets for publication to the ARCH knowledge graph.
Data Quality & Technical Documentation: Implement defined data quality checks and maintain technical documentation for pipelines and data assets, including metadata, lineage, transformations, assumptions, and usage guidance. Apply established access, privacy, licensing, and governance requirements.
Collaboration & Progress Communication: Work with scientific, business, engineering, and platform partners to clarify requirements and deliver assigned work. Clearly present project objectives, progress, risks, and issues; collaborate with internal and contracted contributors without responsibility for directing their delivery.
Operations & Method Improvement: Monitor assigned pipelines for performance, freshness, failures, and resource use; troubleshoot and resolve issues within your scope and escalate when needed. Learn and implement new methods and technologies and contribute to reusable patterns and automation with guidance as appropriate.
Compliance & Standards: Understand and adhere to applicable Corporate and Divisional policies, including code of conduct, safety, GxP compliance, data security, data governance, relevant regulatory or contractual requirements, and the software development lifecycle.
Bachelor’s Degree in Information Technology, Data Engineering, Computer Science, Informatics, Life Sciences, or a related field plus 4 years of experience; Master’s Degree plus 2 years of experience.
Practical experience developing data pipelines or data solutions using SQL, Python, and ETL/ELT patterns, with knowledge of workflow orchestration tools such as Airflow.
Theoretical and practical knowledge of data integration, data modeling, data storage, and modern data platforms sufficient to independently complete routine and complex engineering tasks within established standards.
Experience cleaning, standardizing, transforming, and documenting data for analytics or scientific use, including applying data quality checks and organizing metadata.
Ability to organize assigned work, multitask, meet timelines, understand project objectives, adapt your approach when needed, and learn and apply new methods and technologies.
Strong written and oral English communication skills, with the ability to explain technical work, present project objectives and progress, and collaborate with scientific, business, and technical partners.
Hands-on data engineering: develop reusable, well-structured data assets for defined analytics and AI-enabled use cases.

The Facility Planner serves as a key figure in optimizing the use of an organization's physical spaces, ensuring they are both effective and efficient. Purpose :
The Global Connected Logistics and Internet of Things (IoT) Strategy Lead shapes and advances enterprise capabilities that improve visibility, product protection, sustainability and operational performance across the global distribution and logistics network.
This individual contributor role connects business strategy with practical implementation. The individual will lead global initiatives, coordinate requirements and interdependencies across global functions and regions, and partner with Business Technology Solutions (BTS), external providers and operational teams to deploy solutions that are scalable, viable and fit for purpose. There is a travel element to this role, with business meetings in US and Europe, primarily but not limited to those regions.
The successful candidate will bring a combination of strategic thinking, program leadership, commercial and vendor management, and strong cross-functional influence. The position is designed for an experienced supply chain, logistics, technology-enabled transformation professional and does not require deep engineering expertise in every device or platform.
Responsibilities:
Own and continuously develop AbbVie's global connected logistics strategy and multi-year roadmap. This covers shipment visibility, temperature monitoring, RFID, Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE), geolocation and other monitoring technologies, with the goal of improving product protection, risk management and operational decision-making.
Lead the assessment of emerging logistics technologies and monitoring solutions. Work with regional and functional teams to decide which capabilities to pilot, scale globally, integrate into existing processes or phase out, based on business value and operational fit. Lead priority device and IoT initiatives from opportunity definition through implementation, coordinating requirements, milestones, risks and dependencies to speed up deployment and deliver measurable business value.
Partner with Business Technology Solutions (BTS) and technology partners to turn business requirements into functional, data and integration requirements. Make sure solutions are scalable, supportable and compliant with Good Distribution Practice (GDP).
Manage strategic device, monitoring and technology-provider relationships through performance reviews, roadmap alignment and issue resolution to strengthen service reliability, innovation and value. Own the annual connected logistics budget, including forecasting, spend tracking, vendor invoices, financial reporting and actions to make sure investments deliver expected value.
Partner with Global Supply Chain Security, regional teams, third-party logistics providers and freight forwarders to assess emerging threats. Build product protection and transportation security requirements into logistics strategies, operating models and technology deployments. Implement risk-based security standards and solutions (e.g., TAPA). Lead cross-functional initiatives that improve product security, including programs that make high-value products less visible during transportation and distribution. Together, these reduce theft, diversion and other supply chain risks and strengthen supply chain resilience.

Global Lab Solutions (GLS), part of Operations Quality Assurance, designs and enables the systems, capabilities, standards, and partnerships that strengthen laboratory performance, support pipeline progression, and promote consistent, compliant execution across AbbVie’s global Quality Control network. The role provides independent oversight and decision-making for QC analytical implementation, including review and challenge of validation, co-validation, and method transfer strategies; assessment of laboratory capability and readiness; and determination of the QC method design needed for dependable commercial execution. Success requires deep analytical lifecycle expertise, enterprise thinking, strong risk-based judgment, and the ability to lead across a global matrix without direct authority.

Lead the global QC analytical implementation and lifecycle strategy for assigned late-stage and commercial products.

The Global QC Product Lead helps ensure that AbbVie’s analytical methods can be executed reliably where and when they are needed. The Customer Logistics Planner is the execution and control hub for outbound shipments in the Gaucho third-party manufacturing model. The role coordinates end-to-end order and shipment execution from second-leg stock transport order creation through shipment departure, documentation archiving, exception resolution and stakeholder communication.
The planner helps protect supply continuity and customer service by maintaining accurate system transactions, compliant shipping documentation, timely visibility and early escalation of risks.
The Customer Logistics Planner owns shipment execution and visibility within the Shipment CoE, while Transportation retains ownership of carrier strategy, transportation procurement and carrier management.
Key responsibilities
Order and delivery execution: Create and manage second-leg STOs and outbound deliveries in SAP; update weights and measurements using the Nota Fiscal; create packing lists; post goods issue for departed shipments; and provide accurate shipment data to support commercial invoicing.
Shipping and export documentation: Prepare pro forma invoices and other shipment documentation for customs and payment purposes; check completeness and compliance; and archive final shipping documentation in the designated repository.
Shipment control and visibility: Maintain shipping forecasts and master arrival schedules, monitor open orders and deliveries, review allocation issues and blocks, and escalate overdue or at-risk shipments.
Exception management: Coordinate resolution of shipment delays, booking constraints, documentation gaps, complaints, discrepancies, complex lane requirements and urgent business requests, working with Transportation and other relevant functions as needed.
Stakeholder coordination: Coordinate daily with the third-party manufacturer, Global Supply Planning, Transportation, affiliates, Global Trade Compliance, Finance, Quality, Planning and other supply chain partners. Affiliate and customer service: Provide timely updates and pre-alert information, align around holiday schedules and market-specific requirements, and support affiliates with complex export and transportation needs.
Performance and governance: Support operational and carrier performance reviews by providing shipment data, issue trends and execution insights, together with KPI reporting, month-end activities, audit readiness, process controls and the Calendar of Discipline.
Continuous improvement: Identify process gaps, improve standard work, strengthen controls and visibility, and contribute to scalable solutions as shipment volumes and regional complexity increase. Support stabilization and continuous improvement of new operating models as processes and interfaces mature.

Internal: Shipment CoE, Transportation, Global Supply Planning, Finance, Global Trade Compliance, Quality Assurance, Planning, manufacturing and distribution teams, and commercial affiliates.
External: Third-party manufacturer, freight forwarders, service providers, destination-market partners and carriers, with carrier engagement coordinated through Transportation where applicable.

Minimum three years of relevant experience in logistics, customer logistics, order management, supply chain execution, or a comparable environment.
Hands-on ERP experience, preferably SAP, including order, delivery, shipment, or inventory transactions.
Experience with international shipping documentation, export processes, customs-related requirements, and cross-functional stakeholder coordination.
Fluent written and spoken English; additional languages are an advantage for international market support.

The CS Product Office works collaboratively and strategically with colleagues across the product lifecycle to identify, evaluate, understand and communicate the safety profile of our drugs to protect patients worldwide.

In partnership with the PST Lead, manage multiple Product Safety Teams across multiple Therapeutic Areas. This includes meeting planning and facilitation, meeting minute documentation and post-meeting/general team management activities. Increase meeting productivity and advance decision-making effectively through the application of strong skillsets in influencing, leadership, relationship building, proactive-ness, curiosity, active engagement and developing strategic thinking.
Proactively utilize experience and knowledge to support the PST Lead in framing safety issues and making decisions. Anticipate possible outcomes of safety issues and provide guidance to the PST Lead so that he/she can be proactively prepared. Systematically analyze the impact of safety decisions and connect the dots across other decisions, discussions, and actions. Communicate perspectives to PST Lead and collaborate with other PST PMs and the PST Lead on solutions.
In partnership with PST Lead, manage escalation of safety issues and decisions to management and Safety Review Board (SRB). Create escalation documentation (e. g. SRB presentations) and help prepare the PST Leads for discussions. Manage the close-out of SRB action items for assigned PSTs.
Support the PST Lead in strengthening internal partnership/influence and establishing their role as the company leader of safety issues related to their compounds/products. Identify new opportunities for the PST Lead to build relationships and present thought leadership to peers.
Support the PST Lead in strengthening external engagement/presence by providing recommendations on channels for expanding external engagement including topic ideas for publications, conferences to present at key industry relationships to develop, etc. Support the creation of content for external engagement activities.
Drive timely development of key PST deliverables by planning and facilitating productive working sessions to create deliverables; share perspectives; push the thinking to create robust deliverables, suggest improvements, and connect the dots.
Support inspection /audit readiness activities. Engage in supporting PST-related inspection/audit activities and CAPAs/commitments.
BA/BS/MA/MS (nursing or pharmacy, biologic/medical science, or healthcare professional preferred), with 3+ years clinical or pharmaceutical industry experience (advanced degree is preferred)
Experience in one of the following areas is preferred: clinical operations management, clinical study management, drug development, risk management, and/or drug safety operations
At least 3 years hands-on project management experience in leading cross-functional projects within a global company, including hands-on experience applying project management tools and templates.
Effective verbal and written communication skills. Should be able to adapt communication style to suit different audiences.
Effective facilitation skills. Must be able to facilitate group discussions.
Ability to work independently, influence stakeholders, and present sound business strategies.
Ability to demonstrate effectiveness in working in a multidisciplinary, matrix team situation.
Ability to adapt in a quickly changing environment, ability to engage and forge relationships with team members across diverse functions to facilitate information sharing and maintain a continuous flow of information.

Position Description:
For the Principal Research Scientist I position, we are seeking a highly motivated and experienced data scientist to provide scientific and technical leadership for analytical data science, artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML), advanced analytics, and data automation within Analytical R&D. The successful candidate will partner closely with analytical scientists to frame high-value scientific questions, engineer and integrate complex analytical data, and develop fit-for-purpose models, visualizations, and digital solutions that accelerate data-driven decisions across pharmaceutical development.
The candidate will perform and direct data science and application-development activities, mentor and develop scientists, and provide leadership across multiple projects and initiatives. They will conceive, execute, and communicate multidisciplinary strategies; translate between analytical scientists, statisticians, data engineers, software and IT partners; and convert innovative concepts into sustainable, adopted solutions with measurable scientific and business impact.
This role requires a strong combination of data science depth, pharmaceutical or scientific domain awareness, product-oriented solution development, and collaborative leadership. The scientist will help shape the Analytical R&D data science strategy, establish reusable standards and best practices, coordinate initiatives across a global network, and foster productive partnerships with internal data science, statistics, information technology, and R&D organizations.

Provide scientific and technical leadership for analytical data science, AI/ML, advanced analytics, visualization, and data automation initiatives supporting pharmaceutical development.
Consult with analytical scientists and project teams to define the scientific or business question, assess data readiness, select appropriate analytical approaches, and translate results into clear recommendations and decisions.
Lead the end-to-end delivery of data products and analytical solutions, including problem framing, data acquisition and integration, exploratory analysis, feature engineering, model development and validation, visualization, deployment, documentation, user adoption, and lifecycle support.
Develop and apply statistical, machine-learning, chemometric, and/or generative-AI methods to complex analytical data while ensuring approaches are scientifically sound, interpretable, reproducible, and fit for intended use.
Engineer, curate, and analyze structured and unstructured data from laboratory instruments, scientific systems, documents, and development workflows; improve data quality, traceability, accessibility, and reuse.
Design and deliver intuitive applications, dashboards, reports, and automated workflows that reduce manual effort, improve consistency, and enable scientists to obtain timely insights from their data.
Mentor, guide, and develop data scientists and scientific colleagues; provide technical coaching, peer review, and hands-on support, and create learning opportunities that strengthen data literacy and analytical capability across the organization.
Lead or coordinate a portfolio of data science initiatives, establish priorities and delivery plans, manage risks and dependencies, and communicate progress, value, and recommendations to project teams and senior stakeholders.
Establish and promote standards for analytical data assessment, model validation, software development, documentation, version control, testing, data governance, and sustainable solution support.
Build and foster a global network with Analytical R&D, Development Sciences, statistics, enterprise data science, IT, and external partners; connect teams to the appropriate expertise and facilitate effective cross-functional execution.
Identify high-value opportunities, generate new scientific proposals, evaluate emerging AI/ML and digital technologies, and champion responsible innovation that advances scientific understanding, development speed, quality, and operational efficiency.
Communicate complex methods and findings clearly to technical and nontechnical audiences through decision-focused presentations, reports, visualizations, and scientific publications where appropriate.
Ensure solutions and activities comply with applicable safety, quality, regulatory, data-integrity, privacy, security, and AbbVie requirements.
Bachelor’s, Master’s, or Ph.D. in Data Science, Computer Science, Statistics, Applied Mathematics, Engineering, Chemometrics, Computational Science, Analytical Chemistry, Pharmaceutical Sciences, or a closely related discipline, typically with a minimum of 14 years (BS), 12 years (MS), or 6 years (Ph.D.) of relevant industry experience.

Advanced proficiency in Python and/or R and strong working knowledge of relevant data-science libraries, statistical modeling, machine learning, data visualization, and reproducible analytical workflows.
Experience integrating, cleaning, transforming, and analyzing complex and heterogeneous data; working knowledge of SQL, relational data concepts, APIs, and modern data-management practices.
Demonstrated ability to build and deliver production-quality analytical applications, dashboards, automated workflows, or reusable data products. Experience with tools such as Streamlit, Shiny, cloud platforms, workflow automation, or equivalent technologies is desirable.
Strong understanding of model development and evaluation, experimental design, uncertainty, validation, interpretability, and the limitations and appropriate use of AI/ML methods.
Demonstrated leadership through mentoring, technical direction, project or portfolio leadership, influence across functions, and delivery of complex initiatives. Prior direct people-management experience is beneficial but not required.
Proven ability to partner with domain scientists, quickly learn scientific workflows, translate ambiguous needs into tractable analytical problems, and balance technical rigor with practical, fit-for-purpose delivery.
Experience with software-development practices such as Git/version control, modular coding, testing, documentation, code review, deployment, and lifecycle management.
Excellent analytical problem-solving, project-management, written and oral communication, and stakeholder-management skills, including the ability to explain complex concepts to diverse audiences.
Self-motivated, collaborative, and adaptable, with demonstrated scientific curiosity, creativity, sound judgment, and the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced R&D environment.
Knowledge of pharmaceutical development, CMC, analytical laboratory workflows, regulated environments, data integrity, or scientific data standards is strongly preferred.

New to North Carolina. Known for pursuing breakthroughs in medicine.

Now, we’re bringing that commitment to Durham, North Carolina, with a new manufacturing campus that will expand our ability to produce medicines and create opportunities in the Research Triangle.
The campus will integrate advanced manufacturing, laboratory technologies and AI to support the production of immunology, oncology and neuroscience medicines. We are now recruiting our  Program Manager.
ROLE DESCRIPTION
Leads complex, enterprise-wide project governance and commercial strategy initiatives, applying advanced professional expertise to deliver measurable outcomes across global programs, transformation portfolios, and project finance environments. The role manages work through cross-functional teams and partners, without direct people-management responsibility.
Owns end-to-end delivery of strategic programs and workstreams, establishing governance, financial discipline, commercial alignment, and delivery transparency. Integrates plans, dependencies, resources, risks, and stakeholder expectations to enable timely decisions and sustainable business results.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
Global Program & Transformation Delivery
Integrated Planning, Dependencies & Resources
Procurement, Contracts & Commercial Strategy
Risk, Issue & Root-Cause Resolution
Stakeholder Engagement & Executive Reporting
Methods, Documentation & Continuous Improvement
1. Portfolio Governance & Project Finance — Design and operate project finance portfolio governance that supports investment discipline, prioritization, and executive decision-making. Establish consistent financial controls, business-case standards, and performance measures across the portfolio. Translate portfolio insights into clear recommendations on funding, value realization, and corrective actions.
2. Global Program & Transformation Delivery — Lead end-to-end delivery of complex global programs and transformation workstreams from initiation through closeout. Define integrated plans, milestones, deliverables, and acceptance criteria aligned to strategic objectives. Coordinate cross-functional teams to sustain momentum and deliver committed outcomes.
3. Integrated Planning, Dependencies & Resources — Sequence work across interdependent initiatives, identifying critical paths, handoffs, and resource constraints. Align capacity, priorities, and delivery timelines with functional leaders and program sponsors. Anticipate dependency impacts and adjust plans to protect enterprise commitments.
4. Procurement, Contracts & Commercial Strategy — Shape commercial strategies that balance value, risk, cost, supplier capability, and delivery requirements. Partner with procurement, legal, finance, and business stakeholders on sourcing, contracting, and vendor governance. Monitor commercial commitments and escalate material contractual, financial, or delivery exposures.
5. Risk, Issue & Root-Cause Resolution — Identify, assess, and manage program risks, issues, assumptions, and decisions using disciplined governance practices. Lead structured root-cause analysis and coordinate practical recovery plans for complex delivery challenges. Escalate significant matters with clear options, impacts, and recommended actions.
6. Stakeholder Engagement & Executive Reporting — Build productive relationships with senior stakeholders, sponsors, functional leaders, and external partners. Deliver concise reporting on milestones, risks, financial performance, dependencies, and deliverables. Facilitate governance forums that enable timely decisions, accountability, and alignment.
7. Methods, Documentation & Continuous Improvement — Apply and strengthen program and project management methods, tools, controls, and documentation standards. Improve governance processes, reporting quality, and delivery practices through lessons learned and data-driven insights. Promote repeatable ways of working that improve transparency, efficiency, and execution quality.
EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE
Bachelor’s degree in engineering or science required; master’s degree or MBA preferred.
8–10 years of progressive experience in program/project management, portfolio governance, transformation, project finance, commercial strategy, or related disciplines.
Demonstrated success delivering complex, cross-functional programs or workstreams in a matrixed, global, or enterprise environment.
Strong negotiation and communication skills are required.
Strong proficiency in setting up of WBS, SAP finance, legal agreements for equipment and services, digital and AI literacy. Experience in planning software such as Primavera is an advantage.
CORE SKILLS AND CAPABILITIES
Advanced program and project management expertise, including planning, governance, dependency management, and delivery controls.
Strong financial, commercial, procurement, and contract-management acumen.
Ability to analyze complex information, resolve issues at root cause, and translate findings into clear actions.
Excellent executive communication, stakeholder engagement, facilitation, and influencing skills.
Proficiency with project and portfolio management methods, reporting tools, and governance documentation.

Aseptic Suite Delivery and Accountability: Lead delivery of aseptic manufacturing suites across multiple modalities, partnering with Project Delivery and global engineering SMEs. Own delivery against approved scope, schedule, budget, and design and construction quality expectations.
Equipment Package and Team Leadership: Lead, coach, and guide package leads responsible for filling machines, isolators, lyophilizers, stopper processors, AVI, autoclaves, and washers. Establish clear accountabilities, align priorities, and resolve issues across equipment packages.
Manufacturing Representation and Decision-Making: Represent Manufacturing throughout the project lifecycle, providing operational requirements and timely decisions. Ensure design choices and equipment acceptance support safe, high-quality, and practical manufacturing operations.

Aseptic Practices, Contamination Control, and Quality Culture: Establish operational ownership of aseptic practices and contamination-control expectations. Partner with Quality, Engineering, Validation, and Microbiology/Environmental Monitoring to align the manufacturing operating model with the contamination control strategy
Operational Readiness and Manufacturing Organization: Own Manufacturing Operational Readiness from design through commissioning, qualification, start-up, and routine operations. Develop production strategies for the intended product mix and multi-product operating model. Partner with Supply Chain, Maintenance, Engineering, Quality, and Technical Operations to resolve constraints and improve line performance while balancing GMP compliance, supply reliability, capacity, cost, and operational flexibility.
Education
Bachelor’s degree in engineering, pharmaceutical sciences, manufacturing, or a related technical discipline, or an equivalent combination of relevant education and experience.
Experience
At least 15 years of aseptic operations experience in a cGMP biopharmaceutical industry with extensive floor leadership.
Solid track record of leading high-performance manufacturing teams with an exceptional safety and quality performance.
Experience in roles that supported capital project delivery, C&Q, start-up and forming operational teams is preferred.
Extensive, progressively responsible experience in aseptic manufacturing, engineering, including leadership of complex manufacturing equipment or facility programs.
Hands-on leadership experience across equipment design reviews, vendor and site acceptance testing, commissioning, qualification, and manufacturing start-up.
Experience building and developing teams, establishing manufacturing procedures and training, and preparing an organization for operational readiness.
Experience implementing advanced manufacturing technologies and translating project delivery knowledge into sustainable operational capability.
Skills
Strategic and execution leadership: Ability to connect project delivery decisions with long-term manufacturing needs while maintaining accountability for results.
Aseptic manufacturing expertise: Strong understanding of aseptic process equipment, suite integration, and operational safety and quality requirements.
Cross-functional influence: Ability to align Manufacturing, Engineering, Project Delivery, Construction, commissioning teams, and equipment vendors around timely decisions.
Technical judgment and problem-solving: Ability to evaluate complex equipment and facility issues, assess delivery and operational impacts, and drive resolution.
People leadership: Strong coaching, recruitment, resource planning, and capability-development skills.
Digital and technology fluency: Ability to guide implementation of automation, robotics, data analysis, and digital twins in manufacturing.
Communication and transition leadership: Ability to communicate priorities and decisions clearly and lead teams from project execution through start-up into routine operations.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
This job provides operational and process leadership for the Facilities Engineering area by leading short to medium-term planning and execution, and is accountable for meaningful career development conversations and regular coaching and feedback.
Lead infrastructure strategy across multiple sites and guides planning and design priorities for facilities and utility systems.
Oversees cross-site practices for utilities management and building systems performance, reinforcing consistent operational standards and service expectations.
Directs renovation and infrastructure programs through site leadership, aligning scope, sequencing, and constraints to portfolio priorities.
Drives consistent execution of safety and regulatory requirements for facilities work, ensuring risks, findings, and corrective actions are addressed to closure.
Develops site leaders and engineers by reinforcing disciplined planning routines, stakeholder alignment cadence, and traceable decision and action documentation.
Responsible for leading and optimizing operational aspects across teams, as well as implementing workforce and succession plans to meet business needs.
ADDITIONAL RESPONSIBILITIES
Deliver the Durham campus infrastructure portfolio
1. Lead infrastructure projects—including campus development, utilities, the Spine, warehouse, laboratory, administrative, office, and support buildings—from planning through design, construction, commissioning, and handover. Balance campus priorities and coordinate interfaces and dependencies across infrastructure projects and adjacent scopes. Ensure design inputs, project interfaces, and vendor-provided information are effectively integrated, and that the overall program meets approved objectives for scope, schedule, cost, delivery, and quality.
2. Own integrated project planning and performance
Establish and maintain integrated plans, budgets, schedules, milestones, and performance measures across the infrastructure portfolio. Identify risks, constraints, and decision points early; develop and implement mitigation plans; and provide stakeholders and leadership with clear, timely updates on progress, changes, and emerging issues.
3. Contribute to design development led by Global Engineering
Represent the infrastructure scope as an active partner in the design effort led by Global Engineering. Bring campus requirements, operational needs, constructability, maintainability, and local conditions into design decisions. Coordinate design reviews and stakeholder input, integrate interfaces across project scopes, and help resolve design issues while maintaining alignment with project objectives.
4. Lead procurement and contractor selection
Develop and execute procurement plans for project services, materials, and construction. Establish selection criteria, coordinate bid and proposal evaluations, and assess vendor capabilities and delivery risks. Recommend vendors and contractors whose technical, commercial, schedule, quality, and campus-specific strengths best meet project requirements.
5. Develop and implement the contracting strategy
Develop and apply contracting approaches that support effective project delivery across the Durham campus. In collaboration with relevant stakeholders, determine appropriate contract packaging, delivery models, commercial terms, and risk allocation. Oversee contract formation and administration, promoting clear scope definition and effective change control, performance monitoring, and issue resolution.
6. Manage scope and construction execution in partnership with the Construction Director
Partner with the Construction Director to define, validate, and control project scope from design through construction. Coordinate interfaces among designers, contractors, vendors, campus stakeholders, and other projects. Assess proposed changes for their impact on cost, schedule, quality, and delivery, and support timely decisions that protect project outcomes. Work with the Commissioning and Start-up team and Operations personnel to prepare the infrastructure scope for safe start-up, commissioning, and qualification.
Education and Experience
Bachelor’s degree in engineering or a related field required with at least 15 years of relevant experience; advanced degree or relevant professional credentials preferred.
Extensive experience leading complex, multidisciplinary capital projects or programs from planning and design through construction, commissioning, and handover.
Strong technical expertise in cGMP manufacturing, utilities and design principles. Experience in implementation of Factory of the future concepts preferred.
Experience in managing scope, schedule, cost, quality, risk, procurement, and contractor performance.
Proven ability to lead and develop managers responsible for multiple project packages and to work effectively in matrixed organizations with engineering, construction, commissioning, operations, procurement, and other cross functional teams.
Core Skills and Capabilities
Program and project leadership:  Sets direction across a portfolio, establishes clear priorities, and maintains alignment between package-level execution and overall program objectives.
Commercial and contracting acumen:  Develops procurement and contracting strategies; evaluates delivery models, contract packages, commercial terms, and risk allocation; and oversees contractor performance and change management.
Financial and schedule management:  Uses budgets, forecasts, integrated schedules, milestones, and performance measures to monitor delivery and address variances.
Risk and decision management:  Identifies risks, constraints, and interfaces early; develops practical mitigation plans; and escalates issues with clear recommendations.
Design and technical integration:  Partners with Global Engineering and other technical teams to integrate campus and operational requirements, constructability, maintainability, vendor inputs, and project interfaces.
Construction and commissioning readiness:  Understands construction execution and works across construction, commissioning, start-up, qualification, and operations teams to support safe, effective transition to service.
Leadership and talent development:  Provides direction, coaching, and mentorship to package managers; builds accountability and collaboration; and develops team capability.
Communication and stakeholder influence:  Communicates complex issues clearly, facilitates timely decisions, and builds productive relationships with senior leaders, technical teams, contractors, vendors, and campus stakeholders.

The successful candidate will develop and implement computational approaches to understand disease biology and drug responses using high-throughput molecular profiling data. This role will involve integrating single-cell RNA-seq, scATAC-seq, TCR/BCR repertoire, bulk RNA-seq, and Olink proteomics data to characterize disease-associated cell states, investigate gene regulatory networks, and identify therapeutic opportunities.

Analyze scRNA-seq, and CITE-seq, datasets, including quality control, integration, clustering, and cell-type and cell-state annotation.
Integrate patient cohorts with reference atlases and perform differential expression, abundance, and pathway analyses, accounting for donor variation and study design.
Analyze scATAC-seq data to identify differential accessibility, transcription factor motifs, and candidate regulatory programs; integrate accessibility with gene expression to infer peak-to-gene relationships.
Analyze TCR/BCR repertoires, including clonotype assignment, clonal expansion, diversity, V(D)J usage, and sharing across tissues or time points; link clonotypes to matched single-cell profiles.
Analyze bulk RNA-seq and Olink proteomics data and integrate multiomics findings to support target prioritization and biomarker hypotheses; maintain documented, version-controlled workflows and evaluate methods using cloud or high-performance computing.
Collaborate with internal and external scientists to prioritize hypotheses for validation, communicate findings and limitations, and contribute to presentations and publications.

Proficiency in Python and/or R and experience working in Linux-based computing environments.
Experience with commonly used bioinformatics tools and frameworks such as Scanpy, AnnData, Cell Ranger, scvi-tools, DESeq2, GSEA, WGCNA, or related methods.
Working knowledge of statistical analysis, multiple-testing correction, batch effects, and biological replication in high-dimensional datasets.
Ability to translate biological questions into analyses, interpret and communicate results critically, collaborate effectively, and manage multiple priorities with attention to detail.
Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively, manage multiple priorities, and deliver high-quality analyses with attention to detail.

Experience analyzing Olink or other high-plex proteomics datasets.
Experience with CITE-seq, ATAC-seq, spatial transcriptomics, or integrative multi-omics analysis.
Experience building or benchmarking machine-learning models, including convolutional neural networks, autoencoders, generative models, transfer learning, or foundation models.

Coordinate the utility interface, site substation, medium-voltage distribution, building substations and low-voltage distribution.
Ensure the design incorporates appropriate capacity and flexibility for future campus expansion.

Establish appropriate redundancy and backup-power requirements based on operational and GMP impact.

About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at  www.abbvie.com . Follow @abbvie on  LinkedIn,   Facebook ,  Instagram ,  X  and  YouTube.
Purpose
Oversees the direction, planning, execution, and interpretation of clinical trials or research activities of one or more clinical development programs. Participates in cross-functional teams to generate, deliver, and interpret high-quality clinical data supporting overall product scientific and business strategy.
Responsibilities
Manages the design and implementation of one or more clinical development programs in support of an overall Product Development Plan, based on strong medical and scientific principles, knowledge of compliance and regulatory requirements, AbbVie’s customers, markets, business operations, and emerging issues. Oversees project-related education of investigators, study site personnel, and AbbVie study staff.
Has overall responsibility for oversight of clinical studies, monitoring overall study integrity, and review, interpretation, and communication of accumulating data pertaining to safety and efficacy of the molecule. Along with Clinical Operations, is responsible for oversight of study enrollment and overall timelines for key deliverables. Responsible for assessment and reporting of serious adverse events per corporate policy and regulations for those protocols on which assigned.
Responsible for design, analysis, interpretation, and reporting of scientific content of protocols, Investigator Brochures, Clinical Study Reports, regulatory submissions and responses, and other program documents.
May oversee the work of Medical Directors and/or Scientific Directors, and of Clinical Scientists working on the same or related programs.
Provides in-house clinical expertise for the molecule and disease, coordinating appropriate scientific and medical activities with internal stakeholders as they relate to ongoing clinical projects. May participate in due diligence or other business development activity. As required by program needs, contributes in partnership with Discovery colleagues to design and implementation of translational strategies.
May serve on or chair an Integrated Evidence Strategy Team (IEST), with responsibility for development of a rigorous, cross-functionally-aligned, vetted Clinical Development Plan with full consideration of contingencies and alternative approaches. In the role of IEST Chair, responsibilities may include supervision of matrix team members and serving as Clinical Research representative to lend clinical development and medical expertise to an Asset Strategy  Team (AST)
Acts as a clinical interface and actively solicits opinion leader interactions related to the molecule and disease area; partners with Medical Affairs, Commercial and other functions in these activities as required, consistent with corporate policies, to ensure that broad cross-functional perspectives are incorporated into Clinical Development Plans and protocols as appropriate.
Stays abreast of professional information and technology through conferences, medical literature, and other available training, to augment expertise in the therapeutic area.
Responsible for understanding the regulatory requirements related to the clinical studies and global drug development and accountable for complying with those requirements. Serves as a clinical representative for key regulatory discussions.
Ensures adherence to Good Clinical Practices, pharmacovigilance standards, standard operating procedures and to all other quality standards in conducting research.
Medical Doctor (M.D.), Doctor of Osteopathy (D.O.) or non-US equivalent of M.D. degree with relevant therapeutic specialty in an academic or hospital environment. Completion of a residency program strongly preferred. Completion of a subspecialty fellowship is desirable.
At least 2 years of clinical trial experience in the pharmaceutical industry, academia, or equivalent.
Experience with psychedelic drug development highly preferred
Ability to run a clinical research program of moderate complexity with minimal supervision.
Ability to perform and bring out the best in others on a cross-functional global team.
Ability to interact externally and internally to support a global scientific and business strategy.
Knowledge of clinical trial methodology, regulatory and compliance requirements governing clinical trials and experience in development of clinical strategy and the design of study protocols.
Must possess excellent oral and written English communication skills.

title: Senior Scientist II, Recombinant Peptide Process Development
description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at  www.abbvie.com . Follow @abbvie on  LinkedIn,   Facebook ,  Instagram ,  X  and  YouTube.
AbbVie’s Biologics CMC organization develops processes to support the advancement and manufacture of biologic medicines. AbbVie is seeking a highly motivated scientist to lead development of microbial-based recombinant peptide production processes. This position will serve as a technical lead across expression-system and strain development, fermentation, recovery, purification, and scale-up.
Recombinant production of short peptides can be challenging due to intracellular degradation, low expression, aggregation, and limited solubility. The successful candidate will develop and optimize practical strategies to address these challenges and advance robust, scalable processes for therapeutic peptide production. When aligned with program needs, the candidate will also evaluate and apply genetic code expansion (GCE) strategies to enable the site-specific incorporation of non-canonical amino acids. The role will collaborate with cross-functional partners and contribute to process development, technology evaluation, and technology transfer activities.
Responsibilities:
Lead recombinant peptide process-development activities, including expression strategy, host and clone screening, process optimization, and scale-up.
Design and evaluate expression constructs and microbial hosts, including  Escherichia coli  and yeast, for peptide production.
Develop and assess fusion-tag and carrier-protein strategies—including His-tag, GST, SUMO, and inclusion-body expression—to improve peptide stability, expression, host tolerance, and recovery.
Design and conduct clone-screening studies using microscale cultivation, parallel bioreactors, and other appropriate scale-down or high-throughput approaches.
Develop and optimize peptide recovery processes, including cell harvest and lysis, inclusion-body isolation and processing, and chemical or enzymatic cleavage of fusion partners.
Troubleshoot peptide-specific process challenges, such as aggregation, low solubility, degradation, incomplete cleavage, and co-eluting impurities; recommend and pursue appropriate solutions.
Interpret analytical results, including HPLC, UPLC, and LC-MS data, to assess peptide identity, mass accuracy, purity, and process-related impurities; partner with analytical teams to address characterization needs.
Evaluate emerging technologies and process approaches for recombinant peptide production, including genetic code expansion when relevant to program needs.
Apply AI/ML approaches, where appropriate, to analyze peptide sequence, structure, and experimental data in support of design, optimization, and candidate prioritization.
Communicate scientific plans, progress, challenges, conclusions, and recommendations clearly to project teams and other stakeholders.
Mentor junior scientists and provide technical direction in recombinant peptide bioprocessing.
Contribute to scientific publications and presentations at conferences, as appropriate.
Maintain a high level of productivity while managing priorities and timelines; follow applicable corporate standards for safety, quality, and compliance.
PhD with typically 4+ years of relevant experience, master’s degree or equivalent education with 10+  years of relevant experience or Bachelor’s degree or equivalent education with typically 12+ years of relevant experience is required.
Thorough theoretical and practical understanding of relevant scientific disciplines, with hands-on experience in microbial physiology and recombinant expression systems, particularly  E. coli  and/or yeast.
Demonstrated ability to independently design, execute, and interpret critical experiments to address scientific or development questions.
Experience developing or optimizing expression processes for peptides, small proteins, or other products susceptible to degradation, or instability.
Experience with strain or clone screening, fermentation, and process optimization; familiarity with bioreactors and scale-down or parallel cultivation approaches.
Demonstrated experience with preparative chromatography and peptide or protein purification, as well as peptide recovery and fusion-partner cleavage strategies.
Strong experimental design, data interpretation, troubleshooting, scientific writing, and oral communication skills.
Ability to manage multiple priorities and timelines and work effectively in a matrixed, cross-functional environment.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience developing or manufacturing complex therapeutic peptides, particularly GLP-1 or related incretin peptides, in a pharmaceutical or biotechnology company or start-up environment.
Experience applying genetic code expansion to incorporate non-canonical amino acids at defined positions using engineered orthogonal aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase/tRNA pairs and codon reassignment.

The Analytics and Performance Excellence (APEX) function supports AbbVie’s US organization and is comprised of highly respected researchers, analysts, data scientists and strategists who are committed to being best-in-class within the biopharmaceutical industry.  We serve as a strategic in-house counsel, ensuring that all decisions leverage the key insights that we develop.  We continue to build new capabilities and skill sets, encouraging our team members to pull up a chair, be themselves, be creative, speak their minds, and do good work.  We are a passionate, diverse, flexible, and inclusive organization with a culture that supports the best ideas, wherever they originate.  We are smart, fun, and innovative – and we’d love for you to join us.
General Position Summary/Purpose:
The Market Access and Patient Services Insights (MAPS) organization within APEX plays an instrumental role in shaping market access strategies for all of AbbVie’s US brands. As a member of this team, you will lead the planning and execution of primary/ secondary market research to identify payer opportunities and threats, influence the development of market access strategies and tactics, enable organizational learning, and ensure alignment of insights with the broader commercial goals of each brand.  This is a hybrid role with the focus on Primary Market Research with an opportunity for some data analytics.
The role requires strong research experience as well as subject matter expertise within the overall U.S. market access environment. The role provides insights that directly impact patient and physician access to AbbVie brands through its influence on the development of pricing, contracting, messaging and other access strategies.
Key Accountabilities/Core Job Responsibilities:
Lead primary and secondary market research activities on a key oncology brand and/or launch indications that influence market access through fact-based analysis, customer insights and business knowledge. Co-develop with U.S. Market Access commercial leaders, innovative Pricing and Contracting strategies to achieve optimal payer formulary access that maximize net sales for assigned brands. Deliver customer insights through market research, competitive simulation, and customer/environmental modeling to understand complex economic and clinical dynamics that drive payer access and shape brand demand. Demonstrate strong understanding of the U.S. healthcare landscape and key AbbVie therapeutic areas to identify and proactively address opportunities and threats. Build collaborative relationships with internal U.S. Market Access Sales and Marketing stakeholders. Align insights to Brand insight partners, that when integrated with HCP and Consumer insights, positively impacts brand decision making.
Key areas of functional scope include:
Leading the creative process for developing GPO, IDN, Specialty Pharmacy, Health Plan and PBM go-to-market strategies for launch brands across payer channels and conveying analytical narratives that describe the market environment influencing stakeholder negotiations.
Leading the delivery of brand specific market access insights and response to specific market access issues/ trends. Areas of depth include gross/net pricing, contracting strategy, value proposition development, implications of competitive launches on access, investigative analytics related to market events and competitive actions, strategies for payer formulary coverage and reimbursement, and identifying value drivers that guide clinical data development and value positioning.
Demonstrating a strong understanding of both primary/ secondary research methodologies and the ability to synthesize insights into compelling narratives. Responsible for leading the communication of market access insights to leadership requiring a broad range of market access expertise as these brands commonly experience differing market access challenges.

11 years of professional experience
7 years of related industry experience in market research
Strong story telling skills; ability to distill complex information synthesized into concise and impactful messages and communications.

Oncology Experience
Strong working knowledge of syndicated pharmaceutical data sources.

description:
About Allergan Aesthetics
At Allergan Aesthetics, an AbbVie company, we develop, manufacture, and market a portfolio of leading aesthetics brands and products. Our aesthetics portfolio includes facial injectables, body contouring, plastics, skin care, and more. Our goal is to consistently provide our customers with innovation, education, exceptional service, and a commitment to excellence, all with a personal touch. This is a hybrid role including in office and remote working days. Must be a resident or relocatable to Austin TX area.
Must be able to work one of the below shifts:
8:00am-4:30pm CT, or 8:30-5:00pmCT, 7:30-4:30pmCT or 8:00-5pmCT
The Sr Inside Sales Business Development Manager is a revenue generating position with responsibility for quarterly sales quota attainment for the Facial Aesthetics portfolio of products (BOTOX® Cosmetic, JUVÉDERM® Collection of Fillers, SkinMedica®, KYBELLA®) and for managing and enhancing portfolio growth through business development activities using primarily phone communication.
The Sr IBDM represents the Allergan Aesthetics product portfolio to targeted aesthetic customers within a designated geographical area. Responsible for product and program education, product adoption, and portfolio growth through business development activities.
The Sr IBDM provides technical product and procedure training, as well as competitive product differentiation.  Assigned sales goals are obtained through strategic analysis of account data, strong knowledge of accounts aesthetic goals, understanding of market dynamics, application of consultative selling and implementation of the U.S. Sales/Marketing plan.  The company offers flexible career paths with a strong emphasis on opportunity for internal mobility.
Allergan Sr IBDMs must:
Leverage Allergan Medical resources to enhance adoption of the Allergan Medical Aesthetics Portfolio.  Synergistically work and coordinate activities with other Allergan sales personnel and support teams (include, but are not limited to, Facial Aesthetics, CoolSculpting®, SkinMedica®, and Marketing).  Complies with required reports, requests, and compliance policies.

Consistently achieves sales quota across portfolio. Proficient in sales execution component of marketing plans. Independently creates call and business development plans across the product portfolio. Demonstrates adaptability and creativity with multiple initiatives.

Identifying growth opportunities to include: expanding reach with customer base, expanding product portfolio utilization with existing accounts, and launching new products and new product indications.
Educating and supporting the customer with marketing strategies including but not limited to website and social media development, internal office branding, patient segmentation, and external marketing strategies.
Pre-planning sales calls and maintaining efficient time management skills to ensure maximum customer contact and highest level of customer engagement.
Maintaining updated knowledge of the industry and competitive products.
Maintaining compliance with all applicable quality and regulatory guidelines as an integral part of business operations.
Collaboration with Regional Manager, respective field reps and Inside Sales Area Manager - Work cross- functionally with field sales in order to drive sales objectives, cultivate relationships, and collaborate on growth opportunities.
Leave of absence and vacant territory coverage includes collaboration with the respective Sales Representative, Region Manager, and Inside Sales Area Manager to develop and negotiate a coverage plan.   This can include consistent communication- managing own sample allocation, placing orders, providing marketing materials, and assisting accounts with marketing and business development strategies.   Also includes execution on all campaigns/promotions, new product launches and other sales related initiatives.

Adobe's Marketing Finance organization is reinventing how it operates from the ground up, with workflow automation and AI at the center. This role makes that happen. You'll embed with our marketing finance teams, learn their craft, and design, build and maintain the tools, pipelines, and AI-powered workflows that change how they work, while shaping Adobe's IT systems to meet marketing finance needs. You'll measure yourself by one question: did I make someone’s job easier?

description:
About the Role
The Global Microsoft GTM Lead owns the strategic partnership between Adobe and Microsoft. You will set and execute the joint go-to-market strategy, expand customer relationships and Azure Marketplace adoption, and align executives, field teams, product, and marketing across both companies. As the primary liaison between Adobe and Microsoft, you are accountable for revenue growth, cloud adoption, seller enablement, and delivery of the joint business plan.
This is a build role. The partner ecosystem is early, programs are still being designed, and you will work across three organizations (including SIs) whose incentives on any given deal don’t always align. You will help shape how frontier AI technology reaches the enterprise through the services ecosystem.
Key Responsibilities
Strategy and Execution
Own the end-to-end GTM strategy and operation of the alliance, prioritizing high-value enterprise opportunities and driving revenue through Microsoft field engagement and joint co-sell motions.
Decide where to concentrate investment across the partner portfolio, and make the case to stop investing where returns are not there.
Provide market intelligence and competitive insight on the partner ecosystem to inform product and commercial strategy.
Partner with Adobe’s alliances, sales, partner marketing, and regional cloud teams to keep the motion consistent globally while regions execute locally.
Governance and Operating Cadence
Lead the alliance operating rhythm: annual business planning, executive business reviews (EBRs), and quarterly and monthly business reviews (QBRs, MBRs).
Develop and manage annual business plans, growth initiatives, and partnership objectives with Adobe and Microsoft leaders.
Build scalable processes for partnership operations, including escalation management, business reviews, and reporting.
Maintain executive engagement plans, stakeholder maps, governance frameworks, and action tracking.
Prepare executive-ready materials, including strategic updates, account reviews, business cases, win stories, and operating plans.
Performance and Measurement
Own executive dashboards, scorecards, pipeline reviews, forecasting, and performance reporting for both leadership teams.
Define, track, and report alliance KPIs: revenue influence, Azure consumption, Marketplace performance, co-sell activity, customer adoption, migration outcomes, and executive engagement.
Monitor partnership health, flag risks and opportunities, and recommend actions to accelerate growth. Draw on data from sales, finance, marketing, product, engineering, and customer success.
Drive operational excellence through process improvement, reporting automation, and business insights.
Field Activation and Marketplace Growth
Expand Azure Marketplace adoption and manage incentive programs, sponsorships, funding, and co-sell benefits.
Activate Microsoft field teams around Adobe priorities and strategic accounts to accelerate adoption of Co-Worker/Copilot, AMA Launch, CSC on Azure, Adobe Brand Visibility, and relevant third-party partner solutions.
Deliver enablement programs, workshops, and GTM guidance so Adobe solutions are positioned effectively in Microsoft customer conversations, driving consumption through Adobe workloads and modern workplace initiatives.
Support regional sales leadership meetings, pipeline management, reporting, and field enablement alongside the Adobe Microsoft Alliance team.
Marketing and Thought Leadership
Work with Adobe and Microsoft sales and marketing teams to develop assets, events, and customer programs.
Support customer references, success stories, analyst engagements, and executive communications.
Present at industry events, customer workshops, and alliance forums, positioning Adobe as a strategic cloud, AI, and digital workspace partner in the Microsoft ecosystem.
Cross-Functional and Product Alignment
Align executives, product teams, the Adobe-Microsoft partner team, sales leadership, and marketing around year-over-year revenue growth.
Coordinate stakeholders across sales, marketing, product, engineering, finance, and operations to drive accountability on strategic initiatives.
Work with product management and engineering to align Adobe and Microsoft roadmaps and secure opportunities and funding for integration, innovation, and joint solutions.
Represent customer and Microsoft requirements in product planning, using adoption metrics and usage telemetry to measure impact and business value.
Qualifications
Education: MBA or equivalent practical experience.
Experience: 10-15+ years in global technology partner management, GTM, and partner sales leadership, working directly with enterprise customers, cloud service providers, C-level executives, and sales leaders.
Industry knowledge: Enterprise software sales and operations, competitive landscapes, and cloud marketplace business models.
Alliance expertise: Deep knowledge of alliance management, co-sell metrics and motions, and partner programs, ideally within the Microsoft ecosystem.
Hyperscaler partnerships: Experience developing GTM strategy and co-sell programs with the largest hyperscalers.
Strategic agreements: Experience planning and executing multi-year partner sales and product agreements.
Influence and collaboration: Proven ability to lead cross-functional initiatives and drive execution across matrix organizations, including sales, product, and marketing.
Communication: Exceptional communication skills and executive presence, with the ability to influence senior internal and external stakeholders.
Adaptability: Comfortable in fast-paced, ambiguous environments across time zones, with a focus on measurable outcomes.
