description:
The Opportunity
Typography is central to how ideas are communicated. If you're passionate about beautifully created design, have deep curiosity about what AI can do, and take personal responsibility for creating products that people love; then this may be the role for you. Adobe Fonts supports millions of creatives in choosing and using typefaces across fonts.adobe.com, Express, Photoshop, Illustrator, Acrobat, and more Creative Cloud platforms. Our Internal Services team provides the platform engineering and deployment backbone for all of these. We manage CI/CD, deployment approaches, the services and data layers our engineers depend on, our observability and security stance, and increasingly the agentic tools that transform how our entire organization delivers software.
We're seeking a Senior Software Development Engineer to lead this exciting journey in our San Francisco location.
What you'll do
Own and evolve our deployment platform. Lead strategy for CI/CD, PR environments, and release safety across a mixed fleet that includes containerized services, serverless services, and static front ends.
Build the foundation for AI-accelerated development. Help build our agent factory and grow our internal agentic toolkit and skill library.
Ship inference applications at scale. Take greenfield services from spec to production and standardize our ML/inference footprint.
Modernize our services for the AI era. Identify where an existing service is held back by its current build and lead the fix.
Rethink our security posture for agentic threats. Lead how we secure autonomous agents and their tool use.
Expose Adobe Fonts to the agentic ecosystem. Extend our Model Context Protocol (MCP) surface and conversational, intent-based font discovery.
Work higher up the stack, too. Contribute directly to search, browse, discovery, and the customer-facing experiences our platform powers.
Hold ownership over what you deliver to production, encompassing on-call support, incident management, and the reliability of the services and pipelines that the entire organization depends upon.
Set technical direction and multiply the team. Write the development docs, run the technical reviews, and mentor engineers.
What we're looking for
Software engineering
Deep full-stack fundamentals and craft — build, testing, code quality, code review — plus system development and production maturity: latency, scale, reliability, observability, and on-call ownership.
Ships and owns services end to end, and reasons fluently across the whole stack: front end (JavaScript/TypeScript, React or Web Components), application services (Ruby/Rails, Python, Go, and comfort picking up others), and the SRE/config/hardware layer beneath (Terraform, Chef, Kubernetes/Helm, AWS).
Platform & deployment depth
Strong CI/CD ownership (Jenkins or equivalent), containerization and orchestration, infrastructure-as-code, and AWS (EC2/ASG, IAM, Lambda, API Gateway, CloudFront). Experience making deployment fast, safe, and self-service — ephemeral/preview environments, progressive delivery, rollback strategy.
Solid grasp of the data and messaging layers behind real services, including relational, caching, search, and event-driven/pub-sub. You know how to run migrations and upgrades without downtime.
AI/agentic proficiency
Hands-on understanding of building AI-enabled systems: agent runtimes, tool calling, MCP, LLM/inference serving, and the infrastructure around them — evaluation, feedback loops, observability, and sandboxed execution.
A security outlook for this new surface — you think about how agentic systems fail and get abused, and proactively build guardrails accordingly.
Leadership & scope
Track record of delivering high-impact platform work used across multiple teams, leading complex cross-team technical efforts, and balancing near-term delivery with long-term maintainability, security, and operability.
Excellent written and verbal communication.
Typically 12+ years of software engineering experience, with demonstrated senior-level impact.
Nice to have
Ruby on Rails at scale, and experience decomposing or modernizing a large monolith.
GPU/model-serving infrastructure and low-latency inference (e.g. SageMaker, Kubernetes GPU platforms); search-engine internals (OpenSearch/Elasticsearch, vector/hybrid search).
Experience building developer platforms, internal tooling, or agent harnesses adopted by other teams.
Event-driven architectures and secrets-management platforms (Vault, CyberArk).
Front-end depth with modern component systems (Web Components/Lit, React/TypeScript, build systems).

description:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.
The Community You Will Join:
We are looking for a Senior Manager to lead BizTech Enablement and Innovation (BEI), BizTech's solutions partner to the rest of the company. BEI works with Finance, Legal, People, Marketing, Global Operations, Policy and Communications, Design, and other non-technical functions to understand how they work, turn their problems into working solutions, and make sure employees know about and adopt the technology BizTech provides. The team also brings what it learns back to BizTech product teams and vendors to shape their roadmaps. You will report to the Director, Tech Foundations.
The Difference You Will Make:
This is a strategic leadership role within a large business unit. For the next 18 months, the team's focus is AI. You will own the company's approach to AI adoption and impact outside of Engineering, set the vision for AI-enabled work, hold functions accountable to measurable outcomes, and serve as BizTech's primary partner to E-Team leaders on AI transformation.
More broadly, you will lead how Airbnb's non-technical functions discover, adopt, and get value from business technology. That covers quick consultations and fast-track solutions, go-to-market for new BizTech services, and building or buying new solutions where existing tools fall short. In the near term, you will define where Airbnb should be on AI-enabled work in two years, build the team and partnerships to get there, and make the trade-offs required to deliver it.
Success in this role is measured in business outcomes, not tool rollouts: functions that have redesigned their work around technology and AI, defined their own impact metrics, and can show the efficiency and quality gains, supported by a simpler tool landscape with fewer duplicate and unsupported tools.
A Typical Day:
Help define and own the multi-year strategy for AI adoption and impact across Airbnb's non-technical functions, aligned with company and Tech priorities.
Assess current gaps, existing capabilities, and emerging AI trends to anticipate how functions will need to work 18 to 24 months out, and translate that into a roadmap and investment.
Simplify the tools business teams use by steering them to supported solutions and closing the gaps that lead them to find their own.
Set organizational OKRs and success criteria for near and long-term initiatives, and hold teams and partners accountable for delivery.
Make and communicate hard trade-offs across competing functional demands, platform constraints, and budget.
Serve as the senior BizTech partner to leadership teams on AI transformation, including regular readouts to executives and senior Tech leadership.
Establish the framework by which each function defines, measures, and reports the business impact of AI, and drive adoption of that framework as a standard.
Build a metric-driven accountability culture: clear baselines, targets, and ownership for every function, with a single trusted source of truth for adoption and impact data.
Tailor narratives for different audiences, from detailed methodology with data and engineering partners to concise decision framing for executives.
Seek feedback from partner teams and use it to improve delivery; raise risks to leadership early.
Listen actively and anticipate where change will meet resistance.
Design and continuously refine the operating model that connects different technical functions and networks into one coordinated enablement system.
Shape the enablement approach for AI usage so functions can build and share AI solutions at scale.
Partner with platform and product teams to influence the AI tooling roadmap based on the needs of non-technical users.
Direct external partner and consulting engagements, including scope, governance, and return on investment.
Set quality, reliability, and security standards for the AI solutions the team and functions build; own operational issues in production and drive the fixes that prevent repeats.
Make sure tech debt and the long-term upkeep of shipped solutions are prioritized across the team's roadmap.
Lead a multi-disciplinary, globally distributed organization including managers, Business Solutions Engineers, Systems Architects, and Program Managers.
Create a team environment that values constructive debate, risk-taking, and learning from experiments, and that fosters belonging across regions.
Build an 18+ month talent plan and a succession pipeline, including hiring at L10 and above.
Coach, mentor, and grow the team to communicate clearly, resolve conflict early, and build inclusive teams.
Pilot new technologies, including AI, with business teams, and hand proven solutions to product owners for long-term support.
Coach leaders across functions to connect AI capabilities to business value.
Establish mechanisms that turn learnings from individual functions into reusable patterns across the company.
Represent BizTech in company-wide AI forums and contribute to hiring committees, talent processes, and Airbnb's internal AI community.
Role model Airbnb's core values and strengthen the company's mission through the way AI is introduced to employees.
Your Expertise:
12+ years of industry experience in business technology, enterprise systems, digital transformation, or technical program leadership, including 5+ years leading managers and multi-disciplinary teams.
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Business, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
Demonstrated track record setting and delivering multi-year strategy for a company-wide technology or transformation program with executive visibility.
Experience leading business technology consulting, solutions engineering, or IT business partnering for non-technical teams, including influencing product and vendor roadmaps.

title: Learning & Development Program Manager, AWS Controls Engineering
description:
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global Data Centers infrastructure. We support all AWS data centers power, and cooling equipment related monitoring and automatic controls system that ensure our customers have continual access to the AWS cloud services.
You’ll join a diverse team of industrial controls, and systems engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. As part of the AMER controls team, you will work with highly motivated experts and innovators in the data center industry. You will be responsible for defining the onboarding, training, and career development of Engineers, Technicians, and Program Managers on the AMER Controls Deployment, Service and Fleet (CDS) fleet. You combine instructional design expertise with a working understanding of industrial controls systems (BMS/EPMS), data center operations, or mission-critical engineering environments. You will be responsible for architecting a single standardized training program from the ground up, redesign the existing onboarding experience and accelerate new hire effectiveness.
This role demands excellent verbal and written communication skills, strong program management discipline, and the ability to partner across engineering, operations, and leadership stakeholders throughout AMER.
Key job responsibilities
As a CDS L&D manager, you will
Design, build, and continuously improve a standardized Controls training program covering the full onboarding lifecycle for Controls Engineers and Controls Technicians, including a structured 90-day experience with weekly shadowing plans, monthly partner team rotations, and qualification milestones.
Develop and deliver technical curricula aligned to the daily work of Controls roles — BMS and EPMS system architecture, sequence of operations, controls logic programming, industrial protocols (BACnet, MODBUS, MQTT), commissioning, root cause analysis, and alarm management.
Build role-specific training tracks: Technician content covering field device installation, calibration, provisioning, electrical schematics, and red-line documentation; Engineer content covering project scoping, budgeting, vendor management, and service contract financial oversight.
Create and maintain skill assessments that measure readiness by role and level; track qualification pass rates, manager-assessed proficiency ratings, and onboarding satisfaction as program effectiveness signals.
Partner with Controls Engineers, Technicians, team managers, and DC Operations stakeholders across AMER to align curriculum to operational needs, coordinate SME content reviews, and prevent training materials from going stale.
Own the training program roadmap, milestones, and dependencies — including the onboarding platform, shadowing tooling, and training lab and communicate program status and metrics to senior leadership through regular reporting cadences.

This role directly support following three Controls job families. Understanding their day-to-day work is essential to building training that is practical, relevant, and immediately applicable.
Controls Engineers
Controls Engineers troubleshoot and perform Root Cause Analysis on Building Management System (BMS) and Electrical Power Monitoring System (EPMS) issues; manage the full project lifecycle from scoping and budgeting through commissioning; develop and modify controls logic and GUIs; financially manage BMS and EPMS service contracts; and participate in AWS global on-call schedules. They work with cross-functional stakeholders across construction, operations, and vendor management, and frequently travel to in-operation data centers.
Controls Technicians

They perform point-to-point checkouts, first-line diagnostics, server and controller provisioning, sensor installation and calibration, commissioning support, change management documentation, and factory witnessed tests. They also mentor Facilities team members and actively manage service agreements.
Systems Engineers
Systems Engineers are responsible for Deploy, manage, and support large-scale Windows and Linux environments, including virtualization platforms and networking components. They also create and maintain automation solutions using PowerShell, Python, or Bash, focusing on scalable deployment processes and infrastructure management

title: Principal Product Manager - Technical, AWS Proactive Security / Support Authorization, AWS Proactive Security - AWS Piezo
description:
The Mission
AWS customers trust us with their sensitive data. We are building AWS Support Authorization, the mechanism that puts the decision about Support access in the customer's hands. The customer defines what AWS personnel may do, scoped to their own resources and bound to their open support case, and sees the resulting access in CloudTrail. We are looking for a Principal Product Manager - Technical to own that product and define the experience every AWS service presents when it needs a customer's permission. Your work will change how AWS asks for access to customer content across its services, and it will carry to customer data protection at industry scale.
What You'll Own
You own the approval product end to end, from the API and console surfaces to the evidence a customer keeps afterward and the requirements AWS service teams build to. You define the approval model and the experience a customer moves through when AWS asks for permission, you set the success metrics, and you read the usage data to learn whether customers trust the control enough to use it. You partner with AWS Support, service teams, and Legal on what approval means in each operational context, and with GTM, Marketing, and PR on the strategy, messaging, and themes AWS uses to talk about customer approval and operator access, so what a customer hears matches what they find in the product.
The Product Challenge
A customer with an open case wants two things at once. They want to decide who touches their data, and they want their problem fixed now. Approval that feels meaningful to give takes effort to give, and the person paying that effort is already waiting on help. Designing an experience a customer trusts, can get through without stalling their own case, and recognizes whichever AWS service they called about is the center of this role. There is no predetermined answer. You define it, and you take the definition to the service teams that build to it.
The Impact
Your work will have CISO-level visibility. You write the decision narratives and investment proposals that set product direction, and you take them to VPs and the CISO. You set requirements for engineering teams that do not report to you, and you earn adoption by being right and being clear. You represent the product directly to customers in financial services, healthcare, and the public sector, who ask hard questions about who at a provider can reach their data. As the capability reaches the rest of AWS, the experience you define becomes the way AWS asks for a customer's permission.
What We're Looking For
You are a product manager with real technical depth and a long view. You think about what this product should be two and three years out, before customers have put words to the requirement, and about what it says about AWS to a customer deciding where to run a regulated workload. You have defined a platform product that other engineering teams adopted and built on without reporting to you, and you did it by writing requirements clear enough to survive contact with engineering. You read an authorization or access-control architecture closely enough to know which models a given service can implement. You work across the whole AWS portfolio, where services differ in how they are built and operated, and you guide VPs and directors on where the product goes next. You hold opinions about security and permissions experiences and you back them with customer evidence. You set strategy while the customer requirements are still being discovered, and you own the call when security and customer convenience pull against each other. You have worked with product marketing and PR on positioning a capability whose value is trust, and you have sat across from a regulated customer and answered hard questions about provider access. You develop other product managers as the product grows past what one person owns.
Key job responsibilities
Own the customer experience for AWS Support Authorization end to end: how a customer learns Support needs access, what the request tells them, how they decide, what proof they keep afterward. Define the consent model, covering approval granularity, defaults, duration, revocation behavior mid-case, and the evidence a customer receives. Set the requirements AWS services build to as the capability reaches the rest of AWS, and decide which elements a service team may shape to its own workflow. Own the API and console product surfaces. Define the success metrics and read the usage data to learn how customers respond to consent requests. Partner with AWS Support and service teams on what consent means in each operational context, and bring in Legal on the commitments the product makes to customers. Partner with GTM, Marketing, and PR on how AWS positions customer consent and operator access. Write the decision narratives and investment proposals that set product direction and present them to VP and CISO-level leadership. Represent the product directly to customers. Mentor PMTs and contribute to PMT assessments.
A day in the life
The AWS Proactive Security team builds the controls that protect customer data at scale. You start the day in the usage data, looking at how customers responded to consent requests over the past week and what that says about the experience. You meet a service team preparing to adopt Support Authorization, work through how consent should present for their access patterns, and decide what their integration can and cannot vary. Midday you review messaging with Marketing so the way AWS describes customer consent matches what the console does. In the afternoon you write: a narrative on where the consent model goes over the next two years, for a review with VPs and the CISO. You close the day on a call with a regulated customer walking them through the control and hearing what still gives them pause.

If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

At Amazon, security is central to maintaining customer trust and delivering delightful customer experiences. Our organization is responsible for creating and maintaining a high bar for security across all of Amazon’s products and services. We offer talented security professionals the chance to accelerate their careers with opportunities to build experience in a wide variety of areas including cloud, devices, retail, entertainment, healthcare, operations, and physical stores.

Training & Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, training, and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.
Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why flexible work hours and arrangements are part of our culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve.

title: Senior Power Development Manager (Technical Infrastructure Program Manager), Global Ops Enterprise Services
description:
Power availability is no longer a background variable — it is the binding constraint on where and how fast Amazon can grow its real estate network. Amazon WWOps Real Estate is looking for a Senior Power Development Manager (TIPM) to own power due diligence, utility engagement, and infrastructure strategy across the industrial real estate portfolio. You will embed power intelligence upstream in the site selection process, build repeatable frameworks that replace bespoke assessments, and develop strategic utility relationships that support Amazon investment plans and capacity availability. You will define how power development operates at portfolio scale and shift it from a reactive bottleneck into a proactive input that accelerates network delivery. Along the way, you will build a rare skill set that spans grid economics, real estate development, and capital strategy — a combination that is increasingly sought after across industrial infrastructure.
Key job responsibilities
- Own portfolio-wide power due diligence — load letter requests, substation capacity analysis, service territory research, and interconnection feasibility — to make power intelligence a scalable input to site selection.
- Build and maintain strategic utility relationships across priority markets, moving from transactional inquiries to partnerships that provide advance visibility into grid investment plans and capacity availability.
- Evaluate upstream infrastructure constraints such as interconnection lead times, feeder loading, transformer capacity, and distribution upgrade requirements to identify and de-risk capacity-constrained sites early in the pipeline.
- Translate complex utility and grid data into real estate economics, delivery timelines, and investment decisions for stakeholders across real estate, engineering, operations, design and construction, and transactions.
- Design repeatable processes, templates, and market intelligence tools that standardize power development across the portfolio and reduce assessment cycle time.
A day in the life
Your week alternates between external utility engagement and internal cross-functional coordination, with heads-down analytical work filling the gaps. One morning you might be on a call with a utility interconnection team negotiating service timelines for a capacity-constrained market; that afternoon you are presenting a portfolio-level power risk summary to directors across real estate and operations. Between meetings, you are interpreting substation data, modeling interconnection feasibility, or building the trackers and templates that make the next site evaluation faster. The cadence is deal-driven and portfolio-driven, with no sprint ceremonies or ticket queues. You operate with high autonomy as the dedicated owner of power development, self-organizing across dozens of concurrent site inquiries and using your judgment daily to decide where your time creates the most portfolio impact.
About the team
Amazon's Global Realty Energy and Power team sits at the intersection of utility engineering, real estate development, and energy market strategy. We are changing how the company secures and delivers electrical infrastructure across one of the world's largest industrial real estate portfolios, moving from transactional utility engagement to strategic infrastructure positioning. Our work directly determines whether Amazon can secure the grid capacity it needs, when it needs it, in the markets that matter most. Growth on this team comes through direct leadership engagement — regular one-on-ones, real-time feedback on your work, and sponsorship into cross-functional forums where senior leaders see your contributions firsthand. The role is scoped as a launchpad: build the capability, prove the model, then grow into energy strategy leadership, real estate development management, infrastructure program leadership, or deeper technical specialization in power markets. If you want to build a new capability from the ground up and shape how Amazon approaches power development, we would like to hear from you.

- Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Energy Systems, Power Engineering, or a related technical discipline
- Experience managing concurrent due diligence or project workstreams across a multi-site portfolio with competing priorities and aggressive timelines
- Experience in utility coordination, electrical infrastructure design, power development, or energy project delivery within large-scale utility, industrial, logistics, or data center environments
- Experience with utility easements, real property rights, and right-of-way documentation — including review, analysis, and coordination through resolution

You will also run field trials and stakeholder workshops to validate procedures, collect feedback and drive continuous improvement.

You care deeply about the process of applied scientific research, enjoy supporting technology investigations, and are comfortable jumping across multiple layers of the productization process when the team calls on you, from prototype through shipping. Experience with real-time or near-real-time systems and deeply integrated architectures that span local SoCs through cloud compute.

title: Audio Architecture Engineering Program Manager
description:

title: Audio Tools & Automation Engineer
description:
Imagine what you could do here! At Apple, new insights have a way of becoming extraordinary products, services, and customer experiences very quickly. Do you bring passion and dedication to your job? title: BSR Noise & Vibration Engineer
description:
At Apple, extraordinary ideas have a way of quickly becoming extraordinary products, services, and customer experiences. Sound is an essential and compelling facet of the customer experience. Apple has assembled an elite Acoustics team that enables our customers to experience music with delight, communicate with clarity, and enjoy elegant sound throughout our product line. In Apple Acoustics we work with the utmost attention to detail, directly impacting the design of products that millions of people around the world love!
Our Noise & Vibration team contributes to hardware design, validation, and troubleshooting to minimize distracting audible noises and optimize their sound quality. We are a diverse team of acoustics and vibration experts, accomplished listeners, and creative problem solvers. We work daily with multifunctional teams on innovative solutions to complex engineering challenges. We are looking for a Noise & Vibration Engineer to join our team. Could this be you?
As a BSR Noise & Vibration engineer, you will quantify noises, facilitate user studies, and establish thresholds in lab and factory environments. You will collaborate with cross functional teams to troubleshoot, identify source, and fix noises found during testing by providing design feedback to design teams. The analysis of the validation work that you will lead will help you to better understand root causes of various problems. To accomplish these tasks you will author procedures, test plans and specifications. As a part of a team, you will develop and facilitate use of objective test stations. You will work closely with team members who support product development builds at factories but will need to travel minimally.
Minimum qualifications: Bachelor’s degree or higher in Mechanical Engineering / Acoustics or equivalent field.
5+ years minimum experience in product development that includes acoustic design validation as well as vibration mitigation design.
Willingness to travel domestically and internationally.
Preferred qualifications: Knowledge of acoustic and vibration principles and how motion of mechanical systems turns into radiated noise.
Acoustic and vibration measurement skills with experience making measurements in anechoic/hemi-anechoic chambers and with data analysis /signal processing methodologies.
Ability to quantify noise response relationship to a system’s excitation (motion, thermal, or other) to effectively guide design improvements.
Accomplished listener with excellent hearing over the audible frequency range.
Ability to effectively communicate complex information and concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences.
Creative problem solver who thrives in a fast-paced multi-tasking environment.
Familiarity with statistical analysis methods, experience with precision-grade instrumentation including ultra low noise measurements, knowledge in electro-magnetic actuators, and familiarity with Matlab or other flexible data analysis software.

title: Battery Algorithm ML Engineer
description:
Are you interested to work on the forefront of Battery Management Systems? In this role you will develop future BMS technologies with a hardworking team of engineers in a highly reciprocal and multi-functional environment. title: Bluetooth Software Engineer, Wireless Technologies & Ecosystems
description:
Join the Wireless Technologies and Ecosystems organization and be part of an outstanding team of engineers driving innovation and developing products used by millions worldwide. title: Business & Financial Operations Analyst - AIML
description:

You will serve as a key operational partner in budget forecasting, and vendor procurement, delivering the insights, processes, and frameworks that empower leaders to optimize resource allocation, make informed decisions, and execute seamlessly against our highest priorities.

title: Business Assurance and Compliance Auditor
description:
The Business Assurance and Compliance group is looking for a motivated IT audit or Information Security professional to join our team. You'll lead or contribute to process and systems walkthroughs, test controls across ERP and cloud environments, and stay attuned to emerging regulatory and technology trends, translating them into practical control requirements. The role blends independent and team-based work across concurrent projects sourced from compliance stakeholders, business and finance teams.

Familiarity with both the technical stack (database to network to cloud) and core business processes (Order to Cash, Purchase to Payables, Hire to Retire, and others), bringing a valuable cross-organizational perspective.
Comfortable working independently and within a team, managing concurrent work from a variety of compliance or business sources with limited supervision.
Experience leading, or contributing to, process and systems walkthroughs as part of a risk or control gap assessment.
Strong project management and organizational skills.
Clear, confident communicator and equally effective in group presentations and one-on-one conversations.

title: CV/ML Generalist Engineer

Apple is looking for a creative, versatile Computer Vision and Machine Learning (CVML) Generalist Engineer to join a team of leading researchers and engineers. title: Camera Algorithms Engineer

DESIGN FLOW & METHODOLOGY DEVELOPMENT:
- Establish design guidelines, methodologies, and standards for synthesis, place-and-route, timing closure, and signoff processes

- Stay ahead of industry trends and emerging technologies to continuously improve design methodologies
- Apply strong programming skills (Python, Perl, TCL, Unix shell, C/C++) for methodology automation and enhancement
- Apply ML modeling experience for advanced design optimization and predictive analysis

Thousands of Apple engineers build, test, and ship services with Bazel, and they run it through our toolchain: bazel wrapper CLI, our Bazel Central Registry mirror, shared rulesets, and a remote build execution (RBE) platform that runs their actions at scale. The Bazel team builds and operates that toolchain. We make builds fast, hermetic, and reproducible, and we help large codebases move onto Bazel and stay there.
We're looking for an Engineering Manager to lead this team. You'll own the roadmap for Apple's Bazel ecosystem and RBE platform, and you'll grow a team of engineers whose work directly sets how fast other teams can ship. You'll also represent Apple in the open-source Bazel community.

Forge is part of Enterprise Technology Services (ETS), within Apple's Information Systems and Technology (IS&T) organization, the engine behind everything Apple does for customers and for the people who build for them. title: Materials Scientist - Capacitors
description:
Join Apple's innovative hardware team as a Materials Scientist for Capacitors, where you will own Apple's technology strategy across the polymer, electrolytic, film, and safety capacitor families — driving critical component solutions from initial concept to high-volume mass production across all Apple product lines.
In this senior role, you will serve as the primary technical expert bridging Apple's cross-functional teams with our global network of capacitor suppliers across the full non-MLCC capacitor space: tantalum polymer (including PFAS-free transition), aluminum polymer, aluminum electrolytic, film, safety/Y-rated, and emerging electrochemical energy storage technologies. You will be responsible for predicting component performance from supplier process choices — pellet morphology and sintering chemistry, oxide film formation kinetics, foil etch architecture, winding geometry, and conductive polymer chemistry — rather than relying on datasheet specifications, and will set Apple's technology direction across these families 3+ years ahead of integration. You will work closely with our existing Passive Component Technologists, SI/PI teams, LOB EEs, and commodity managers across iPhone, iPad, Watch, Mac, AirPods, Vision, Power Adapters, and beyond. This is an exceptional opportunity for a scientist or engineer with deep materials science or electrochemistry expertise who is passionate about making a significant impact at Apple. This role requires approximately 10–20% overseas travel.
Minimum qualifications: Deep Polymer, Film, and Safety Capacitor Expertise — Extensive professional experience across tantalum polymer (MnO₂ and conductive-polymer types, including PFAS-free pellet and termination chemistry), aluminum polymer & electrolytic (etch architecture, conductive layer deposition, ESR/ESL behavior), film capacitor construction (winding geometry, self-healing metallization, voltage derating), and safety/Y-rated capacitors (safe-failure construction, IEC 60384-14 X/Y classification, creepage and clearance). Proficiency in material characterization, DC-bias degradation, surge and leakage current reliability, and construction-to-performance modeling is required.
Materials Science and Electrochemistry Depth — Command of the physical mechanisms driving capacitor behavior: dielectric oxide formation kinetics (Ta₂O₅, Al₂O₃), pellet porosity and sintering, polymer conductivity and thermal stability, self-healing metallization failure modes, leakage current mechanisms, and capacitor-level safe-failure design. Ability to challenge and evaluate supplier process and material claims from first principles.
Cross-Disciplinary Knowledge — Familiarity with PDN and EMI filter circuit topologies, power supply design, IEC safety standards and regulatory frameworks (including PFAS/REACH restrictions and their supply-chain implications), and device-level reliability requirements across consumer electronics product categories.
Program Management and Influence — Proven ability to work as an individual contributor within a highly cross-functional environment. Must possess strong interpersonal skills to identify technical challenges, engage with suppliers, drive solutions, and manage development programs to successful and on-schedule delivery.
Hands-On Manufacturing Experience — A minimum of 5 years (preferably in a recent role) of direct, on-site factory floor experience with capacitor manufacturing processes is mandatory.
Education and Experience — PhD in Materials Science & Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Chemistry, or Physics with a minimum of 5 years of relevant professional experience in capacitor or passive component technologies.
Preferred qualifications: Solid track record of leading passive component product development from concept to mass-production across multiple capacitor technology families
Experience with PFAS-free materials qualification and supplier transition management
Familiarity with MLCC ceramic dielectric R&D and supercapacitor / EDLC construction and reliability limits is a plus
In-depth knowledge of capacitor supply chains, including tantalum ore sourcing, aluminum foil markets, and polymer electrolyte supply base
Strong interpersonal skills and demonstrated cross-LOB technical collaboration

title: Module System Engineer
description:
Apple is a place where extraordinary people gather to do their best work. Our community is
made up of every kind of individual: artists and designers, engineers and scientists, thinkers and
doers. Together we create things and experiences people once couldn’t have imagined — and
now can’t imagine living without. So if you’re excited by the idea of making a real impact, a
career with Apple might be your dream job. Just be ready to dream big.
We're looking for a Module System Engineer to design and deploy the test instruments that validate our camera and battery modules, from prototype through high-volume manufacturing. You'll build test fixtures, automated test sequences, and data acquisition systems; commission them at our factories; and use them to drive root-cause analysis when modules fail. Your work will directly shape the quality and reliability of modules used in consumer electronics, including smartphones, tablets, laptops, and wearable devices.
This is a generalist role. Prior camera or battery experience is a plus but not required — you'll build module domain knowledge on the job. What we need is strong fundamentals in test system design, electrical measurement, and problem-solving in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.
Minimum qualifications: Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Materials Science, or a related field with experience in electrical design
Experience in test equipment hardware design or hardware validation engineering for PCBs, flex circuits, or System-in-Package (SiP)

Demonstrated ability to learn new technical domains quickly

title: Network Business Development & Partnership Manager  - Wallet, Payments, and Commerce
description:
At Apple, extraordinary people come together to do their life’s best work. Together, we create products and experiences people once couldn’t have imagined, and now can’t imagine living without.
Our Payment Network Partnerships team manages and builds partnerships with payment card networks globally for Apple, including American Express, Mastercard and Visa.
We are seeking a Business Development & Partnership Manager to support Apple Pay and Apple Wallet growth globally, and to support Apple as a merchant from a payment network perspective. The scope encompasses current and future payment products and features (including alternative payments and digital wallets), the evolving payment card ecosystem (including card issuing, card acceptance, merchant acquiring, card processing, risk management, and card operations), adjacent products and services (e.g. transit, identity), the regulatory environment, and supporting Apple products and services that involve payment cards.
This role is ideal for a dynamic, results-oriented individual who thrives in high-growth, fast-paced environments and excels at building and scaling impactful partnerships across the global payment ecosystem.
This individual contributor business development role is external-facing with partners in the payment ecosystem and also requires broad internal engagement across functions and across Apple Pay markets globally.
The core responsibility for this role is to work across Apple and external partners to develop a roadmap that delivers on business priorities and enhances Apple Pay. This will involve understanding Apple’s product roadmaps and business priorities, analyzing markets and the competitive landscape, assessing growth opportunities, aligning on priorities and business plans, and managing and coordinating large initiatives or investigations.
Success in this role requires the ability to initiate and build strong and productive relationships at both senior leadership and operational levels. It also requires commercial judgement, analytical rigor, the ability to navigate complexity, and a bias for action.
Minimum qualifications: 6+ years of professional experience in financial services at either a payment network, card issuer, merchant acquirer, or PSP.
Understanding of consumer payments, including card issuing and acquiring, fraud and risk management, with a knowledge of international market dynamics and payments innovation.
Strong strategic thinking, analytical and financial modeling skills; ability to evaluate opportunities from both quantitative and qualitative perspectives.
Demonstrated success launching and scaling new products or business programs that require significant internal and external collaboration.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with experience presenting to executive teams.
Bachelor Degree or equivalent experience.
Preferred qualifications: Working knowledge of payment network rules and regulations.
Direct experience structuring and negotiating partnerships with global payment networks, issuers or FinTechs is desirable.
Experience coordinating and leading cross-functional teams, including product and engineering.
Highly organized and accustomed to knowing and working in the detail.
Ability to work with ambiguity and to manage multiple projects simultaneously.
Experience building and presenting executive-level business cases.
Deep understanding and passion for payments, emerging technology and web products.

title: PACE, Senior Regulatory Engineering Project Manager (EPM)
description:
Imagine what you could do here! Do you care about what makes products not only delightful, but safe, sustainable, and trustworthy? Apple’s Product Analysis & Compliance Engineering (PACE) group ensures our products don't just meet global Safety, Environmental, EMC, and Wireless regulations—they exceed them to set the standard for product integrity.

title: PMU Analog Layout Designer
description:

Working with circuit design team to plan/schedule work and negotiate any necessary layout trade-offs as needed to build complex analog layout in deep SubMicron CMOS technologies.

Running complete set of design verification tools available on Mega-cell level (also on chip level).

Utilizing advanced CAD tools and mask design knowledge to deliver correct and robust layout that meet stringent matching performance, area and power requirements.
Minimum qualifications: BS and a minimum of 3 years relevant industry experience
Preferred qualifications: Relevant experience in analog/mixed-signal layout design of SubMicron CMOS circuits.
Experience building tight matching, low capacitance, low power analog blocks, resistors, capacitors, high voltage devices, pad IOs, ESD structures, etc.
Experience with custom and standard cell based floor planning and hierarchical layout assembly.
Understanding of IR drop, RC delay, electro-migration, self-heating and cross capacitance.
Looking for relevant experience with analog and DFM practices.
Experience in PMU and chip level layout is highly preferred.
Scripting experience in PERL or SKILL CODE is considered a plus
Excellent communication skills and able to work with multi-functional teams.
Proficiency in interpretation of Calibre, DRC, ERC, LVS, etc. reports.
Knowledge of MENTOR GRAPHICS or CADENCE layout tools.
Master's Degree preferred.

title: PMU Design Verification Engineer: Analog & Mixed Signal Engineer
description:
Did you know that Apple is hiring analog & mixed signal verification engineers? We are looking for engineers that are enthusiastic to find bugs! You have the opportunity to work with a creative team to craft test plans and enable production-quality first silicon. As a member of the analog and mixed signal verification team, you will be working with specialists for full-chip verification of the state of the art mixed-signal systems used in Apple’s world-leading products!
In this role, you will be responsible for ensuring high quality silicon for IC chips and IPs. Daily work involves verification of mixed signal IC designs using a combination of analog circuits and RTL in the same simulation. Responsibilities include all phases of pre-silicon verification from early discussions with architects, reviewing specifications, writing verification plans, running simulations, triaging issues, and reviewing results with the team.
• Develop detailed test and coverage plans based on IC specifications.
• Completion of verification plans from beginning to end: test bench and environment bring-up, regressions, failure debug, and tape-out.
• Develop verification methodology suitable for the IP, ensuring scalability and portability.
• Develop verification environment, including stimuli, checkers, assertions, trackers, and coverage.
• Sign-off mixed signal designs in preparation for tapeout.
Minimum qualifications: BS and a minimum of 3 years of relevant industry experience
Preferred qualifications: Ability to verify analog/mixed-signal designs in a collaborative team environment.
Proficient in hardware descriptive languages: Verilog, System-Verilog, and/or Verilog-AMS code.
Familiarity with authoring analog assertion checks to catch bugs.
Capability to identify failure mechanisms and review verification results in analog IC designs.
Ability to write test plans, present results, and communicate clearly with multi-functional teams.
Comfortable with running simulations through compute clusters while optimizing simulation and wall time.
Understanding of both power management and related auxiliary circuitry: switching converters, linear converters, reference circuitry, bandgaps, data converters, and/or clock generators.
Have a familiarity with verification methodologies and tools: simulators, waveform viewers, execution automation, coverage collection, gate level simulations.
Experience developing scalable and portable test benches.
A background that includes scripting or programming languages is preferred. These include, but are not limited to, TCL, Skill, Python, and/or PERL.
Your familiarity with analog behavioral models is also a plus.

title: RealityKit Spatial UI Rendering Engineer
description:
Shape the future of spatial computing by building the rendering technologies that bring Apple's user interfaces into three dimensions. As part of the RealityKit team, you'll architect and optimize the systems that turn conventional app interfaces into spatial experiences, delivering exceptional visual fidelity, responsiveness, and power efficiency on Apple's next-generation vision products.
Operating at the intersection of Core Animation, SwiftUI, and RealityKit, you'll advance the architecture that renders windows, text, and controls as spatial content in real time. You'll also shape RealityView, the API through which developers combine app UI with 3D content. Your work will define the visual quality and performance characteristics of spatial UI, establishing the foundation on which developers and users interact with apps across Apple's vision ecosystem.
Description
As a Spatial UI Rendering Engineer on the RealityKit team, you'll own the rendering quality, power, and performance of spatial UI and RealityView. You'll drive the evolution of the rendering pipeline that brings Core Animation content into RealityKit, and develop the GPU techniques necessary to ensure UI elements maintain exceptional clarity and performance under spatial viewing conditions. Your scope includes texture resolution and filtering strategies, foveated and multi-view rendering of UI content, and the shader and render-pass optimizations that preserve the clarity of text and controls while minimizing GPU, memory, and power cost.
You'll also own how RealityView renders app UI and 3D content together, from the underlying rendering integration to the developer-facing behavior and APIs. You'll address complex rendering challenges, including maintaining legibility as viewing distance and render resolution change, rendering UI and 3D content together seamlessly, managing large texture workloads efficiently, and sustaining stable frame rates, memory, and power across extended sessions. You'll collaborate closely with the Core Animation, UI frameworks (UIKit, AppKit, and SwiftUI), Metal, and GPU teams to deliver cohesive solutions that meet Apple's standards for performance and user experience.
Minimum qualifications: Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or equivalent practical experience
5+ years of professional experience in real-time graphics or rendering engine development
Demonstrated ability to independently own and ship significant rendering features end to end
Proficiency in C++ and shader programming languages (Metal Shading Language, GLSL, or HLSL)
Solid understanding of texture sampling, filtering, and resolution management, and of GPU memory management and frame pacing
Familiarity with foveated rendering, multi-view rendering, or other advanced real-time rendering techniques
Proven record of diagnosing and resolving GPU performance, power, or memory issues using profiling tools such as Instruments, RenderDoc, PIX, or Perfetto

description:

title: Video Processing Engineer
description:
Do you love problem solving in a collaborative environment and then having the results of your efforts benefitting millions around the world? At Apple, our Architecture group is responsible for connecting our hardware and software into one unified system. Join this team, and you’ll collaborate with engineers across Apple to design how all of our technologies work in unison! You’ll drive development of our renowned system-on-a-chip architecture and develop algorithms to improve image quality and enable new use cases. You’ll develop forward-looking prototype systems as well as build and deploy software development tools that will be distributed to the Apple engineering community and help build the seamless technology experiences we’re known for worldwide.
This role will be responsible for investigating techniques for improving video processing solutions along the quality vs. power axes. State-of-the-art video processing solutions often involve the use of Machine Learning, but this can be computationally intensive and not practical. There exists a computational gap between Machine Learning techniques and traditional methods. The goal is to find operating points in between that can leverage the improved quality due to Machine Learning when needed and fall back to traditional, low-compute methods when not needed. Examples of video processing solutions that can benefit from using a hybrid solution comprised of traditional techniques and Machine Learning based techniques include (but not limited to) 1) Under Display Camera enhancement 2) Motion Estimation for Codec, GGM and MCTF 3) Face ID processing. The result of finding hybrid solutions is better video quality and/or longer battery life on the Phone, Pad and Mac. You will be responsible for investigating hybrid video processing techniques that can be translated into efficient SoC architectures. You will be expected to be able to translate architectures into specifications and C-models. You will also be expected to work cross-functionally with other Architects as well as Design and DV.
• Investigate and develop hybrid video processing architectures.
• Support chip architecture team and software teams to map algorithms into well-defined architectures that can be implemented in software and/or hardware.
• Generate architecture test vectors for quality validation.
• Write bit exact C-models of defined architectures.
• Support Design and Verification teams when verifying designs against bit exact C-models.
Minimum qualifications: BS degree
Ability to program in the following languages: Python, PyTorch and/or C/C++
Understanding of image/video/signal processing fundamentals
Understanding of neural network fundamentals
Preferred qualifications: MS or PhD degree or 3+ years of experience
Demonstrated ability of developing new image/video processing algorithms
Experience in developing neural network based image/video processing algorithms
Communication skills and ability to work across various groups
Understanding of fixed point representation and processing and/or ability to write bit-accurate software models
Understanding of pipelining and pixel processing architectures
Knowledge of computer architecture fundamentals

title: Box Truck Driver (Dallas-Fort Worth)
description:
ABOUT BASE

Base is America’s next-generation power company. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time.




ABOUT THE ROLE

The last mile delivery driver handles the final leg of delivery and installation getting Base Power battery systems to members' homes on time and setting them up right. Day-to-day work includes operating a 26ft box truck with a passenger team member, loading products, driving a route, installing ground-mounted batteries systems, and keeping accurate delivery records in our in-house app. 

What You'll Do

 - Deliveries: Transport and hand off products to residential and business addresses safely and on time

 - Equipment operation: Use electric pallet jacks and dollies to move pallets in and out of the truck

 - Battery installation: Stack batteries, complete light assembly, and commission the app-based system at each site

 - Member interaction: Answer or direct questions and address concerns on-site with clear, professional communication

 - Site cleanup: Remove all packaging and debris from the member's property before leaving

 - Route management: Follow efficient routes to hit delivery windows consistently

 - Vehicle upkeep: Keep the delivery vehicle clean and organized. Run basic maintenance checks before each shift

 - Delivery logging: Record delivery times, addresses, product, and notes accurately in the delivery app

 - Inventory: Assist with loading and unloading. Run truck cycle counts when requested

 - Safety: Follow all driving and product-handling safety protocols

 - Issue reporting: Flag delays, damages, missing items, or road issues to dispatch or a supervisor promptly

 

What You'll Bring

 - Valid driver's license with a clean record

 - Ability to pass a DOT physical

 - Experience driving box trucks, vans, or commercial vehicles preferred

 - Strong communication skills and comfort working directly with members

 - Able to learn and use apps, systems, and tech platforms required for the role

 - Able to lift and carry 50+ lbs

 - Comfortable navigating routes using GPS or mapping software

 - Self-directed and reliable in a fast-paced environment

 - Basic vehicle maintenance knowledge

 - Able to work outdoors year-round in all weather conditions

 

About the Team

Our delivery and warehouse team ensures solar batteries, inverters, and installation equipment reach residential job sites on time and in perfect condition. We handle the last-mile logistics that determine whether thousands of families get their clean energy systems installed on schedule. Your work directly impacts our ability to scale—every efficient route, properly kitted job, and damage-free delivery means another home powered by renewable energy instead of the grid.



Please note: Base is a startup, which means priorities shift and evolve quickly. Your role may expand or change based on the needs of the business at any given time, so the responsibilities listed may not be exhaustive.




OUR VALUES

 - First Principles Thinking: Question assumptions. Principles > rules.

 - Operate at Base Pace: Focus on what matters, act quickly, and learn by doing.

 - Give & Get Feedback: Be direct, be humble, and maintain a growth mindset.

 - Everyone’s an Owner: Follow through on commitments and own results.

 - Strong Opinions, Loosely Held: Drive clarity and make calls with imperfect information.

 - Committed to the Mission: Rebuilding the grid is a big challenge. We work hard because we care deeply about the impact we’re creating. We work in-person. It’s not a 9-to-5. We are all-in.

 - Fun & Optimism Coexist with Grit: Collaboration and celebration coincide with the intensity of building real things.
   
   


DO THE BEST WORK OF YOUR LIFE AT BASE.

 - Build the internal motion for real estate sourcing so deployments, launch, operations, and finance all plug into one process instead of five side conversations

 - Maintain the system of record for the portfolio: commencement dates, renewal windows, ROFO and ROFR rights, certificates of occupancy, insurance, and landlord contacts

 - Write the playbook as you go, so each new launch runs faster than the last and can be handed to the team running that market

description:
Senior Business Manager, Product Analytics
We are looking for a tenured, highly technical Product Analytics Sr. Manager to serve as a key architect for our experimentation and product strategy. This is a hands-on, individual contributor role for a seasoned practitioner who thrives in the weeds of data but operates with the strategic view to drive Product growth. You’ll team with world-class professionals to develop and test strategies that ultimately impact the bottom line. And you will do it all in a collaborative environment that values your insight, encourages you to take on new responsibility, promotes continuous learning, and rewards innovation.
You will help shape product development, quantify new opportunities, and identify upcoming challenges.  You will  help define the methodologies for how we measure success, serving as the subject matter expert in experimentation, causal inference, and metrics selection. Your work will help partner teams prioritize what to build, set goals, and understand their impact.
Your work will directly influence product direction, investment decisions, and the product vision for the Retail Bank. You will help drive product led growth by employing a varied toolkit of rigorous analytical approaches, different statistical methodologies, and frameworks to surface insights on new and exciting opportunities and challenges. This is a highly collaborative role in which you will problem solve alongside partners and leadership in Product, Engineering, Research, Data, Finance, and others.
Key Responsibilities
Product Strategy & Roadmap Influence: Partner closely with Product Management and Engineering to identify high-leverage growth opportunities. Translate complex behavioral data and user funnels into actionable product recommendations and feature requirements.
Experimentation & Causal Inference: Serve as internal authority on experimentation and causal inference. Define and enforce the standards for randomization, power analysis, and conversion window modeling. Design, analyze, and interpret complex A/B/n tests using advanced statistical techniques (randomization, power calculations, variance reduction, quasi-experiments) to isolate true customer incrementality.
Hands-On Technical Execution: Query, clean, and transform massive, complex datasets using SQL, Python, or R. Develop statistical models, user segmentation frameworks, and exploratory analysis to uncover engagement patterns.
Cross-Functional Leadership & Alignment: Drive alignment across cross-functional partners (Product, Tech, Research, Finance). Facilitate peer review gates to maintain rigorous analytical integrity and establish standardized KPI frameworks.
Data Storytelling & Executive Communication: Synthesize multi-faceted data insights into clear, strategic narratives. Able to influence audiences beyond vanity metrics to focus on underlying customer value and long-term business impact.
What success looks like
Proven Track Record: A seasoned analytical expert with significant experience in high-velocity product environments (e.g., e-commerce, fin-tech, or SaaS). You have navigated complex, ambiguous zero-to-one challenges and delivered clear outcomes.
Technical Mastery: Fluency in SQL and Python is a baseline requirement. Deep expertise in statistical modeling, DoE (Design of Experiments), and causal inference methodologies is critical.
Influencer Mindset: You possess strong executive communication skills and the ability to drive agreement through intellect and interpersonal negotiation rather than hierarchy. You can explain the "why" behind a complex statistical result to non-technical partners.
Product Sense: You understand how digital products are built, instrumented, and scaled. You know when to utilize centralized, self-serve experimentation tools versus when a high-bar, gate-kept methodology is required.
Basic Qualifications:
Bachelor’s Degree
At least 3 years of experience performing quantitative analysis
At least 3 years of experience performing qualitative analysis
At least 1 year of experience performing people management
At least 1 year of experience performing project management
Preferred Qualifications:
Master’s Degree in Business or quantitative field such as Finance, Economics, Physical Sciences, Math, Statistics, Engineering
5+ years of experience in quantitative analysis
5+ years of experience in qualitative analysis
2+ years of experience in people management
2+ years of experience in product development
2+ years of experience in financial modeling

2+ years of experience in project management

description:
Your Journey at Crowe Starts Here:
At Crowe, you can build a meaningful and rewarding career. With real flexibility to balance work with life moments, you’re trusted to deliver results and make an impact. We embrace you for who you are, care for your well-being, and nurture your career. Everyone has equitable access to opportunities for career growth and leadership. Join us at Crowe and embark on a career where you can help shape the future of our industry.
Job Description:
Forensic Accounting Managing Director - Litigation Support & Economic Damages
Essential Job Functions:
Economic Damages, Litigation & Forensic Analysis:
Lead complex economic damages and financial analyses in commercial disputes, including lost profits, breach of contract, intellectual property, business interruption, shareholder and other business disputes.
Develop, review, and defend sophisticated damages, valuation, and financial models using financial statements, transaction-level data, forecasts, market information, and other relevant evidence.
Evaluate opposing expert analyses, damages theories, assumptions, and methodologies; identify strengths, weaknesses, and alternative approaches.
Lead litigation support engagements from early case assessment through expert reports, depositions, arbitration, and trial, including preparation of expert exhibits and demonstratives.
Apply forensic accounting and investigative techniques where disputes involve allegations of fraud, accounting irregularities, asset tracing, or other complex financial issues.
Use quantitative analysis and data analytics to support damages calculations, forensic investigations, post-acquisition disputes, and other litigation-related inquiries.
Client & Engagement Management:
Conduct engagements in compliance with applicable professional, legal, regulatory, and firm requirements.
Manage a broad spectrum of matters involving investigations, litigation support, post-acquisition disputes, and insurance claims.
Lead a broad spectrum of matters involving economic damages, litigation support, forensic accounting investigations, post-acquisition disputes, and other complex financial disputes.
Position the team for successful engagement execution, quality results, and client satisfaction by clearly working within project parameters, managing resources and processes, and anticipating/resolving issues.
Serve as a senior advisor to clients and counsel, translating complex financial and accounting issues into clear, defensible analyses and practical litigation strategies.
Lead engagement execution, including scope, workplan, staffing, budgets, quality, risk management, expert-report development, and client satisfaction.
Manage engagement setup and completion activities, including conflicts, engagement letters, billing, collections, and other engagement administration.
Develop and maintain trusted relationships with outside counsel, in-house legal teams, executives, and other senior client stakeholders.
Recruit, mentor, and develop professionals across the damages and broader Disputes & Investigations team, including development of future expert witnesses.
Business Development:
Originate and expand economic damages and litigation support engagements through an established network of law firms, corporate clients, and referral relationships.
Build Crowe’s market position in economic damages and litigation support, with an expectation of developing into or continuing as a recognized testifying expert.
Identify opportunities to expand existing client relationships and cross-sell Crowe capabilities across forensic accounting, investigations, digital forensics, post-acquisition disputes, and other Advisory services.
Collaborate with Crowe partners and leaders across Advisory to identify disputes, litigation, and expert-services opportunities within existing client relationships.
Maintain and expand an external network of attorneys, experts, corporate decision-makers, and industry contacts to generate opportunities and strengthen Crowe’s brand in the disputes market.
Represent Crowe through relevant legal, accounting, damages, and industry organizations, conferences, CLE/CPE programs, publications, and other thought-leadership activities.
Develop a recognized area of expertise within economic damages and litigation support and contribute to Crowe industry and market initiatives.
Reporting & Communication:
Draft, review, and support expert reports, rebuttal reports, declarations, presentations, and trial demonstratives that clearly communicate complex damages and financial analyses.
Present complex financial concepts and conclusions to attorneys, executives, boards, arbitrators, judges, and juries in a clear and credible manner.
Serve as a senior client and counsel contact and, based on experience, provide deposition, arbitration, and trial testimony as an expert witness.
Basic Qualifications:
Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Economics, Business, or a related quantitative field required; advanced degree is a plus.
CPA, CFA, CFF, ABV, CVA, CFE, or other relevant professional credential strongly preferred. A CPA is preferred for candidates whose expert work is primarily accounting-based.
Minimum of ten (10) years of progressive experience in economic damages, litigation support, forensic accounting, valuation, dispute advisory, or related professional services, including significant responsibility for complex matters.
Significant professional-services experience with demonstrated responsibility for law-firm and client relationships, engagement leadership, team development, and financial performance.
Deep knowledge of economic damages methodologies and financial analysis, with experience in areas such as lost profits, breach of contract, intellectual property, business valuation, business interruption, shareholder disputes, or other complex commercial litigation.
Demonstrated experience developing or managing complex damages models and contributing substantially to expert reports, rebuttal analyses, deposition preparation, arbitration, and trial. Prior expert testimony is strongly preferred, but candidates with substantial second-chair or supporting-expert experience and a clear trajectory toward testimony will be considered.
Proven ability to manage multiple complex engagements simultaneously, including scope, budgets, staffing, deliverables, expert deadlines, risk management, and client/counsel expectations.

Leading organizational sourcing and procurement maturity assessments to understand gaps and opportunities and develop improvement plans
Building out detailed category sourcing strategies with clients to shape plans to improve commercial terms and improve alignment with suppliers
Facilitating ideation workshops independently to gain alignment with stakeholders and refine strategies grounded in feedback

Leading implementation of resulting supplier agreements
Supporting client optimization of sourcing and procurement organizational structures, policies, processes, and management practices

Collaborating with our extended team and client(s) to assess, design, and implement broader operational and supply chain transformation projects for diverse industries

Travel 95% of the time – Sunday through Thursday, more than 45 weeks a year (no flexibility on this)
Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management or a relevant field required, or more than ten (10) years of professional field experience
More than three (3) years of strategic sourcing experience – creating and executing category strategies independently, in industry or as a consultant

DoorDash’s DashOS business helps merchants grow and operate their businesses through technology that connects their own customer channels with the broader DoorDash ecosystem. Our Strategy & Operations team turns merchant needs and business opportunities into product and go-to-market priorities, then builds the operating capabilities needed to deliver them. We work across Product, Engineering, Sales, Marketing, Finance, and Revenue Operations to build and scale this business.

We are looking for a Director of Strategy & Operations to set the strategic direction and lead business operations within DashOS. You will translate a long-term vision into financial plans, product and go-to-market priorities, and an operating model that supports growth, merchant retention, and healthy unit economics.
You will lead the Strategy & Operations team, with direct ownership of product operations, and partner closely with leaders across go-to-market, launch and implementation, support, and account management. You will help design the operating model across these functions and stay closely involved in the merchant experience as the business scales. As a leader of managers and operators, you will build the team and systems needed to grow, align cross-functional leaders around shared outcomes, and navigate decisions involving merchant needs, growth, profitability, and partner dependencies. This role requires an entrepreneurial leader who can identify new opportunities, make thoughtful decisions amid uncertainty, and stay close to the operational details that drive results.

title: Manager, Lease Accounting
description:
About the Team
The DoorDash Lease Accounting team ensures DoorDash’s lease portfolio is reported accurately and on time under ASC 842. This requires deep technical accounting review and careful interpretation of complex, often ambiguous lease arrangements. As the portfolio grows in size and complexity, we continue to strengthen our processes to keep pace with the business.
About the Role
You will report to the Senior Accounting Manager on our Lease Accounting team. As the Lease Accounting Manager, you will be a key technical expert on ASC 842, ensuring DoorDash’s leases are accounted for accurately as the business grows. This role is built for someone who takes ownership, stays ahead of the work, and works closely with partners across functions. Success means well-supported conclusions and dependable reporting each period, with the opportunity to apply your expertise to increasingly complex leases.
You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…
Review lease abstractions against new lease agreements and lease modifications to ensure accurate classification and recognition of each lease in accordance with ASC 842.
Perform detailed accounting analysis of complex lease arrangements and unique scenarios that go beyond standard treatment, documenting conclusions and supporting analysis.
Perform lease monthly close activities including journal entries, account reconciliations, and flux analysis
Own lease financial reporting deliverables, including cash flows, rollforwards, and disclosures.
Partner closely with Real Estate, Lease Administration and other cross-functional teams to understand lease activity early and keep the accounting accurate and timely.
Proactively identify and lead process improvements and automation initiatives to reduce manual work and improve the accuracy and efficiency of processes.
Maintain lease SOX controls and support both internal and external audit requests.
We’re excited about you because…
Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, or a related field, and/or equivalent work experience.
6+ years accounting experience, including in-depth experience applying US GAAP lease accounting (ASC 842), which is essential to this role.
Proven experience reviewing lease agreements, interpreting lease terms, and assessing their financial implications to determine the appropriate accounting treatment.
Ownership mindset and proactiveness, with a track record of managing multiple deliverables and following them through to completion on close timelines.
Strong cross-functional partnership and communication skills to work effectively with internal and external partners.
Close attention to detail and demonstrated problem-solving skills.

The New Verticals team is building the future of local commerce through expanding our product offerings on our marketplace platform. You will build and execute the go-to-market plan that brings pharmacy merchants onto DoorDash, grows their volume, and keeps them. You'll work closely with Product, Engineering, Partnerships, Marketing, Finance, Legal, and New Verticals platform teams to be successful.
You'll be responsible for turning the pharmacy opportunity into a repeatable motion: planning and launching GTM programs, pitching and negotiating with merchants, and shaping how we speak to returning customers about pharmacy on DoorDash. You are the owner for knowing how Pharma merchants are performing, where the funnel leaks, and where to place the next bet to drive growth. You turn targets into operating plans, and plans into measurable outcomes.
This role requires strong commercial instincts and comfort with data. You should move fluently between merchant-level detail and business-level economics, build frameworks for tradeoffs and prioritization, and familiarity with modeling different scenarios and outcomes. title: Manufacturing Test Engineer - Dot
description:
About the Team
DoorDash is seeking a Staff Manufacturing Test Engineer to lead production testing for Dot, our autonomous road-going delivery robot. You will be the directly responsible individual for manufacturing test strategy, equipment, software, and fixturing at our final assembly site. You will also help define test requirements and acceptance criteria for subassembly lines and suppliers in coordination with our Manufacturing Quality team, and work with our Manufacturing Integration Engineer to productionize internal tooling. This is a hands-on role spanning prototype builds through production ramp. You will commission test stations, troubleshoot failures on the line, improve test coverage and yield, and ensure manufacturing processes consistently produce reliable robots. This role requires regular hands-on work in lab and production environments, occasional off-shift support during builds, and travel to supplier and manufacturing locations as needed.
You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…
Define the manufacturing test strategy and coverage for Dot components, subassemblies, and final robot assembly.

Track production test performance, including first-pass yield, false positives, cycle time, capacity, and equipment uptime.

Hands-on experience delivering and sustaining manufacturing test equipment for complex electromechanical products.

Strong electrical and mechanical troubleshooting skills, including familiarity with debugging PCBAs, motors, lithium-ion batteries, and wire harnesses.
Experience managing equipment from requirements and supplier selection through commissioning, qualification, and production support.
