title: Perception & State Estimation Engineer - DoorDash Air
description:
About the Team
DoorDash Labs is an independent team within DoorDash. We explore robotics and automation to transform last mile logistics in the long term. If you have a passion for applying robotics solutions in a service used by millions of people, then we want to talk to you!
About the Role
We're hiring a State Estimation & Perception Engineer in our Autonomy Software team. In this role, you'll own and develop the perception and state estimation for our package pickup and delivery system. You'll influence system design decisions, including sensor selection, sensing architecture, and observability analysis, at the earliest stage when choices still matter.
You're excited about this opportunity because you will…
Play an integral role on a small and focused team
Own tuning and implementation of the state estimation stack on the drone (PX4 EKF modifications, fault tolerance, multi-sensor fusion with VIO and laser odometry)
Own state estimation and perception of the delivery mechanism, including dynamics modeling, observation model design, and sensor selection
Work closely with controls and planning to close the loop on automated pickup and delivery
Work closely with the hardware team to define sensing principles and sensor placement
Design and execute flight test campaigns to validate estimator performance
Identify and resolve failure modes in estimation (degenerate geometries, sensor dropout, initialization)
We're excited about you because…
You have deep experience with state estimation and filtering (EKF, UKF, MSCKF, particle filters)
You have experience with optimization-based methods (factor graphs, GTSAM, Ceres, SymForce)
You have experience with visual-inertial odometry (VIO) and/or laser odometry (LIO)
You're proficient in modern computer vision (feature extraction, tracking, depth estimation)
You have strong C++ and/or Rust skills, with Python for prototyping and analysis
You have experience deploying estimation on real hardware with real sensor noise
You can derive an EKF from scratch, including process model, measurement model, observability analysis, and consistency checks
You have deep linear algebra knowledge (matrix decompositions, sparsity exploitation, numerical conditioning)
You've closed a perception-to-control loop on real hardware under degraded conditions
You're comfortable operating at the intersection of theory and embedded reality
You're driven by a passion for delivering outstanding customer experiences
You have a proactive approach to development, often crafting new tools
MS/PhD degree in CS, EE, ME, Robotics, or related technical field
Nice to have experience includes
Experience with PX4 / ArduPilot EKF internals
Experience with multi-body state estimation (tethered or suspended payloads)
Familiarity with SLAM in GPS-denied environments
Publications or open-source contributions in state estimation or VIO
You've debugged estimator failures in the field, not just in simulation
Applications for this position are accepted on an ongoing basis

Our Occasions pod sits within this team and our mission is to help DoorDash become the #1 destination to buy anything you need around seasonal and celebratory moments. location: Seattle, WA; New York, NY; San Francisco, CA; Los Angeles, CA
description:
About the Team
DoorDash for Business is building the premier corporate dining and benefits platform—helping companies of all sizes feed their teams through industry-leading products and meal programs. Our mission is to become the go-to solution for executives, administrators, and employees who need seamless, high-quality food programs at work. We move fast, operate with an ownership mindset, and are growing new product lines to better serve our corporate customers.
About the Role
As a Senior Associate on the DoorDash for Business Strategy & Operations team, you will help grow and run Self-Serve Meal Manager, our free, self-serve product that automates recurring meals for teams and offices. Because the product is self-serve, growth is product-led: customers find us, sign up, set up a calendar, and decide whether to stay without a sales rep in the loop. Your job is to make every stage of that funnel work better.
Acquire: Bring new teams in at the top of the funnel, both on the DoorDash platform (merchandising, in-app placements, lifecycle messaging) and off platform (paid, email, and organic channels).
Activate: Turn sign-ups into first orders through strong onboarding, and find and fix where customers drop off.
Retain: Keep teams ordering through a reliable, high-quality product experience, and catch the issues that cause churn before customers leave.
This is a role for someone versatile who will wear many hats: analyst, growth operator, customer-facing problem solver, and product partner. You will be expected to find a problem in the data, work out why it is happening, and drive the fix yourself. The role is built to grow. As the product scales, so will your scope and ownership.
You will report to the Manager, Strategy & Operations for DoorDash for Business and can work remotely or hybrid depending on preference.
You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…
Own the funnel: Analyze the self-serve funnel end to end, from visitor to sign-up to activation to repeat ordering. Find where customers drop off and run experiments on acquisition channels, onboarding, selection, and promotions to lift conversion and retention.
Go deep on the data: Write SQL daily to size problems, segment customers, measure lift, and tell a real result from noise. Build the dashboards and automated checks that let a small team support a growing customer base.
Work directly with customers: Email customers, resolve issues, and run proactive outreach to teams that are stuck, at risk, or churned. Hear first-hand why people stay and why they leave.
Turn issues into patterns: Translate individual customer problems into trends, then flag them to product and engineering with a clear call on severity: urgent and big, or real but minor, backed by the metric impact.
Improve reliability: Root cause order defects such as late deliveries, point of sale issues, and failed drop-offs. Work with merchants, Dashers, and support partners on fixes and track the impact on quality metrics.
Use AI to scale: Build AI-assisted workflows that flag at-risk customers, orders, and merchants, and replace slow manual analysis and one-off fixes with repeatable processes the team can maintain.
Influence the roadmap: Bring customer, merchant, and order data to product, engineering, and operations partners as clear recommendations.
We're excited about you because…
You have 2–5 years of experience in strategy and operations or growth, ideally at a marketplace company, a high-growth B2B startup, or an early-stage AI company.
You are deeply analytical. You write SQL fluently, are comfortable with large datasets, and can get to a root cause and turn complexity into a clear recommendation.
You have run growth or conversion experiments and can tell a real lift from noise.
You are hungry to learn and quick to pick up new domains, tools, and skills. You are versatile, happy to switch between analysis, customer conversations, and process building, and you want a role you can grow into.
You are comfortable in customer-facing work: writing clear emails, handling frustrated customers, and resolving issues with empathy and ownership.
You have a product mindset. You can spot patterns across customer issues and judge what is urgent and what is not, and you can make that case to product partners.
You are extremely comfortable using AI (e.g., Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, or similar) in your daily work to automate workflows, analyze data, and make faster, better decisions.
You own problems end to end, from diagnosis to testing to rollout, and are comfortable building processes in ambiguous, early-stage environments.
You communicate with clarity and influence, tailoring your message for customers, merchants, cross-functional partners, and senior leadership.

DoorDash’s mission is to grow and empower local economies. By building intelligent, last-mile delivery technology for local cities, DoorDash connects people with the local businesses they care about — helping grow businesses and the communities that support those businesses.
To help further that mission, the B2B Marketing team is responsible for helping Merchants,  Advertisers, and businesses find the right DoorDash products and services to grow. We do this by building lasting relationships with our B2B audiences through personalized, scalable, cross-channel experiences that drive retention and engagement. We take pride in being the trusted advisor to our Advertisers and DoorDash for Business customers, and their prominent advocate to our cross-functional partners — navigating them through every step of their DoorDash journey and empowering them with the right, personalized resources, education, and suite of solutions to maximize their business, at scale.

For Ads, you will drive awareness and adoption of the Ads & Promotions product suite across SMB, Enterprise, and CPG advertisers. For DDFB, you will drive adoption and activation of the DoorDash for Business suite among company administrators and their employees (B2B2C). Both are new and fast-growing businesses, so this is a chance to build from the ground up and own a “mini startup” within a wildly successful organization, leading a team that strategically leverages every touchpoint to deepen these customers’ relationships with DoorDash and support their long-term success.

8+ years experience in B2B marketing, engagement or operations with 5+ years managing high performing teams

Experience in B2B2C, SaaS, or advertising products and familiarity with SQL are a plus
Bachelor’s Degree; Master’s degree a plus

description:
About the Team
DashMart is a local-fulfillment center owned and operated by DoorDash, offering customers household essentials and other items to their doorsteps with speed, reliability, and quality.

In this role, you’ll manage a 5-15k sq ft distribution center, the local warehouse operating team, and be responsible for ensuring we maintain high quality for our customers.
You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…
Lead: Recruit, lead, coach & retain a high-performing team of Shift Leads (3+) and Operations Associates (6+). Set your team up for success to work safely and productively. As a leader, you will be responsible for building a strong, positive culture and will be accountable for driving strong employee satisfaction scores. You’ll partner with your Shift Leads to effectively delegate daily tasks and ensure high performance from your team.

Work cross-functionally with central teams including our inventory and training teams to provide your team with the tools and resources to achieve this goal.

You act like an owner. You do what it takes to support a 24/7 business across multiple shifts. You’re excited to have ownership over a new and rapidly growing business.
You solve problems from first principles.   You’re excited to solve problems in innovative ways, and you resist “this is how it’s always been done” thinking

The Strategic Inside Sales team drives DoorDash’s growth by acquiring high-impact restaurant brands across key markets. The team focuses on higher-value and more complex opportunities, working with local and regional operators whose scale meaningfully shapes the marketplace.
Through disciplined execution, thoughtful prioritization, and a consultative sales approach, Strategic Inside Sales expands DoorDash’s merchant ecosystem while helping restaurant partners understand how DoorDash’s platform and solutions can support their growth.
About the Role
As a Strategic Account Executive (SAE), you will acquire high-value restaurant partners in DoorDash’s most strategic markets. You’ll own the full sales cycle, from prospecting and prioritization through discovery, negotiation, and close, while managing a high-volume portfolio of opportunities with varying levels of complexity and potential impact.
Success in this role requires more than activity. You’ll use data, technology, AI-enabled tools, and strong business judgment to determine where to spend your time, how to approach each opportunity, and how to navigate more nuanced commercial conversations.
You’ll have autonomy over your day and pipeline while being accountable for clear activity, pipeline, and revenue outcomes. You’ll also work cross-functionally to structure deals, solve merchant challenges, and continuously improve how we sell.
We expect this role to be flexible, with a mix of remote and in-office work. You will need the ability to travel as needed for trainings, offsites, team-building events, and other business needs.
You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…

Prioritize for impact: Manage a large portfolio of prospects and opportunities while using data and business judgment to focus time on the highest-value opportunities.
Run the full sales cycle: Lead merchants from initial outreach and discovery through negotiation and close, adapting your strategy based on merchant needs and deal complexity.
Navigate commercial conversations: Understand merchant economics, evaluate potential deal structures, and negotiate intentionally within established financial guardrails.
Build and manage pipeline: Maintain disciplined outbound activity across calls, emails, and follow-ups while creating and advancing sufficient pipeline to consistently deliver against goals.
Leverage technology and AI: Use CRM, sequencing, automation, AI-enabled tools, and other sales technology to research accounts, prepare for conversations, improve productivity, and make better decisions.
Exercise ownership and judgment: Identify obstacles, independently determine next steps, and bring in cross-functional partners when their expertise can meaningfully advance an opportunity.
Continuously improve your craft: Use performance data, coaching, and experimentation to identify gaps, refine your approach, and adapt quickly when a strategy isn't working.
Raise the bar for the team: Share successful approaches, tools, and learnings that can improve execution beyond your individual book of business.
Represent DoorDash at a high standard: Deliver a thoughtful merchant experience that establishes credibility and creates the foundation for a long-term partnership.
We’re excited about you because you have…
3+ years of inside sales or B2B sales experience, including demonstrated success in a closing role.
A track record of meeting or exceeding quota in a fast-paced, high-volume sales environment.
Experience managing a portfolio of opportunities and prioritizing across accounts with different levels of complexity and revenue potential.
Experience navigating higher-value or more complex deals, including multi-location or larger SMB customers.
Strong prospecting, discovery, objection-handling, negotiation, and closing skills.
Strong business judgment and the ability to make decisions with incomplete information.
A high level of ownership and comfort independently diagnosing problems and determining next steps.
A data-driven approach to understanding your performance and identifying opportunities to improve.
Experience using CRM and sales technology such as Salesforce, Outreach, Sales Navigator, or similar tools.
Curiosity and willingness to adopt emerging technology, including AI, to improve productivity and sales effectiveness.
A growth mindset and demonstrated ability to incorporate coaching, test new approaches, and adapt quickly.
Curiosity about local businesses, technology, and how platforms like DoorDash can create value for merchants.

description:
About MISUMI Americas
MISUMI Americas, a division of MISUMI Group, is a leading provider of standard, configurable, and custom manufacturing solutions. With operations in the San Francisco Bay Area and Chicago, the company serves as a vital partner for the most innovative companies in the Americas.
About the Foundation
MISUMI Imprint Foundation is the first corporate giving organization in MISUMI Group 's history. It launched in October 2026 with a $2 million seed investment from MISUMI Americas and a mandate to fund the people who will build the physical world.
The reasoning is straightforward. MISUMI supplies the components that engineers design into machines, and as AI moves out of software and into factories, vehicles, operating rooms, and orbit, demand is rising for engineers, machinists, and technicians who can build hardware that works safely and reliably in the real world. The United States is not producing enough of them. The Foundation exists to widen that pipeline.
We make grants in three areas:
Scholarships & Access — need-based support for first-generation and underrepresented students in engineering, manufacturing, and supply chain, at four-year universities and community colleges alike
Maker Programs — equipment grants for manufacturing labs, engineering team sponsorships, maker spaces, and student hackathons
Industry–Academia Bridges — curricula built around real manufacturing problems, internship and apprenticeship pathways, mentorship and career support
The Foundation launched under the fiscal sponsorship of the SME Education Foundation and has filed for independent 501(c)(3) public charity status. Its defining structural feature is partner co-investment: MISUMI's global supplier partners are invited to contribute annually and join the Foundation Advisory Board, with seats at three tiers — Founding, Growth, and Community Partner.
About the role
This is a founding role. The mission is set, the seed capital is committed, and the board is in place. Almost everything else is yours to build: the first grant cycle, the review criteria, the partner program, the measurement framework, and the independent organization itself.
You will be the Foundation's first full-time employee and its public face — to universities and community colleges, to K–12 and robotics programs, to MISUMI's supplier partners, and to the press. You will report to the Board Chair and work closely with MISUMI Americas leadership, but the Foundation's day-to-day direction will be set by you.
We are looking for someone who wants the version of this job where the answers do not exist yet.
What you'll do
Build and run the grantmaking. Design the application, review, and award process across all three program areas. Source and evaluate grantees. Set award sizes and durations. Make the hard calls about what we fund and what we decline, and be able to explain both.
Grow the partner co-investment program. Recruit supplier partners into the Founding, Growth, and Community tiers. Run the Advisory Board, which convenes twice yearly to set grant priorities and announce awards jointly. Manage relationships with senior executives at some of the world's largest component manufacturers.
Complete the transition to an independent 501(c)(3). Work with counsel and the board to move the Foundation out of fiscal sponsorship into standalone operation — governance, policies, financial controls, audit readiness, and state charitable registrations.
Measure and report honestly. Define what success looks like beyond dollars granted, build the data to track it, and publish results — including the parts that did not work. Produce the Foundation's annual report.
Represent the Foundation externally. Speak at conferences and on campuses. Work with MISUMI Americas marketing on announcements and storytelling. Build relationships with industry bodies, workforce coalitions, and peer funders.
Build the team. Scope and hire the Foundation's next one to three roles as grant volume justifies them.
First-year priorities
Open and close the inaugural grant cycle, with a defensible process and a portfolio you can stand behind
Secure the first cohort of Founding Partners and hold two Advisory Board meetings
Complete the 501(c)(3) determination and operational transition from fiscal sponsorship
Publish a measurement framework and the Foundation's first annual report
Establish institutional relationships with a target set of universities, community colleges, and K–12 programs
Desired Traits
Seven or more years in philanthropy, workforce development, education, or a closely adjacent field, including direct ownership of a grantmaking or scholarship program — you have made funding decisions, not only administered them
Experience building something from the beginning. A founding role, a new program inside a larger institution, or an organization you took from idea to operating. Comfort with ambiguity is not a nice-to-have here
Credible with two very different audiences. You can hold a room of community college deans and a room of manufacturing executives, and you do not change your argument between them
Fundraising or partner development track record. You have asked people for significant money and been told yes
Working knowledge of nonprofit governance and compliance — 501(c)(3) requirements, fiscal sponsorship, board management, charitable registration. You do not need to be a lawyer, but you need to know what you are looking at
Clear writing. Grant guidelines, board materials, annual reports, and declines all live or die on it
Genuine interest in manufacturing and engineering education. You do not need an engineering degree. You do need to find this industry interesting enough to learn it properly
Helpful, not required
Background in engineering, manufacturing, or the skilled trades, or lived experience of a technical education pathway
Familiarity with community college and technical program funding, CTE, or registered apprenticeships

Japanese language ability or experience working across U.S. and Japanese organizations

Competitive salary, health coverage, retirement contribution, and paid time off
Remote-first, with travel to campuses, partner sites, MISUMI Americas offices, and the Advisory Board convenings

Fortune Brands Innovations is hiring a Manager, Product Integrity to join our Connected Products team .  Product Integrity is the team that confirms our connected products — Flo by Moen water devices, Yale and August smart locks, and Master Lock connected padlocks — do what their requirements say they do before they reach a customer. This role leads that team and owns the bridge between requirements and proof: taking what Product, Systems Architecture, and Compliance ask for and turning it into tests with a method, a sample size, and a pass/fail criterion.
The role also owns 100% end-of-line testing at the factory, including test fixture design and test software. Depending on test complexity, fixtures are built fully in-house or developed with a supplier.
We are looking for a systems architect who leads a test team . The right person understands the whole product — electrical, mechanical, firmware, and how they interact — well enough to argue a requirement with Product, an interface with Architecture, and the statistics with Reliability, and then run the lab that proves it.
Position location: this position is eligible to work in a hybrid environment out of our North Olmsted, OH or San Francisco, CA locations.
What you will own
The Product Integrity team. Lead a team of test engineers covering production and 100% test, hardware test, reliability test, quality inspection, and overall confirmation of product requirements. You set the direction and the standard; the team executes.
Requirements into tests. Turn every hardware requirement in the PRD — from Product, Systems Architecture, and Compliance — into a testable requirement with a method, a sample size, an acceptance criterion, and a gate. Product defines the design envelope; you define how we test to it.
Gate evidence. Every stage gate (EVT, DVT, PVT) carries your evidence package: what was tested, against which requirement, with what result.
Reliability. Define the reliability test plan for each program and own the statistics behind it: sample sizes, confidence levels, and acceleration factors for environmental testing.
Production test. Develop fixtures and test software that meet approved cycle times, with test limits tied to expected field performance.
Field performance. Review returns and field data, and feed what you learn back into requirements and test plans.
The team and the logistics
Team: test engineers covering production test, hardware test, reliability test, and quality inspection. The lab is in North Olmsted.
Location: North Olmsted, OH or San Francisco, CA. If based in San Francisco, expect occasional travel to North Olmsted.
Travel: ~15%. Travel to factories in Nogales and Tecate, Mexico; Hanoi, Vietnam; and between North Olmsted and San Francisco.
Qualifications
10+ years on connected consumer hardware spanning electrical, mechanical, and firmware.

Basic knowledge of CO₂ and Freon systems, plumbing, and soldering

description:

Miller is building a new software-as-a-service business from the ground up: cloud software for the welding and fabrication industry, backed by nearly a century of industry leadership and the resources of ITW. Minimum 10+ years of toolroom, tool & die, or precision machining experience preferred.

description:

As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care , our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion —have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.

Primary Function of Position
The Global Access, Value and Economics (GAVE) organization at Intuitive is seeking a highly motivated, hard-working, and professional AI/ML Engineer Intern to join our team for Summer 2027. The AI/ML Engineer Intern will support GAVE’s mission of generating clinical evidence to drive the adoption of robotic-assisted surgery. They will work within the Global Access and Evidence Management Center of Excellence to develop a system to optimize evidence management and synthesis processes. They will design a tool to identify, deduplicate, validate, and ingest new publications related to Intuitive products. They will also work with the team to integrate existing large language model (LLM) pipelines into this solution. The intern will get hands-on experience with software development, data management, machine learning, and systems design thinking. Beyond technical skills, this internship will require effective communication with numerous cross-functional stakeholders.

Design an end-to-end data pipeline to optimize critical evidence management, synthesis, and generation processes.
Implement and automate publication search and deduplication strategies.
Assist in integrating additional large language model (LLM) workflows into this system.
Collaborate with cross-functional stakeholders to develop the solution.
Present and interpret findings to a broad range of teams across the organization.
Required Skills and Experience
Self-motivated individual with a strong interest in data science and machine learning.
Proven ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams and address the needs of multiple stakeholders.
Excellent mix of communication and technical skills to engage effectively across all audiences.
Self-driven problem solver who can work with minimal supervision.
Strong desire to learn and grow in the field of data science and machine learning.
Proficiency with Python programming language.
Strong understanding of relational databases and SQL.
Solid grasp of machine learning concepts and algorithms.
Understanding of systems thinking and system design principles.

Current enrollment in a Computer Science, Data Science, Computer Engineering, or related degree-seeking program at the Bachelor’s or Master’s level.

None

Experience with LLM APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure OpenAI, or similar), including prompt engineering and structured outputs.

Experience with NLP techniques such as vector embeddings and semantic similarity.

Experience with scikit-learn is a plus.

Enable teams to build sustainable programs with surgeons, care teams, hospital leaders, key opinion leaders, training centers, and reference sites.

Define leading and lagging indicators for program effectiveness, adoption progress, launch readiness, content utilization, and return on investment.
Work with FSO to create dashboards and decision forums that help leaders assess progress, resolve barriers, redirect low-value work, and scale successful programs.
Support initiative portfolio tracking by clarifying owners, milestones, dependencies, risks, and expected outcomes.
Support budget planning, tracking, and forecasting for cardiac Market development and marketing programs, in partnership with the Cardiac Sales Directors, VP US Marketing, and VP, Global Cardiac.

Design scalable processes, standards, and ways of working that increase execution quality, speed, consistency, and accountability.
Clarify interfaces and handoffs across Global, Regional, and local Market teams to reduce duplication, scale best practices, close gaps, and improve matrix efficiency.
Establish quality controls for plans, programs, content, metrics, and launch deliverables, so work is compliant, decision-ready, and fit for use.
Facilitate cross-functional problem-solving and remove barriers that limit field execution or customer impact.
Contribute to a culture of disciplined experimentation, learning, and continuous improvement using data and field feedback.

Capitalize on synergies with US Thoracic Marketing Team to maximize opportunities at accounts, society meetings, and other marketing plans.

Partner with US commercial teams to drive alignment through influence and collaboration.
Act as the US point of contact for the VP, Global Cardiac on implementation of key global society initiatives, programs, training curricula, and global KOL development initiatives.
Communicate progress, insights, and performance clearly to the Cardiac Sales Directors, VPs/GM US, and the VP Global Cardiac.

The Human Factors Manager works closely with fellow Human Factors managers and engineers and collaborates with other cross-functional managers of clinical engineering, system and software engineering, product managers, and program managers among other important functional teams in the development of novel technologies and devices.
The Human Factors Manager's primary role is to support, inform and guide development of Human Factors team members and represent the Human Factors function within and across business units, ensuring the successful execution of Human Factors Usability Engineering Initiatives, process activities and deliverables, while keeping a patient-first mindset, acting as an advocate for the clinical caregiver end-users regarding safety and usability, and as representative for medical device regulatory compliance.
As a member of new product-development project teams, the Human Factors Manager leads as a key stakeholder within a creative and structured process to help their direct HF team plan, communicate and advocate the value of Human factors function, and execute the appropriate scale of usability engineering activities prior to launch, within a regulated design controls environment.

Forecast planning and budgeting for needed usability research and testing efforts, including estimates for needed resources and equipment.
Mentor, support and guide HF team members in the translation of design insights into actionable usability considerations and requirements and proactively collaborate with design engineering partners to ensure best in class usability.
Support the execution of, and report to leadership on, usability research and evaluations at various stages of product development.
The Human Factors Manger will balance testing efforts across multiple projects from early prototypes to formal External Standards-mandated validation testing in US and OUS market environments.
Advocate strongly and consistently for the clinical caregiver experience for safety and usability, with understanding of the nuance and balance of user/customer needs and business needs.
Interface and associate with end-user customers in multiple international markets to gather design insights in a highly professional manner, during complex workflow-oriented usability formative study and user research activities.
Write and revise highly accurate, clear, and concise usability engineering documents in a timely manner for multiple projects.
Synthesize complex information into internal communications and presentations for product teams and broader organization leadership audiences.
Prepare and review documentation for submission to regulatory agencies and notified bodies, including supporting the response to questions for additional justification and rationale

Demonstrated experience in HF (UX) and User Research project management.
Demonstrated experience of successful execution or direct support of global regulatory submissions.
Keep abreast of regulations and best practices for medical device
human factors (e.g. IEC 62366, AAMI HE75, FDA Applying Human Factors and Usability Engineering to Medical Devices) and advise management regarding potential improvements to internal processes and regulatory issues related to usability engineering.
Excellent verbal communication and presentation skills working within a highly statured communication environment using multiple communication channels (email, text, video conference, instant messaging platforms).
Experience working with Digital project collaboration tools is appreciated. (e.g. Mural, Smartsheets, etc).
Demonstrated ability to advocate and effectively champion user-centered design and usability engineering principles to product research, development, and design in a fast-paced product development environment.
Demonstrated ability to collaborate with and across various functional leadership and levels of management within the organization, including other engineering groups, marketing, clinical engineering, and regulatory to solve complex usability issues involving detailed risk analysis.
Ability to travel internationally as well as domestically (up to 20%; 25-30%)

Position Summary
The Quality Assurance Manager, Audits & Inspections is responsible for the planning, execution, management, and continuous improvement of the company’s GxP audit and regulatory inspection readiness programs supporting late-stage pharmaceutical development.
The role provides hands-on leadership for internal, external, vendor, and study-related audits and establishes a sustainable inspection-readiness program as the organization progresses through Phase 3 clinical development toward regulatory submission, pre-approval inspection, and commercialization readiness.
Working under the direction of the Head of Quality Assurance, the Manager partners with Clinical Operations, CMC, Regulatory Affairs, Pharmacovigilance, Nonclinical, and other functional teams to identify compliance risks, assess inspection readiness, manage audit observations and corrective actions, and ensure the organization and its critical service providers remain prepared for regulatory inspection.
This is a hands-on individual-contributor role requiring demonstrated experience conducting GxP audits and supporting FDA and/or other health-authority inspections.
Key Responsibilities
Audit Program Management
Develop and maintain a risk-based annual and multi-year GxP audit program covering internal functions, clinical studies, CROs, CDMOs, laboratories, pharmacovigilance providers, and other critical GxP vendors.
Plan, schedule, conduct, document, and close GxP audits in accordance with approved procedures and applicable regulatory requirements.
Develop audit plans, agendas, checklists, reports, observations, and follow-up documentation.
Evaluate audit observations for regulatory significance, systemic risk, and potential impact on product quality, subject protection, data integrity, and regulatory submissions.
Track audit findings, commitments, CAPAs, and effectiveness activities through closure.
Perform audit trending and provide periodic reporting of significant findings and emerging compliance risks to QA leadership.
Regulatory Inspection Readiness
Develop and maintain the company’s inspection-readiness program for FDA and other applicable health authorities.
Support readiness for BIMO, GCP, GMP, GLP, GVP and, as applicable, Pre-Approval Inspections (PAI).
Conduct inspection-readiness assessments, mock inspections, document reviews, interview preparation, and functional readiness exercises.
Identify potential inspection vulnerabilities and coordinate remediation activities with responsible functional owners.
Maintain inspection-readiness tools, procedures, playbooks, request-management processes, and supporting documentation.
Support development and maintenance of inspection war-room, document-request, response-review, escalation, and communication processes.
Regulatory Inspection Management
Support the Head of Quality Assurance in coordinating and managing regulatory inspections.
Facilitate inspection logistics, document requests, SME preparation, inspection-room activities, and real-time issue escalation.
Review proposed responses and supporting evidence for accuracy, completeness, consistency, and regulatory defensibility.
Support evaluation and response to inspection observations, including FDA Form 483 observations and comparable health-authority findings.
Track post-inspection commitments and associated CAPAs through completion and effectiveness verification.
Vendor and Partner Quality Oversight
Conduct qualification, routine, for-cause, and risk-based audits of CROs, CDMOs, laboratories, and other GxP service providers.
Evaluate vendor audit findings in the context of sponsor oversight responsibilities and program risk.
Partner with functional owners to establish appropriate remediation and escalation plans.
Support vendor qualification and ongoing performance monitoring based on audit results, quality events, compliance history, and risk.
Compliance Risk & CAPA
Identify emerging or systemic compliance risks through audit findings, inspection trends, quality events, and other quality intelligence.
Support or lead root-cause investigations associated with significant audit and inspection findings.
Review CAPAs for adequacy, proportionality, sustainability, and regulatory defensibility.
Perform or coordinate CAPA effectiveness verification associated with audit and inspection observations.
Escalate significant compliance risks promptly to the Head of Quality Assurance.
Cross-Functional Quality Partnership
Serve as a hands-on QA resource to functional teams preparing for audits and regulatory inspections.
Provide training and coaching to employees and SMEs regarding inspector interactions, documentation practices, inspection conduct, and response expectations.
Collaborate with QMS and GxP QA program functions to translate audit and inspection findings into sustainable improvements to the Quality Management System.
Maintain appropriate independence and objectivity when conducting audits and evaluating compliance.
Promptly escalate requests requiring significant regulatory interpretation, acceptance of material compliance risk, or final compliance disposition to the Head of Quality Assurance before communicating a final QA position.
Required Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in life sciences, pharmacy, chemistry, engineering, or another relevant discipline.
Minimum of 7 years of progressive pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or regulated life-sciences Quality Assurance experience.
Demonstrated hands-on experience planning, conducting, documenting, and closing GxP audits.
Experience conducting audits of CROs, CDMOs, laboratories, clinical sites, or other regulated service providers.
Demonstrated experience supporting FDA or other health-authority regulatory inspections.
Strong working knowledge of applicable FDA regulations, ICH guidance, and GxP requirements.
Experience with audit observations, investigations, CAPA development, remediation, and effectiveness verification.
Strong technical writing skills and ability to produce clear, evidence-based audit reports and compliance assessments.
Ability to independently evaluate complex compliance issues and appropriately escalate significant risks.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience supporting Phase 3 and late-stage pharmaceutical development.
Experience preparing for or supporting FDA BIMO and/or Pre-Approval Inspections (PAI).
Cross-functional auditing experience spanning GCP, GMP, GLP, and/or GVP.
Experience with clinical-stage organizations operating through outsourced CRO/CDMO models.
Experience developing or implementing formal inspection-readiness programs.
Lead Auditor certification, ASQ certification, RQAP, or comparable professional credential is desirable but not required.

The successful candidate should demonstrate strong auditor judgment and independence, exceptional attention to detail, regulatory and compliance acumen, concise technical writing, effective interviewing skills, and the ability to distinguish between isolated procedural deficiencies and systemic compliance risk. The individual must be comfortable challenging conclusions when warranted while maintaining productive working relationships with operational teams.

Primary Function
The Senior Human Factors Engineer works closely with designers, clinical engineers, and technical product managers to inform and guide the development of new products and ensure that those products are safe and easy to use. As part of new product development projects, they conduct user research, analyze and characterize use-related risks, and conduct usability testing of products prior to launch. They have primary responsibility for creating usability risk analyses and conducting final usability validation studies. The Senior Human Factors Engineer also works closely with the regulatory group to create the usability engineering documentation
required for submission to medical device regulatory agencies.
Roles & Responsibilities:
Collect and synthesize detailed information on how users interact with Intuitive products through various techniques including interviews, simulations, direct observations, task analyses, and persona development.
Present results of field observations, research, and usability testing.

Analyze complaints from on-market products and update usability risk assessment and escalate usability-related issues as necessary.
Design, execute, and report on usability (human factors) tests at various stages of product development from early prototypes all the way through formal FDA-mandated validation testing.
Write and execute usability test protocols. Analyze test data and write test reports.
Develop validation strategies for projects involving updates to existing products.
Lead the efforts required to create and update usability risk analyses for Intuitive products
Maintain traces between use risks, mitigations, and validation test cases.
Reinforce a human centered design approach across the organization.
Represent the Human Factors function on core teams for large projects.
Coordinate human factors efforts across projects involving several sub-systems.
Manage usability engineering activities within development projects and provide schedules and status to technical product managers and engineering project managers.
Mentor junior human factors engineers (e.g. interns) and others in organization in usability engineering methods and best practices, as well as Intuitive product development processes.
Prepare and review documentation for submission to regulatory agencies and notified bodies.
Answer questions and provide additional justification and rationale to any questions received.
Keep abreast of regulations and best practices for medical device human factors (e.g. IEC 62366, AAMI HE75, FDA Applying Human Factors and Usability Engineering to Medical Devices) and advise management regarding potential improvements to internal processes and regulatory issues related to usability engineering.

Skills, Experience, Education, & Training:
Minimum BS in Human Factors Engineering, Cognitive Psychology, Computer Science with human-computer interface (HCI) emphasis, Human Centered Design, or related field. MS strongly preferred.
Minimum 8+ years relevant Human Factors/Usability Engineering experience in hardware product development industry
Experience in medical device, or similar regulated industry, a significant plus
Ability to lead usability engineering activities (i.e. establishing usability requirements; creating usability risk analyses, test protocols, and test reports) for a complex, software-controlled electro-mechanical medical device
Ability to interface with customers in a highly professional manner
Ability to analyze and synthesize large quantities of information into usable communications
Superior ability to write accurate, clear, and concise protocols, reports, operating procedures, etc. in a timely manner
Excellent verbal communication and presentation skills
Ability to work with and across various groups and levels of management within the organization, including other engineering groups, marketing, clinical engineering, and regulatory. Excellent collaboration skills.
Ability to apply user-centered design and usability engineering principles to product research, development, and design
Ability to travel internationally as well as domestically (up to 25%)

It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful? Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at Intuitive . As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care , our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion —have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
Primary Function of Position
This role provides expert support for regulatory project management, strategic submissions, and cross-functional compliance activities in
global regulated markets for complex products.
Essential Job Duties
• Develop regulatory strategies for new product development and market entry.
• Advise cross-functional teams on global compliance requirements.
• Lead regulatory submissions, agency communications and strategy for the US and Canada for complex product approvals.
• Provide expert guidance in interpretation of international regulations.
• Represent regulatory affairs team in project meetings.
• Coordinate with OUS global regulatory teams for product registrations and variations.
• Review, approve, and update project documentation.
Required Experience and Education
• 8+ years of experience in regulatory affairs and bachelor’s degree in a relevant discipline, or equivalent combination of education
and experience.
Required Knowledge, Skills and Abilities
• Agency negotiation and strategic planning proficiency.
• Expertise in global regulatory requirements and registration processes.
• Advanced project leadership and communication skills.
• Technical documentation review and approval capabilities.
• Experience with audits, submissions, and training.

description:
It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful? Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at Intuitive . As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care , our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion —have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.

The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
Primary Function
The Advanced Product Development (APD) team is leveraging the cutting-edge technology of today to design and develop the surgical robotic systems of the future. Robotics Algorithms and Controls engineers (Systems Analysts) perform a central role in the design, development, and support of new products in the daVinci product line. They are responsible for developing the surgical teleoperation, motion control, and safety algorithms. This responsibility crosses into electrical, mechanical, software, control, user interface, and safety engineering. Systems Analysts strive to provide early design input, prove out new designs, and seek out solutions to challenging problems.
As a Systems Analyst, you will work with a small, multidisciplinary team of talented and dedicated engineers. This role demands in-depth collaboration with cross-functional teams, utilizing technical and interpersonal skills to develop a shared understanding of new product requirements. Systems Analysts maintain awareness and interest in developing research and technologies related to medical devices and safety-critical systems and actively apply this knowledge to system design.
Roles and Responsibilities:
Contribute to the development of new robotic systems through analysis and characterization.
Analyze complex electro-mechanical devices for dynamic safety and clinical risk.
Apply control theory to the design and verification of mechatronic and tele-robotic systems.
Integrate prototype hardware with existing systems.
Develop and implement motion control and safety algorithms, including documentation of risks, requirements, and test protocols.
Develop cartesian controls for manipulator robotics to design and implement precise and efficient robotic movements.
Participate in clinical observations and experiments to ensure that performance requirements are relevant and realistic.
Communicate system performance to the organization.
Support and track system performance as it evolves from design engineering to manufacturing.
Provide analytical assistance and tool building for other engineering issues.
Act as an interface between various technical specialties. Take ownership of issues that cross disciplinary boundaries and use a broad skillset to ensure the success of the project.
Document and communicate intellectual property.
Skill/Job Requirements:
Minimum MS degree in CS, ME, EE, or similar with 4–5+ years of industrial experience or PhD with 1–3+ years of experience.
Experience designing and implementing servo control systems.
Possess strong embedded development skills including intimate knowledge of C and modern C++.
Possess MATLAB and Python programming capabilities, as well as hardware and software integration skills.
Be detail-oriented and able to develop and drive a single solution to completion.
Comfort with concepts of design input, design output, traceability, and risk analysis.
Hands-on engineering experience with proven ability to work well in a team environment.
Self-motivated and proactive in engaging with interdisciplinary teams to address and solve complex problems.
A desire to deliver a quality and innovative product that will improve millions of people’s lives!

The Senior Software Engineer will design, build, and evolve key components of a modern, scalable Data-as-a-Service (DaaS) platform that supports Intuitive Digital products and serves more than 2,000 engineers across the organization. This role is responsible for independently delivering significant features and services within our real-time and micro-batch data pipelines that power product development, internal tools, and analytics. The engineer will make sound design decisions within their area, collaborate effectively across functions, and contribute to the reliability, performance, and usability of the platform at scale.
Major work will focus on developing high-throughput, low-latency data delivery through streaming pipelines, dynamic transformations, and APIs that enable application development, AI/ML, and actionable insights. You will help implement the architecture and engineering practices that support self-service analytics and operational decision-making.
Essential Job Duties
Design and build scalable distributed systems that leverage event-based and streaming data pipelines to handle ingestion and processing of robot, manufacturing, and clinical data
Develop self-service APIs and applications that enable users to access and interact with data
Partner with core engineering teams to evolve data models in response to changing business needs
Apply software development best practices — CI/CD, automated testing, infrastructure-as-code, and microservice architectures — in your day-to-day work
Actively participate in team planning, code reviews, KPI reviews, and design discussions, offering constructive input and driving decisions to closure within your area
Serve as a mentor to junior engineers and new team members, sharing knowledge and helping accelerate their ramp-up and growth
May lead moderately complex projects within the data domain, coordinating with cross-functional partners to deliver successful outcomes
Required Skills and Experience
Fluent coding in at least two major programming languages
Hands-on experience building data pipelines and working with distributed systems using technologies such as Apache Spark, Kafka, Elasticsearch, Snowflake, and Airflow
Working technical knowledge and experience with Data Platform components / design patterns:Event-Driven Pipelines (e.g. AWS Lambda)Message Queues (e.g. Kafka)Container Orchestration (e.g. Kubernetes)Stream Processing (e.g. Flink, Spark)Relational Databases (e.g. Postgres)Data Warehouses (e.g. Snowflake)Analytics Engineering (e.g. DBT)Workflow Orchestration (e.g. Airflow)Search Engines (e.g. Elasticsearch)
Solid understanding of CI/CD workflows, unit testing and integration testing, and deployment patterns
Experience with AWS and/or GCP
Experience with SQL and relational databases
Ability and enthusiasm to work collaboratively and cross-functionally, take ownership of your deliverables, and drive your own progress while knowing when to escalate
Required Education and Training
Solid quantitative background in Computer Science, Engineering, Physics, Math, or a related field. Minimum a bachelor's or master's degree in computer science, information technology, or a related field, with a typical minimum of 5 years of relevant experience.
Preferred Skills and Experience
Experience on a Platform team
Experience with Gitlab CI/CD or other CI tooling
Experience with Terraform, Ansible, Packer + general IaC best practices
Familiarity with CNCF projects and successful use of them in past projects

Lead technical assessments of supplier capabilities, manufacturing readiness, quality systems, and scalability
Drive design-for-manufacturability and design-for-supply-chain excellence throughout product development

Drive supplier selection, technical assessment, cost optimization, performance improvement, and manufacturing readiness for these technologies: Motor assemblies

Gearboxes
Brakes and actuation mechanisms
Bearings, rails, ball screws, and precision motion hardware
Printed circuit board assemblies (PCBAs)
Cable assemblies and interconnect systems
Precision machined components
Castings and forgings

Influence technical and business decisions without direct authority
Facilitate alignment among diverse stakeholders with competing priorities
Communicate effectively with collaborating teams

Proven ability in New Product Introduction
Outstanding analytical skills along with good judgment
Strong knowledge of GD&T required
Proficient in Six Sigma and Lean Manufacturing techniques
Proficient in pFMEA, process validation, route cause investigation, inspection, and test techniques

title: Sr. Electrical and Electronic Design Engineer - Future Forward
description:
It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful? Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at Intuitive. As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care, our technologies like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
Were a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
The Future Forward organization is Intuitive’s advanced concepts group. We explore emerging technologies, prototype next-generation solutions, and build software experiences that shape the future of robotic-assisted surgery.
If you're ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare, you'll find your purpose here.
The Future Forward group within Intuitive Surgical is searching for a Sr. Electrical and Electronic Design Engineer to architect, design, and bring up the electronic hardware behind next-generation robotic and vision systems. This role is an exciting opportunity to join a small and innovative team in the early phases of product development, where design decisions made at the schematic and architecture level shape the performance of the entire system.
Joining Intuitive Surgical means joining a team dedicated to using technology to benefit patients by improving surgical efficacy and decreasing surgical invasiveness, with patient outcomes as our highest priority. The Sr. Electrical and Electronic Design Engineer owns analog, digital, and mixed-signal circuit design from concept through schematic capture, layout direction, prototype bring-up, design verification, and transfer to manufacturing. The ideal candidate designs for electromagnetic compatibility and signal integrity from the first block diagram rather than after the first chamber failure, and can isolate the most difficult board-level and system-level failures on the bench. A strong sense of integrity, care, and attention to detail is required, together with a commitment to developing products of the highest quality.
Roles and Responsibilities:
Design analog, digital, and mixed-signal circuits from concept through schematic capture, layout direction, prototype bring-up, and transfer to manufacturing.
Lead schematic and design reviews, and guide PCB layout for signal integrity, power integrity, and manufacturability.
Design for EMC and EMI from the start through grounding, shielding, filtering, isolation, and ESD protection, and support pre-compliance and compliance testing.
Bring up and debug prototypes in the lab, and drive hardware issues to root cause and a verified fix.
Integrate sensors, cameras, illumination, motor drives, and compute platforms in partnership with Mechanical, Firmware, Software, Vision, and Test teams.
Document designs, verification protocols, and results under Intuitive design controls.
Mentor engineers and help shape design practices, reference designs, and the technology roadmap for future products.
Drive external suppliers and design partners for camera, sensor, optics, and PCBA subsystems, setting technical direction and holding builds to schedule and quality targets.
Skills/Job Requirements:
Minimum 8 years' experience designing production electronics in the medical device, automotive, or robotics industry, including at least one product taken from concept to production.
Bachelor of Science degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Computer Engineering, or Computer Science; a Master of Science degree preferred.
Strong schematic design, review, and debug skills across analog, digital, and mixed-signal circuits, using Altium Designer, Cadence OrCAD/Allegro, or Siemens Xpedition.
Practical EMC and EMI design and troubleshooting experience, with working knowledge of standards such as IEC 60601-1-2, CISPR 11/32, or the IEC 61000-4 immunity series.
Solid signal integrity and power integrity fundamentals for high-speed interfaces such as MIPI CSI-2, LVDS, PCIe, USB, DDR, or Ethernet, including impedance control, return paths, crosstalk, and decoupling.
Direct experience with imaging and vision hardware, motor drive electronics, or precision sensing, and with transferring designs into manufacturing and production test.
Confident in the lab with oscilloscopes, spectrum analyzers, near-field probes, and logic or protocol analyzers, working with embedded interfaces such as I2C, SPI, UART, CAN, USB, and Ethernet, and using Python or MATLAB for test automation and data analysis.
Experience under a regulated quality system such as ISO 13485, FDA 21 CFR Part 820, IEC 60601-1, and ISO 14971, or automotive functional safety such as ISO 26262, is desired; FPGA design experience with VHDL or SystemVerilog is a plus.
Clear communication, strong documentation habits, and the ability to lead technical decisions, work independently, and mentor others.

If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
About the Team
Future Forward Research — Synthetic Data, builds the simulation and data infrastructure that powers Intuitive's autonomous surgical capabilities.
The Role
You'll build the virtual surgical worlds and the data pipelines that train our perception and policy models. Day to day, that means designing simulation environments, generating large volumes of labeled synthetic data, and working with ML engineers to close the sim-to-real gap for robotic surgery. It's a hands-on engineering role at the intersection of 3D simulation, machine learning, and robotics.
What You'll Do
Design and build high-fidelity simulation environments for surgical tasks.
Generate scalable synthetic datasets including photo realistic imagery, segmentation masks, depth, optical flow, and kinematic state — and own their quality, versioning, and delivery.
Implement domain randomization and procedural scene generation to maximize sim-to-real transfer.
Model deformable soft-tissue physics, tool-tissue contact, and instrument kinematics that match Intuitive's platforms.
Partner with ML engineers to define task curricula, reward functions, and evaluation benchmarks.
Develop and refine sim-to-real transfer strategies, and validate simulated behaviors against benchtop phantoms and real systems.
Build reusable tools, APIs, and documentation so the broader team can spin up new tasks without deep simulation expertise.
What You Bring
We care more about real depth in a few of these than shallow coverage of all of them.
Strong software engineering. You write maintainable, tested code in Python, C++ and/or C#, and you're comfortable in a Linux / Git / Docker / GPU workflow.
Hands-on simulation or graphics experience. You've built things in a physics simulator, game engine, or rendering/VFX pipeline — robotics simulators, real-time engines, and offline graphics pipelines all count.
A feel for data and models. You've produced data that trained an ML model (or worked closely alongside that), and you understand how data quality and distribution show up in model behavior.
Working knowledge of 3D and physics fundamentals — coordinate frames, rendering, rigid-body and contact dynamics — enough to reason about why a simulated scene does or doesn't look and behave correctly.
You've likely spent several years building games, simulation, graphics, robotics, or data systems — but we're far more interested in what you've built than in a specific number on your résumé. The Senior Software Engineering Manager will lead a team of software engineers building the network connectivity software that powers Intuitive’s flagship surgical robotic platforms and its next-generation surgical robotics line. Hands-on experience with cloud service (e.g. AWS, GCP, Azure) supporting connected embedded devices.
Experience with medical device cybersecurity practices (e.g., threat modeling, secure communications, vulnerability management) consistent with FDA premarket cybersecurity guidance.
Experience working in an agile development environment.
Excellent communication skills with the ability to collaborate across departments.
Proficiency in written and verbal communication.
Comfort with presenting to large or small groups.

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field; Master’s degree preferred.
10+ years of experience in software engineering with at least 3 years in a leadership or management role.

Experience with all phases of the product development lifecycle (design, implementation, debug, verification, validation, and transfer to manufacturing/service).
Experience with designing software products in an FDA or other regulated industry or for mission critical applications.
Experience with MQTT or other event-driven/pub-sub messaging protocols for IoT telemetry at fleet scale.
Experience with CI/CD pipelines and DevOps practices.

title: Manager, Ingredients - Cheese & Dairy (Canada)
location: Chicago/Aon Center, Illinois, United States of America
description:
Role purpose. The Manager, Canada Cheese & Dairy will lead the procurement strategy and commercial management for the full Canadian Business Unit portfolio of Cheese, Dairy Powders, Cheese Powders and Cream Mix. The role is accountable for category value delivery, supplier strategy, supply continuity, cost competitiveness, cross-border compliance and cross-functional execution across maintenance, productivity and innovation workstreams. The Manager will connect the Canadian Business Unit with North American category experts, translate market and business requirements into a Canada-specific sourcing strategy, and ensure clear information flow between Procurement and Canadian Business Unit leadership. Job Description
Primary Responsibilities:
Strategic Sourcing & Commercial Management • Own and execute end-to-end sourcing strategies for the Canadian Cheese and Dairy portfolio, including market analysis, supplier segmentation, sourcing events, negotiations, contracting, implementation and ongoing commercial governance. • Develop and maintain a multi-year Canada sourcing strategy aligned with North American category strategies while reflecting Canadian market dynamics, business priorities, regulatory requirements and supply-chain constraints. • Partner closely with North American category experts to leverage market intelligence, supplier relationships, sourcing scale and best practices, while maintaining clear accountability for Canadian Business Unit outcomes. • Lead complex and high-value negotiations, supplier award recommendations and contracting, ensuring appropriate cost, service, quality, capacity, flexibility and risk protections. • Develop and communicate a strong point of view on Canadian and North American cheese and dairy markets, including commodity drivers, manufacturing economics, capacity, trade flows, tariffs and regional supply-demand dynamics. • Ensure pricing, contracts, specifications, supplier records and sourcing decisions are accurate, current and compliant within relevant source-to-pay and business systems.
Canada Cheese & Dairy Portfolio Responsibilities • Lead procurement for Cheese, Dairy Powders, Cheese Powders and Cream Mix across the Canadian Business Unit, balancing cost, functionality, specification, service and supply requirements. • Provide portfolio-level governance across maintenance, productivity, innovation, reformulation, promotions, plant transitions, capacity changes and new business opportunities. • Partner with R&D, Quality, Manufacturing, Commercial, Finance, Materials Management and the Canadian Business Unit to define requirements, technical specifications, project economics and implementation timing. • Lead supplier and procurement readiness for innovations, renovations, reformulations, promotions, plant transitions, product maintenance and business continuity initiatives. • Assess and manage category complexity, including product specifications, lead times, minimum order quantities, yields, conversion economics, supplier capacity and cross-border supply lanes. • Build and maintain contingency strategies for critical materials, suppliers, manufacturing locations and logistics routes serving Canada.
Cross-Border, Quota, Tariff & CDC Managemen t • Own procurement coordination for cross-border cheese and dairy flows into and out of Canada, ensuring commercial plans reflect applicable quotas, tariffs, customs requirements and regulatory obligations. • Lead procurement management of Canadian Dairy Commission (CDC) requirements and related processes, working with internal and external experts to support compliant and cost-effective execution. • Monitor quota availability, tariff exposure and cross-border cost implications, incorporating these factors into sourcing decisions, budgets, supplier negotiations and risk assessments. • Coordinate with Trade Compliance, Legal, Finance, Logistics, customs brokers, suppliers and category experts to resolve cross-border issues and maintain continuity of supply. • Maintain clear governance, documentation and escalation paths for quota, tariff and CDC activities affecting the Canadian portfolio.

title: Processor 1
location: HPC - Jacksonville Factory, Florida, United States of America
description:
Job Purpose
To ensure we are supplying customers with the highest quality products while adhering to all food and safety standards. This is accomplished by batching food product/condiments to corporate/customer approved recipes.
Essential Functions & Responsibilities
• Obtains instruction from lead processor or supervisor.
• Ability to follow complete production schedules with minimal scrap/spoilage
• Keep up with volume of work required
• Visually inspects equipment at station for cleanliness or obvious maintenance problems.
• Cleans small machine components, as needed.
• Reports any problems to lead processor or supervisor.
• Makes piping connections as needed for particular process on schedule.
• Monitors equipment controls, temperature meters, valves and adjusts as needed.
• Operates forklift/pallet jack to obtain ingredients or move pallets/totes in and around processing area.
• While slow, assists processing assistants in cleaning processing areas by scrubbing walls, hosing floor, sweeping floor/emptying trash and performing other cleaning duties.
• Utilizes can openers, knives, band cutters, snips, pliers and other small items to open ingredient cases/packages.
• Maintains neat work area. Wipes spills that have occurred during mixing process.
• Records data pertaining to work completed, ingredients used, lot codes and other processing information.
• Assists in cleaning equipment and lines between recipes.
• Very occasionally obtains ingredients/supplies from warehouse.
• Obtains samples of batches and taste test.
• Asks lead, supervisor or material handler if there is any rework.
• Uses rework if there is any consistently.
• Determines ingredients required for formula/recipe and the required amount.
• Ability to safely lift 50lbs on a regular basis.
• Obtains ingredients from storage area or around work area and pours into kettle.
• Meters in other ingredients as required by watching meters and turning on/off kettle.
• Utilizes drum lift by strapping drum into lift and operating hydraulic lift with chain.
• Manually pushes drum lift to kettle and dumps drum of ingredients as needed.
• Operates controls to activate mixers and equipment.
• Monitors controls, equipment temperature, valves, and adjusts equipment to meet formula requirements.
• Hoses spills off floor and hoses towards drains.
• Obtains, measures and weighs additional ingredients to set aside in preparation for next batch or recipe.
• Assists other processors in pouring ingredients into kettles as needed.
• Collects samples and tests for pH, acidity, viscosity and solids.
• Reads test results and adjusts equipment/recipe accordingly.
• Notifies lead processor of any major adjustments needed, or problems with process.
• Transfers finished products to drum, tote, or tank by pumping through piping system.
• Operates switches to control pumps when batch is complete.
• Assists in preparing drums, totes, or tanks for storage of product by ensuring that the proper placarding information is on the package.
• Determines appropriate size of batch needed to accommodate orders and line.
• Closely monitors batch temperature while processing and waiting for packaging to ensure that product will not set prematurely.
• Operates equipment in a safe manner following GMP guidelines and keeps work area clean.
• Supports the Jacksonville plant FSQ and QRMP initiatives on any and all procedures/programs pertaining to product safety.
• Participates in meetings and have scheduling flexibility.
• Trains others as necessary.
• Fills in for other positions as necessary.
• Occasionally testing batches in the lab and recording information on proper documentation.
• Additional responsibilities of this position include assisting in the creation of a culture of safety and health by performing work safely in accordance with all company safety procedures.
• Operates equipment safely and reports any unsafe work conditions or practice to supervisor. Occupational safety and health performance is measured in this position
• Other duties as assigned

title: Production Supervisor
location: Jacksonville Plant, Florida, United States of America
description:
The Production Supervisor is a member of the plant leadership team and is responsible for day-to-day manufacturing operations within an assigned area and shift under the direction of the Business Unit Manager. This role provides leadership to deliver business results and operational improvements while achieving productivity, efficiency, customer service, cost, quality, safety, and employee engagement objectives through individual and team contributions.
Key Responsibilities
Manage day-to-day manufacturing operations for the assigned area and shift to meet productivity, efficiency, customer service, cost, quality, safety, and employee engagement objectives.
Provide direction, leadership, development, and support to direct reports through empowerment, teamwork, on-the-job assignments, and continuous improvement projects and initiatives.
Develop, implement, and promote safety programs and safe work practices through participation in plant safety teams, programs, and initiatives.
Promote sound employee and labor relations within the department by developing and maintaining an effective organization with qualified personnel.
Develop, promote, and support continuous improvement efforts and cross-functional initiatives that deliver business results and operational improvements.
Additional Responsibilities
Shift execution: Translate production priorities into daily assignments, communicate expectations, and coordinate staffing, materials, and equipment readiness to support the production schedule.
Operational results: Monitor production output, downtime, waste, yield, and labor utilization. Identify deviations, communicate barriers, and coordinate corrective actions with appropriate support teams.
Safety leadership: Reinforce established safety procedures, personal protective equipment requirements, housekeeping standards, and hazard reporting. Escalate unsafe conditions and support incident reviews and corrective-action follow-through.
Food safety and quality: Partner with Quality and Food Safety personnel to reinforce good manufacturing practices, sanitation requirements, product specifications, and required production checks. Escalate deviations and follow established product hold and disposition procedures.
Cross-functional coordination: Work with Maintenance, Sanitation, Planning, and Warehouse teams to address equipment concerns, changeovers, material availability, and other issues affecting safe and reliable production.
Training and development: Identify training needs, coordinate onboarding and cross-training, reinforce standard work, and maintain required training documentation. Provide clear instructions and timely coaching to support employee development.
Employee communication: Conduct shift meetings, communicate operational updates, recognize team contributions, and promptly elevate employee concerns to the appropriate leader or Human Resources.
Labor relations: Partner with Human Resources and plant leadership to apply established policies and applicable collective bargaining agreement provisions consistently when coordinating assignments, staffing, and employee matters.
Continuous improvement: Use production data and team input to identify recurring losses, support root-cause analysis, implement approved improvements, and confirm that corrective actions are sustained.
Documentation and handoffs: Maintain accurate production records and shift reports. Communicate equipment status, unresolved issues, quality concerns, staffing needs, and follow-up actions to the incoming shift.
Qualifications:
BA/BS Degree in Business, Food Science, Engineering or related field is preferred
1-5 years of experience in a manufacturing environment is required
Ability to lead, motivate and mentor large teams of hourly associates is required
Strong communication and leadership skills
Strong analytical/critical thinking
Strong accountability, consistency and follow-through skills
Ability to work effectively with a wide array of plant personnel ranging from hourly employees to senior management
