description:
Job Description
As a Sr. Scientist within the Process Technology group in R&D Central Processing you will serve as a technical processing expert responsible for exploring and developing new process technologies, building our internal processing capabilities, and hands-on execution of complex, high-impact processing projects from concept through commercialization. You will own the technical delivery of assigned initiatives, partnering closely with cross-functional stakeholders to translate processing concepts into manufacturable, Right-First-Time solutions.​
Essential Functions & Responsibilities
​​Identify, evaluate, and prioritize emerging process technologies (equipment, automation, digital, etc) aligned to business needs.
​Develop scale up strategies from prototyping to pilot plant, and right the first time commercialization to drive optimal project execution.
​Execute end-to-end technical delivery across assigned complex processing projects, including technical briefing, concept development, technical design, learning plans, pilot runs, capital design, and commercialization handover to Operations/Supply Chain.
​Develop and maintain detailed technical documentation including Manufacturing Procedure Specifications, Transformation Flowsheets, and Process Design Scopes, ensuring processing parameters meet defined quality, shelf-life, consumer experience, and manufacturing performance requirements.
​Apply processing commercialization tools (CQV, FMEA, CPRA) to systematically identify and mitigate technical risks, drive design decisions, and ensure Right-First-Time launch readiness.
​Partner with Platform R&D, GDI R&D, Packaging R&D, Quality, Operations, and external suppliers to define processing requirements and success criteria, resolve technical trade-offs, and maintain project timelines and milestones.
​Lead and support pilot line trials and scale-up activities, translating learnings into robust commercial processing solutions.
​Contribute to STAR and Tech Review Board processes, preparing and presenting technical content that clearly communicates design rationale, risk status, and commercialization readiness.
​Maintain compliance with all regulatory and safety requirements throughout project execution.
​Support cost optimization and value engineering efforts that improve margin, sustainability, and reinvestment priorities.
​Serve as an informal technical mentor to junior processing engineers on the team, sharing applied expertise and supporting capability development.​
Key Outputs & Deliverables
Deliver successful technical execution across concurrent complex processing projects within innovation and platform portfolios, meeting committed timelines, budgets, and technical performance targets.
Achieve and sustain >95% Right-First-Time (RTF) launches across assigned projects, ensuring processing solutions meet manufacturability, quality, regulatory, and supply chain readiness criteria at first commercial production.
Produce high-quality processing technical deliverables — including Manufacturing Procedure Specifications, Transformation Flowsheets, Process Design Scopes, FMEAs, and CQV documentation — that meet enterprise engineering standards.
Generate clear, data-driven technical recommendations and risk assessments that enable informed go/no-go decisions at governance milestones.
Contribute to team capability by sharing technical learnings, best practices, and processing expertise across the broader E2E projects organization.
Expected Experience & Required Skills
​​BS/MS/PhD degree in Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or related discipline.
​Minimum 4 years of experience in R&D or Engineering roles within consumer goods, food & beverage, pharma, or a similar industry.
​Demonstrated experience in emulsions / shear processing, fermentation, extrusion, thermal processing & validation, aeration, drying, or powder mixing preferred.

title: Finance Business Partner
description:
Job Description:
Position Summary
The Finance Engineering Manager serves as the primary finance business partner to the Engineering organization, providing financial leadership and governance across the capital investment portfolio. This role is responsible for ensuring capital projects are appropriately evaluated, validated, approved, and executed in alignment with approved business cases and company financial objectives.
The Finance Engineering Manager supports Site Finance Managers through advanced analytics, factory benchmarking, and value realization processes that drive operational performance and network productivity improvements. The role serves as a key link between Engineering, Operations, and Finance to ensure investments and improvement initiatives deliver sustainable business results.
Key Responsibilities
Capital Project Financial Governance
Partner with Engineering teams to evaluate, validate, and prioritize capital investment opportunities.
Develop, review, and challenge project business cases to ensure financial assumptions, risks, and expected returns are robust and well supported.
Ensure capital expenditure requests comply with company financial policies, approval requirements, and investment criteria.
Support the capital authorization and approval process, providing financial recommendations to leadership.
Monitor project execution against approved scope, budget, timelines, and financial commitments.
Project Performance Tracking & Analysis
Track capital project actual spending against approved budgets and forecasts.
Identify and communicate project variances, financial risks, and opportunities throughout project execution.
Establish reporting and governance processes to monitor project performance across the capital portfolio.
Analyze project outcomes and conduct post-implementation reviews to ensure expected benefits and returns are realized.
Site Finance Partnership & Factory Performance Leadership
Partner with Site Finance Managers to provide financial insights, analytics, and benchmarking that drive factory performance improvements across the manufacturing network.
Develop and maintain standardized performance metrics, productivity & spending reporting and operational KPI analysis to support decision-making at the site and network levels.
Develop and analyze site-level depreciation modeling, including Asset Under Construction data, to develop affordability targets and scenario planning.
Analyze manufacturing performance trends, including cost, productivity, labor, efficiency, waste, and throughput, identifying opportunities to improve financial and operational results.
Support Site Finance Managers in evaluating the financial impact of operational initiatives, productivity programs, and continuous improvement efforts.
Provide data-driven insights to help factories identify performance gaps and prioritize improvement opportunities.
Collaborate with Site Finance and Operations leaders to track and validate value realization from productivity and operational improvement initiatives.
Drive consistency in performance measurement, reporting methodologies, and value tracking across the manufacturing network.
Continuous Improvement
Partner with engineering and operational leaders to identify opportunities for improved capital efficiency and investment returns.
Benchmark project performance, investment metrics, and financial outcomes across manufacturing facilities.
Share best practices and lessons learned to improve future project selection, execution, and value realization.
Strategic Business Partnership
Act as a trusted advisor to Engineering leadership on capital allocation, investment strategy, and portfolio management.
Support long-term manufacturing and engineering strategies through financial analysis and scenario modeling.
Provide insights and recommendations to senior leadership regarding capital deployment and resource prioritization.
Foster strong cross-functional relationships among Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, and Finance teams.
Qualifications
Education
Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Engineering, or related field required.
MBA, CPA, CMA, or other relevant professional certification preferred.
Experience
7+ years of progressive experience in Finance, FP&A, Manufacturing Finance, Capital Management, or Engineering Finance.
Experience supporting engineering, manufacturing, operations, or supply chain organizations.
Strong understanding of capital investment analysis, project governance, and financial modeling.
Experience managing large capital portfolios and cross-functional projects preferred.
Knowledge, Skills, & Abilities
Strong financial modeling and investment analysis capabilities, including NPV, IRR, payback, and ROI methodologies.
Knowledge of manufacturing operations and capital project management processes.
Ability to influence decision-making across multiple levels of the organization.
Excellent analytical, communication, and presentation skills.
Strong project management and organizational abilities.
Ability to translate complex financial concepts into actionable business recommendations.
Advanced proficiency in financial systems, ERP platforms, and Microsoft Office applications.
Success Measures
Success in this role will be measured by:
Capital projects delivered within approved budgets and business case expectations.
Accuracy of project forecasts and financial tracking.
Achievement and validation of approved project savings and productivity targets.
Consistency of capital project valuation methodologies across the network.
Improved capital efficiency and return on investment.
Effective partnership and support of Engineering and Site Finance teams.
Timely identification and mitigation of project financial risks.
This role plays a critical part in ensuring the company's capital investments create sustainable value and support long-term manufacturing excellence.

Job Opportunity: Grinding Utility (Military & Veteran Friendly)
Shift: Nights (6pm - 6:30am) 223 Schedule

About Us
Royal Canin is seeking a Grinding Utility to join our exciting pet food business at our Fremont, NE manufacturing plant. We focus on the unique needs of cats and dogs. Our obsession with detail allows us to deliver precise, effective nutrition and help them become their magnificent best.
As part of our overall total compensation package, Royal Canin offers a competitive benefits package to all associates: Medical, Dental, Vision & Life Insurance, Short- & Long-Term Disability, and 401k match. Role Purpose & Military Value
The Grinding Utility role functions as a member of an area team that is directly responsible for the efficient production of quality products in the required quantities. This is a high-autonomy, leadership-oriented role where you will operate/change over specified machinery, coordinate shifts, and manage daily crewing needs—frequently without direct supervision.
We highly value the leadership, technical troubleshooting, shift coordination, and peer-training skills of military Non-Commissioned Officers (NCOs), Petty Officers, and technical specialists. If you have experience managing watch bills, crew assignments, equipment maintenance, or training junior service members, your skills are directly transferable here.
Key Responsibilities
Autonomous Leadership: Provide operational leadership and shift coordination for full shifts or multiple process areas, often without a production supervisor assigned (analogous to Tactical Operations/Watch Standing).
Crewing & Scheduling: Address daily crewing needs and shift schedule changes for optimized operation using planning skills and Staffing Tools (analogous to managing Watch Bills, Duty Rosters, or Section Staffing).
Production & Efficiency: Meet or exceed plant productivity goals by directing operational needs, staffing, and inventories.
Equipment Operation & Troubleshooting: Safely and efficiently operate pet food manufacturing equipment. Monitor production lines, identify faults, and immediately escalate complex downtime to Maintenance or QA.
Resource Coordination: Facilitate clear communication and planning with other leads/operators to ensure seamless shift changeovers, minimize downtime, manage waste, and ensure all ingredients and supplies are prepared.
On-the-Job Training: Conduct structured training and peer guidance for new associates on safety requirements, technical equipment operation, quality systems, and sanitation (analogous to Unit/Section Training and Certification).
Conflict Resolution & Team Building: Successfully resolve operational challenges and conflicts by listening, sharing information, and fostering a high-performing, positive team climate.
Reporting: Ensure all process logs, quality reports, and shift documentation are completed accurately, legibly, and on time.
Physical Requirements & Working Environment
Standing on a concrete floor for extended periods.
Wearing proper personal protective equipment (PPE) at all times (hair net, bump cap, ear plugs, safety shoes, and uniform).
Bending, stooping, twisting, turning, reaching, climbing stairs, and regularly lifting up to 55 lbs.
Adaptability to environmental and temperature extremes (hot/cold climates, dust, dirt, and food-safe chemicals).
Vision correctable to 20/20.
Qualifications & Experience
Minimum Requirements:
Be 18 years of age or older.
Have a High school diploma, GED, or equivalent.
Must be willing and able to work and accept varying shifts and schedules (night shift focus).
Ability to understand and effectively communicate in the English language.
Preferred Skills & Experience (Civilian or Military Equivalent):
Machine Operation: 1 year of experience operating machinery or managing technical systems (e.g., motor pool, aviation support, electrical/mechanical systems).
Technical Discipline: 1 year of experience in manufacturing, mechanical repair, trade discipline, or tactical equipment maintenance.

Equipment Certification: Ability to operate (or learn to operate) a Forklift and Scissor Lift.
Computer Literacy: Competency in computer and PC software (MS Office, email, spreadsheets).

Work with over 130,000 like-minded and talented Associates, all guided by The Five Principles.

Supply Administration & Logistics (3043, 3051): Highly transferable strengths in tracking control systems, warehouse logistics, safety standards, and stock distribution.

Effective Control and mitigation of occupational health risks globally.
Robust Clinical Governance and 100% regulatory compliance across all operating regions.
High-Quality Service Delivery from regional teams and external providers, leading to a safer, healthier, and more resilient workforce.

Job Description:
The Learning Business Partner acts as a strategic co-pilot and advisor to senior business leaders, driving organizational performance by translating complex business strategies into sustainable capability architectures.
This role owns the end-to-end learning value chain—from strategic business relationship management and performance consulting to learning needs analysis, high-level learning solution design, and evaluation. This role creates high-impact capability strategies and designs holistic learning experiences that seamlessly integrate into the daily flow of work, directly enabling business growth and Associate skill building
Key Responsibilities
1. Performance Consulting & Stakeholder Relationship Management (Consulting & Influence)
·         Strategic Business Partnership: Act as the primary interface and trusted advisor to stakeholders. Proactively manage senior stakeholder relationships, establishing credibility to influence decision-making and champion the enterprise learning agenda.
·         Performance Diagnostics: Use advanced performance consulting methodologies to diagnose organizational performance challenges. Conduct root-cause analyses to distinguish between training opportunities and other organizational, process, or talent-related interventions.
·         Demand & Portfolio Management: Effectively manage and prioritize the pipeline of learning requests. Act as a strategic gateway, aligning proposed learning solutions with key business priorities and long-term talent strategies.
2. Learning Needs Analysis & Capability Architecture (Skills & Learning Strategy)
·         Diagnostic Skills Assessment: Apply quantitative and qualitative research methodologies (surveys, data benchmarks, focus groups, interviews) to map existing skills inventories, isolate skill gaps, and define the critical capabilities required for future-readiness.
·         Capability & Skills Architecture: Design and maintain agile skills matrices and capability frameworks aligned with business strategies. Define current versus ideal performance states and design scalable learning pathways to close the gap.
·         Enterprise Synergy: Collaborate across functional domains to identify horizontal capability trends, scaling successful learning models and preventing fragmented, redundant initiatives.
3. Holistic Learning Solution Design (Design & Orchestration)
·         High-Level Solution Design: Map human-centered learner journeys and establish robust instructional design frameworks. Architect multi-faceted learning ecosystems that integrate formal, social, and experiential (70/20/10) learning components.
·         Modality & Technology Selection: Evaluate and select optimal delivery formats (digital self-paced, synchronous virtual, classroom, social learning networks, or workflow-embedded tools) that maximize engagement and drive behavioral change.
·         ID Partnering & Quality Assurance: Define and document high-level design specifications and standards for external and internal Instructional Design (ID) partners. Collaborate closely during the build phase, maintaining accountability for the overall design integrity, context alignment, and deployment success.
4. Data Literacy, Measurement, and Impact (Analytics & Valuation)
·         Success Metrics Definition: Define key performance indicators (KPIs) and business impact metrics at the outset of every initiative in collaboration with business sponsors.
·         Measurement & Evaluation: Apply robust evaluation frameworks (e.g., LTEM, Kirkpatrick) to monitor learner engagement, behavior change, and business ROI.
·         Insights-Driven Optimization: Analyze data to derive insights, communicate the strategic value of learning to executive leadership, and continuously optimize the portfolio.
Context and Scope
The Learning Business Partner operates in a fast-paced, highly matrixed, global environment. The role holder must successfully navigate complex stakeholder landscapes across global segments, cultures, and time zones.
The role operates at the critical intersection of business leaders and centralized learning execution teams. Rather than producing raw training content, the Learning Business Partner owns the "What" and "Why “defining the strategic learning agenda and designing the learner experience—while steering the "How" in partnership with Instructional Designers and vendors. The position requires a high degree of autonomy, executive presence, and the ability to influence without authority.
Job Specifications / Qualifications
Education & Professional Qualifications
·         Minimum Experience: 8+ years of progressive experience in Learning & Development
·         Global Readiness: Demonstrated capability to operate effectively across diverse geographical regions and cultures. Regular availability to support US/European time zones is required.
·         Travel: Ability to travel up to 10% of the time for key stakeholder alignment meetings and learning forums.
Key Knowledge & Experience
·         Consulting & Influence: Masterful ability to conduct diagnostics, build trusted-advisor relationships, manage expectation mismatches, and influence VP/Director-level stakeholders.
·         Business & Functional Acumen: Deep understanding of corporate structures and business value chains (Sales, Supply, R&D, Finance, P&O, etc.) with the ability to speak the language of business leaders.
·         Digital Fluency & AI Capability: Savviness in utilizing modern learning technology stacks (LMS, LXP, social learning environments) and emerging AI capabilities for automated curation, skill taxonomy tagging, and personalized learning journeys.
·         Data Literacy: Proven experience defining data collection methodologies, reading dashboards, interpreting learner analytics, and synthesizing data points into executive-level narratives.
·         Adult Learning Strategy: Expert-level knowledge of adult learning theories, cognitive design principles, behavioral economics/change management, and 70/20/10 operationalization.
Competency Profile
Key Mars Leadership Competencies
·         Strategic Mindset: Sees ahead to future possibilities and translates them into breakthrough strategies.
·         Balances Stakeholders: Anticipates and balances the needs of multiple stakeholders across a matrix.
·         Collaborates: Builds partnerships and works collaboratively with others to meet shared objectives.
·         Manages Ambiguity: Operates effectively, even when things are not certain or the way forward is unclear.
·         Nimble Learning: Learns quickly when facing new situations, experimenting to find solutions.

description:
Job Description:
Job: Material Handler
Segment: Mars Petcare (Greenies)
Location: North Kansas City, MO
Shift: Day Shift (6:00 AM – 6:30 PM)
Job Type: Full-Time, Permanent
Join Our Greenies Team in North Kansas City
At Mars Petcare, we are passionate about pets. Our Greenies brand is dedicated to keeping pets healthy and happy, and we manufacture our world-renowned products right here in our highly desirable, fully climate-controlled North Kansas City facility.
Being a Mars Associate is all about opportunity. The opportunity to do the kind of challenging, interesting work that shapes the world’s best-loved brands. To work with real purpose, supported by talented, friendly people from all sorts of different backgrounds.
Whether you are an experienced warehouse professional, a skilled forklift operator looking for a stable day-shift position, or a transitioning military Veteran, Reservist, or National Guard member, we welcome your unique talents! We highly value the dedication, safety-first mindset, and structured teamwork developed in the military and look forward to helping you build a successful civilian career.
Job Summary
The Material Handler is responsible for the end-to-end logistics flow within our plant. This dual-focus role handles all incoming packaging and raw ingredients, manages safe product movement inside the site, loads outbound trailers for shipment, completes all logistics paperwork, and maintains perfect inventory control. This associate works closely with production, purchasing, receiving, shipping, and quality teams to ensure seamless plant operations in a clean, temperature-controlled environment.
Key Responsibilities
Receiving & Inbound Logistics
Receive and verify all incoming raw materials, ingredients, packaging, and components against purchase orders and shipping manifests.
Use a forklift to safely unload inbound trucks and transfer materials to their correct designated storage locations.
Conduct strict quality and food safety checks on incoming materials, including collecting product samples and verifying supplier paperwork.
Collaborate with external logistics departments and freight carriers to ensure correct and safe delivery of production materials.
Material Handling & Warehouse Operations
Safely and accurately operate material handling equipment (including forklifts) to transport inventory, raw materials, WIP (work-in-process), and finished goods throughout the facility.
Support production schedules by ensuring that the correct materials are issued and staged in production areas when needed.
Stage, build, and load outbound trailers for shipment, ensuring proper cargo weight distribution and trailer utilization.
Ensure proper labeling, sorting, FIFO (First-In, First-Out) rotation, and general organization of all materials in storage areas.
Inventory, Systems, & Documentation
Scan and track material movements using warehouse management systems to ensure perfect real-time inventory accountability.
Perform daily cycle counts, participate in precision monthly inventories, and assist with formal physical audits.
Investigate inventory discrepancies promptly and report findings to management.
Generate, review, and complete accurate shipping/receiving paperwork, logging all transactions accurately into the plant database.
Safety, Quality, & Food Safety Culture
Participate and adhere to all food safety requirements, Quality Management Processes (QMPs), and site safety programs, championing a safety-first culture.
Maintain a clean, organized, and sanitary warehouse environment in accordance with Good Manufacturing Practices (GMPs).
Promptly report any safety, food safety, or quality concerns to leadership.
Position Requirements
Minimum Qualifications:
Education: High school diploma, GED, or equivalent civilian/military education.
Experience: Proven experience in warehouse logistics, receiving, shipping, or material handling roles.
Equipment: Demonstrated experience operating a forklift safely in an industrial or warehouse environment.
Physical Ability: Must be in good physical condition with the ability to stand and walk for extended periods, bend, reach, climb, and safely lift up to 40 pounds manually.
Technical Literacy: Working knowledge of basic computer programs for entering data, record keeping, and maintaining inventory logs.
Core Skills: Basic math skills, a keen eye for detail, strong organizational skills, and excellent written and verbal communication abilities.
Teamwork: Demonstrated ability to work in a high-performing team environment with a willingness to learn and be coached.
Military & Veteran Technical Equivalency Guide
At Mars, we recognize that your military service has prepared you to excel in logistical operations. Your training in high-stakes material movement, precision inventory tracking, and supply chain management maps directly to this role. If you served in any of the following specialties, we highly encourage you to apply:
U.S. Army: Automated Logistical Specialist (92A), Unit Supply Specialist (92Y), Cargo Specialist (88H), Motor Transport Operator (88M), Ammunition Specialist (89B). Your experience with warehouse databases, material handling equipment (MHE), and precise property book audits is an excellent fit.
U.S. Navy: Logistics Specialist (LS), Storekeeper, Aviation Storekeeper (AK). Your experience managing inventory, shipboard supply warehouses, and processing shipping manifests maps directly to our material tracking systems.
U.S. Air Force: Materiel Management (2S0X1), Traffic Management (2T0X1), Ground Transportation (2T1X1). Your training in cargo loading, receiving inspections, strict compliance with safety procedures, and inventory precision is an exact match.
U.S. Marine Corps: Warehouse Clerk (3051), Supply Administration & Operations (3043), Logistics/Embarkation Specialist (0431), Motor Vehicle Operator (3531). Your focus on cargo staging, load planning, and material handling equipment matches our shipping and receiving operations.
U.S. Coast Guard: Storekeeper (SK), Marine Science Technician.
What We Offer (Total Rewards & Benefits)
At Mars, being an associate is more than a job—it's an opportunity to build a long-term career. We provide a competitive, industry-leading package starting on your very first day:
Compensation: Competitive base pay based on experience, shift differentials, and significant overtime (OT) potential.
Annual Bonus: Eligibility for our annual performance-based company bonus and annual merit increases.
Health & Wellness: Comprehensive Medical, Vision, and Dental insurance starting on Day One.
Retirement Planning: An exceptional 401(k) program with up to 6% company match.
Work-Life Balance: Generous paid vacation time, paid holidays, and predictable rotating 2-2-3 day shifts.
Family Support: Paid Parental Leave, plus Short-Term and Long-Term Disability.
Career Growth: Access to top-tier learning and development through Mars University.
Onsite Perks: Access to our onsite gym.
About Mars, Incorporated
Mars is a family-owned business with over a century of history making diverse products and offering services for people and the pets people love. We produce some of the world’s best-loved brands: M&M’s®, SNICKERS®, TWIX®, MILKY WAY®, DOVE®, PEDIGREE®, ROYAL CANIN®, WHISKAS®, EXTRA®, ORBIT®, 5™, SKITTLES®, BEN’S ORIGINAL®, and COCOAVIA®.
Alongside our consumer brands, we proudly take care of half of the world’s pets through our nutrition, health, and services businesses such as Banfield Pet Hospitals™, BluePearl®, Linnaeus, AniCura, VCA™, and Pet Partners™.
The Mars Five Principles – Quality, Responsibility, Mutuality, Efficiency, and Freedom – inspire our 130,000 Associates to take action every day toward creating the world we want tomorrow.

Conversion - Manage the efforts of operating teams of a multi-line, area, or technology on one shift in efficiently converting materials into quality products in a safe, secure, and sanitary manner within the product design specifications.

Ability to convey communications clearly and concisely.

Proficiency in Microsoft Office software (Word, Excel, etc), internet software, e-mail.

Experience in plant sanitation practices and procedures.

The Human Genome Project made human protein sequences accessible at scale; AlphaFold did the same for structure prediction. But our understanding biomolecular function is still in its infancy, limiting our ability to develop safe, effective medicines.
Our aim is to solve biomolecular function at scale. You will own outcomes related to activation and sustained usage by shaping how enablement drives measurable customer impact.

This role is based in San Francisco or New York. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.




IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Own the enablement of OpenAI products, including ChatGPT Enterprise and Agents, helping define effective enablement patterns that support adoption across business and technical teams within enterprise organizations.

 - Serve as a Subject Matter Expert (SME) for designated product areas, building deep expertise, supporting internal enablement, identifying emerging customer use cases for new product surfaces, and aggregating customer feedback to inform product development.

 - Lead customer enablement across the full customer lifecycle, from initial onboarding through expansion, optimization, and long-term adoption.

 - Design and deliver high-impact engagements, including onboarding sessions, advanced capability trainings, executive briefings, hackathons, and hands-on workshops for audiences ranging from senior leaders to working teams.

 - Drive customer activation, sustained usage, and measurable business value through structured enablement programs designed for durable, organization-wide adoption.

 - Partner closely with Sales, Solution Architects, and Delivery Leads to drive adoption across our core product suite.

 - Develop and refine reusable training assets, playbooks, and best practices based on patterns observed across customers and regions.

 - Gather customer feedback from training and enablement engagements, synthesize themes across accounts, and relay insights to internal stakeholders to inform product and program improvements.


YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:

 - Have strong product fluency across ChatGPT, Agents, and the broader OpenAI ecosystem, with a practical understanding of how AI capabilities can be applied to real world workflows and enterprise use cases.

 - Have experience leading workshops and enablement programs, with the ability to design learning journeys, facilitate live sessions, and respond to questions in real time.

 - Can identify patterns across customers and translate them into scalable approaches that improve adoption across the broader customer base.

 - Can connect product capabilities to concrete business outcomes such as productivity gains, operational efficiency, cost reduction, risk mitigation, or revenue impact.

description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

OpenAI Finance is responsible for ensuring the organization is set up for success in pursuit of its mission to ensure that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity.

The Controllership team delivers the financial truth that powers OpenAI’s growth. By translating operational activity into accurate, timely, and decision-grade financial data, we enable leadership to scale the business with confidence. Our commitment to rigorous controls and best-in-class systems ensures financial integrity as OpenAI grows. 

 


ABOUT THE ROLE

We are seeking a strategic and execution-oriented Accounting Lead, Hardware to build and scale inventory accounting capabilities across consumer hardware and robotics businesses. This role partners closely with Finance, Supply Chain, Manufacturing Operations, Technical Accounting, Strategic Finance, and Systems teams to establish scalable inventory and supply chain accounting processes and reporting infrastructure supporting rapid growth and product launches.

The ideal candidate brings strong accounting fundamentals, sound judgment, and a track record of building scalable processes in complex, evolving businesses. Inventory, cost accounting, or supply chain experience is preferred, and accounting experience supporting hardware, infrastructure, data centers, or other capital-intensive operations is also valuable. We welcome strong accounting professionals from other backgrounds who have demonstrated the ability to quickly learn unfamiliar business models and accounting topics and take ownership of new areas. This person should thrive in ambiguity, combine strategic thinking with hands-on execution, and communicate effectively with cross-functional partners and senior leadership.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

 


IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL: 


INVENTORY ACCOUNTING

 - Lead inventory and supply chain accounting across consumer hardware and robotics programs, including inventory valuation, supply chain/sourcing arrangements, manufacturing variances, reserves, and close processes.

 - Partner with Supply Chain, Operations, and Strategic Finance to support BOM accuracy, labor and overhead assumptions, operationalize supply chain strategies and gross margin analysis.

 - Develop scalable accounting processes for NPI, prototyping, engineering builds, and mass production.

 - Own inventory-related accounting policies and controls, including capitalization, overhead allocation, LCNRV/NRV assessments, rebates, freight, tariffs, and inventory controls.


ERP SYSTEMS & PROCESS DESIGN

 - Serve as a finance lead for Oracle Fusion manufacturing costing and inventory implementations, enhancements, and process optimization.

 - Partner with Systems, IT, and Operations to design scalable finance processes, controls, reporting structures, and operational workflows.

 - Partner with Systems and Operations to define accounting requirements and guide ERP design for product costing, inventory transactions, and related reporting and controls.


FINANCIAL CLOSE, REPORTING & CONTROLS

 - Lead monthly, quarterly, and annual cost accounting close activities and improve scalable reconciliations, reporting, and management review processes.

 - Partner with Strategic Finance on margin reporting, inventory analytics, and budget versus actual analysis.

 - Establish SOX-ready controls, support audits and technical accounting matters, and drive continuous improvement across close and reporting processes.


CROSS-FUNCTIONAL LEADERSHIP

 - Act as a strategic partner to Operations, Supply Chain, Procurement, and Program Management teams.

 - Translate ambiguous business needs into scalable accounting and operational frameworks.

 - Influence senior stakeholders through strong communication, executive presence, and data-driven recommendations.

 - Help build and scale the long-term roadmap for hardware controllership, manufacturing accounting, and operational finance infrastructure.

 


YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:

 - Bring strong accounting judgment and enjoy learning how physical products, infrastructure, and operational workflows translate into financial reporting.

 - Have a track record of quickly developing expertise in unfamiliar accounting areas, asking thoughtful questions, and turning what you learn into practical processes and controls.

 - Can comfortably operate between strategic leadership discussions and highly detailed operational accounting analyses.

 - Have strong executive presence and can communicate effectively with senior leadership and cross-functional partners.

 - Enjoy building scalable processes and infrastructure in fast-moving, ambiguous environments.

 - Are highly detail-oriented and maintain a strong control mindset while balancing business partnership.

 - Have a strong systems orientation and enjoy designing scalable ERP and reporting processes.

 - Are intellectually curious, proactive, and solutions-oriented.

 


QUALIFICATIONS


REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field.

 - 8+ years of progressive accounting experience, with ownership of complex accounting areas, close processes, or operational accounting.

 - Strong understanding of U.S. GAAP and demonstrated ability to research unfamiliar accounting topics and apply sound judgment.

 - Demonstrated ability to quickly learn new business models, systems, and operational processes and take ownership of unfamiliar accounting areas.

 - Experience building or improving accounting processes, reconciliations, controls, and reporting.

 - Strong systems aptitude and experience working with ERP systems and financial data.

 - Excellent analytical, communication, and cross-functional partnership skills.

 - Demonstrated ability to influence stakeholders and execute effectively in ambiguous, fast-moving environments.


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

Experience in one or more of the following areas is valuable; candidates are not expected to bring all of them:

 - Inventory, cost, manufacturing, or supply chain accounting, including inventory valuation, standard costing, manufacturing variances, overhead allocation, rebates and buy/sell etc.

 - Accounting supporting hardware, infrastructure, data centers, electronics, robotics, semiconductors, or other capital-intensive operations.

 - Work with contract manufacturers, global supply chains, hardware product launches, or manufacturing scale-up.

 - Oracle Fusion, particularly Costing and Inventory modules, or comparable ERP implementation and process improvement experience.

 - CPA and/or public accounting background.

 - Experience in a high-growth technology environment or building and leading accounting teams.

 


WHY THIS ROLE MATTERS

This role will play a foundational part in building the accounting infrastructure that supports the next generation of AI hardware products. You will help shape the systems, policies, controls, and operational processes that enable scalable manufacturing operations, reliable financial reporting, and launch readiness as the business rapidly grows.

description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Legal team helps address the cutting-edge legal questions that arise from developing and deploying advanced AI. The Security and Public Sector Legal team helps protect OpenAI’s technology, systems, data, and people and supports the safe and responsible use of our tools. We work closely with technical and operational teams to provide practical advice on novel, consequential, and fast-moving issues.



About the Role

We are seeking a counsel to help lead legal responses to cybersecurity and AI safety incidents. This is an opportunity to bring deep incident response expertise to some of the hardest questions in AI, and help build the legal frameworks and practices for answering them.



You will advise on complex cybersecurity incidents, from discovery through to resolution, and also help develop our response to incidents involving the safety of our models and tools. AI safety incident response is a new and rapidly evolving legal practice area. Your work will help define how frontier AI companies investigate and respond to safety events such as unexpected model behavior, degradation of safeguards, harmful uses of our services, and potential harm to third parties—often where established legal standards do not yet exist. Working directly with Security, Safety, Product, Engineering, and colleagues across Legal, you will advise on consequential decisions where established approaches may offer little guidance.



We are looking for a practical, dynamic lawyer who can turn incomplete information into clear recommendations, exercise sound judgment on novel questions, and follow matters through to resolution. You will help establish the facts, assess risks, and guide investigations, communications, remediation, and reporting. You will also turn lessons from individual incidents into durable response processes, helping further develop a legal function that evolves alongside the technology.



This role is based in Washington, D.C. or San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.



In this role, you will be:

 - Serving as legal lead on assigned cybersecurity and AI safety incidents, coordinating fact development, legal analysis and advising, cross-functional escalation, and follow-through with the response team.

 - Working with investigators to understand incident scope, attack paths, root cause, and affected systems and data, and potential third-party impacts, while helping teams distinguish established facts from gaps in the evidence.

 - Managing outside counsel and third party service provider engagements necessary to incident response.

 - Serving as key Legal point of contact for cross-functional teams.

 - Partnering with Privacy, Product, Regulatory, and other counsel to assess notification and reporting obligations, advise on timely customer and user communications, and coordinate third-party outreach and incident-related information sharing with industry peers and government partners.

 - Preparing concise incident updates and decision materials that distinguish established facts, uncertainties, options, and recommended next steps.

 - Developing severity-based escalation criteria, response playbooks, exercises, and clear decision and handoff processes for cybersecurity and AI safety incidents, adapting established practices to emerging model risks.

 - Supporting post-incident reviews, tracking agreed corrective actions, and turning lessons into practical improvements to safeguards and response processes.
   
   

You might thrive in this role if you have:

 - A JD and a license or qualification to practice law in your jurisdiction.

 - 5+ years of relevant experience.

 - Relevant legal experience managing cybersecurity or privacy incident responses or comparable complex technology investigations at a technology company, law firm, or government agency, including work with technical teams, other counsel, and communications partners.

 - The ability to translate technical findings into practical legal advice, with a working understanding of technical information.

 - Sound judgment under time pressure, clear communication of uncertainty, and an understanding of when to act, seek specialist advice, or escalate.

 - Clear, concise writing and the ability to keep cross-functional teams aligned through changing facts and competing priorities.

 - Ownership of details and follow-through, paired with collaborative work with colleagues who bring different expertise.

 - A strong interest in the novel challenges of AI safety and a willingness to help develop new approaches. Direct AI incident experience is helpful; strong transferable incident response skills are welcome.

 - Availability to participate in time-sensitive incident response, including occasional work outside normal business hours.

title: EDA Cloud & Developer Infrastructure Engineer
description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops AI-native silicon and system-level solutions for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. Building on efforts like Jalapeño, our custom silicon program, the team works across silicon architecture, RTL design, verification, physical design, systems software, and infrastructure to deliver highly performant, efficient, and scalable hardware solutions.

The Silicon & Systems team brings together hardware and software engineers to co-design and build the next generation of AI infrastructure. We operate at the intersection of silicon, systems, and software, tackling complex technical challenges across the full hardware development lifecycle, from early architecture and design through validation, deployment, and production.

About the Role

We’re looking for an Infrastructure Software Engineer to build and scale the infrastructure and developer workflows that power OpenAI’s custom silicon development. You’ll work closely with engineering teams across design verification, physical design, emulation, formal verification, and systems software to develop reliable, automated, and efficient workflows that accelerate hardware development.

In this role, you'll own and improve the cloud infrastructure, high-performance computing (HPC) environments, CI/CD pipelines, regression systems, and data platforms that support our silicon engineering teams. You'll translate complex hardware development requirements into scalable infrastructure solutions, reducing manual overhead, improving reliability, and enabling engineers to iterate faster.

This is a highly collaborative, hands-on role with opportunities to drive improvements across the entire hardware development lifecycle. We're looking for engineers who bring deep expertise in one or more infrastructure domains, strong software engineering fundamentals, and an interest in expanding their impact across the broader platform.

In this role, you will:

 - Build developer tools and workflows: Partner with hardware engineering teams to understand their development processes, identify bottlenecks, and build tooling, services, and APIs that automate workflows and accelerate engineering productivity.

 - Develop and scale regression infrastructure: Design, implement, and operate large-scale regression systems spanning job scheduling, execution, results collection, triage, and reporting, with a focus on performance, reliability, and reproducibility.

 - Own CI/CD infrastructure: Build and maintain automated pipelines for infrastructure, developer tooling, and cluster configurations, enabling safe deployments, testing, and continuous improvement.

 - Scale cloud and HPC environments: Design, provision, and operate cloud infrastructure and high-performance compute clusters, optimizing scheduling, capacity, reliability, and cost efficiency to support demanding silicon development workloads.

 - Build data infrastructure and observability: Develop data pipelines, databases, and monitoring systems that provide visibility into regression results, infrastructure health, resource utilization, and engineering efficiency.

 - Drive platform reliability and operational excellence: Troubleshoot complex infrastructure issues, improve monitoring and alerting, automate recovery processes, and build systems that are resilient, maintainable, and scalable.

 - Collaborate across hardware and software teams: Work directly with engineers across RTL, verification, physical design, emulation, and software to continuously improve the infrastructure supporting OpenAI's silicon development.

You might thrive in this role if you:

title: Editor, Research Team
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

OpenAI didn’t begin as a traditional company. It began as an idea: that artificial intelligence could be developed in a way that benefits everyone. As a creative team, our role is to help make sure the work behind that idea is understood, as it leaves the lab and meets the world.

This company works at the frontier of intelligence. Like any frontier, it’s unfinished, constantly shifting, and still being explored. Our job is to stay close to that uncertainty and help shape how this story gets told, in a way that feels grounded and human. We do this through campaigns, launches, films, brand systems, and work that doesn’t fit neatly into any of those categories yet. This team is for people who want to help shape something from the beginning.




ABOUT THE ROLE

As Editor, Research, you will help define the editorial voice of OpenAI’s research films. You will personally edit films that introduce new models, demonstrate emerging capabilities, and tell the stories behind our research. You will lead the editorial approach across assigned projects, guide collaborators, and set a high standard for cinematic storytelling and craft.

Your influence will begin well before footage reaches the edit. Working alongside researchers, filmmakers, and production, design, and product partners, you will shape concepts, develop narratives, test ideas through prototypes, and help plan shoots and demonstrations with the finished film in mind. You will bring clarity, humanity, and emotional depth to complex, evolving subjects, finding compelling ways to show the research while preserving its meaning and technical accuracy.

This is a hands-on leadership role for an exceptional editor who makes the work—and the people around them—better. You will take responsibility for editorial execution from concept through delivery, provide clear creative direction and actionable feedback, mentor editors, and lead external collaborators. You will also strengthen shared workflows and practices that help the studio deliver ambitious work across formats, platforms, markets, and timelines.




IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Lead editorial work from concept through final delivery, personally editing research launch films, cinematic demonstrations, and stories about the people behind the work while directing the contributions of other editors on assigned projects. Take responsibility for narrative quality and continuity across development, production support, editing, finishing, and delivery.

 - Set editorial direction across assigned projects, translating creative goals into a clear approach and helping internal editors and external partners deliver cohesive, distinctive work. Bring exceptional judgment to story, structure, pacing, performance, music, sound, and the relationship between picture and graphics.

 - Shape stories from the beginning, partnering with filmmakers and researchers on concepts, treatments, scripts, interview questions, and demonstration coverage. Use rough cuts, story assemblies, and rapid prototypes to find the strongest narrative and inform what needs to be captured.

 - Lead editorial reviews, presenting work and explaining creative choices clearly. Synthesize feedback from researchers and creative partners into focused revisions that strengthen the film while preserving the accuracy of demonstrations and technical explanations.

 - Lead editors and editorial collaborators on assigned projects, setting clear expectations, delegating work, supporting onboarding, and providing actionable creative feedback. Mentor editors and assistant editors to strengthen their storytelling, technical skills, and independent judgment.

 - Partner with production to scope and deliver editorial work, assessing resource needs, estimating effort, setting realistic schedules, and recommending the right talent for each assignment. Brief and creatively lead external editorial partners, surface risks early, and help resolve competing priorities.

 - Guide work through finishing, collaborating with motion designers, sound designers, composers, colorists, and VFX artists to preserve the creative intent through final delivery.

 - Strengthen editorial workflows and uphold shared standards, including project setup, technical specifications, media organization, version control, review processes, secure asset handling, handoffs, archival, and delivery quality. Identify improvements through project experience and share effective practices with the team.

 - Own the editorial approach to adaptations of assigned work, guiding cutdowns, platform variations, and localized versions. Review work for narrative clarity, cultural context, and consistency of meaning, tone, and emotional impact.

 - Evaluate new tools and approaches, including AI-enabled creative tools, that expand the studio’s ability to explore, edit, and deliver work. Share findings and partner with editorial leadership on testing and adoption.

 - Collaborate closely with researchers to translate complex capabilities into compelling stories, developing a working understanding of what a model can do and what a demonstration actually shows. Find inventive ways to make those capabilities clear on screen, and work with researchers to ensure edits preserve the context and meaning of the underlying work.

 - Partner with editorial and post-production leadership to build and maintain a world-class team, helping identify exceptional talent, mentor collaborators, and create a culture of creative excellence, collaboration, and shared craft.




YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:

 - Have 8+ years of relevant editing experience and a portfolio demonstrating exceptional cinematic storytelling, with work that shows your ability to make complex ideas compelling and accessible. Experience with research, science, technology, documentary, or demonstration-driven films is especially relevant.

 - Have experience leading editorial projects and guiding other editors or external partners, with clear examples of how your direction improved the work.

 - Combine strong narrative instincts with precise execution, and can build a compelling film from varied material, including interviews, demonstrations, live-action footage, and model-generated content.

 - Remain deeply engaged in the craft of editing while comfortably taking responsibility for the quality and progress of work beyond your own timeline.

 - Can articulate why an edit works, give specific and constructive feedback, and help others find solutions while encouraging their creative ownership.

 - Bring advanced proficiency in professional editing software and a strong understanding of post-production, including media workflows, motion graphics, sound, color, VFX, finishing, localization, versioning, archival, and delivery.

 - Have experience delegating work, onboarding collaborators, and coordinating editorial contributions across a project.

 - Build trust with researchers and creative partners, ask thoughtful questions to understand unfamiliar technical ideas, and translate feedback into clear editorial decisions under deadline pressure.

 - Know how to balance creative ambition with schedules and resources, and introduce enough structure to help teams do their best work.

 - Are curious about AI research and emerging creative technologies, and excited to explore how cinematic storytelling can reveal new capabilities and the people behind them.

ABOUT THE TEAM

ABOUT THE ROLE

We are looking for an accountant to own an assigned portfolio of intercompany and investment accounting processes. You will manage recurring reconciliations, coordinate the accounting for intercompany funding, review transfer pricing calculations and journal entries, and partner with Technical Accounting on investments. A fundamental part of the role is understanding OpenAI's group structure, partnering closely with Tax on complex transactions, and providing guidance to the wider accounting group on intercompany flows.

You will own work from source data through close, resolve routine issues independently, and improve processes within established policies and approval controls. You will identify matters requiring technical assessment early and bring clear analysis and supporting facts for review. You will be a pivotal interface between global finance teams, treasury, tax, and systems to support our mission-critical financial close and reporting processes.

 


WHAT YOU WILL DO

 - Develop and maintain an understanding of OpenAI's group structure, ownership relationships and intercompany arrangements and flows.

 - Partner with Tax, Technical Accounting and your manager to assess complex intercompany transactions and coordinate implementation of agreed accounting treatments.

 - Provide guidance to the wider accounting group on intercompany flows, accounting treatments and cross-entity accounting questions.

 - Own monthly and quarterly close activities for assigned accounts, including reconciliations and resolution of reconciling items.

 - Coordinate accounting for intercompany funding and settlements with Treasury and Tax, within established approval and execution controls.

 - Review transfer pricing calculations prepared by the TP team for intercompany accounting accuracy, including entity, account, currency and FX rate treatment.

 - Prepare and review assigned journal entries for accuracy, supporting evidence and consistency with approved accounting treatments and controls.

 - Maintain investment accounting records and reconciliations, implement agreed accounting treatments, and partner with Technical Accounting and your manager on new transactions and technical assessments.

 - Careful review habits and the ability to trace a calculation or journal entry to its source, explain discrepancies, and document how they were resolved.

title: ML Silicon Performance Lead
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM:

OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops AI-native silicon and system-level solutions for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. Building on efforts like Jalapeño, the team is developing future generations of AI-native silicon and tightly integrated systems to power the next generation of frontier models. By co-designing chips, systems, tools, and methodologies, the team helps deliver faster, more efficient, and production-ready hardware for OpenAI’s supercomputing platform.


ABOUT THE ROLE:

We’re looking for an ML Silicon Performance Lead to drive hardware/software co-design for our silicon architecture. You will work across models, kernels, compilers, and silicon to shape how ML workloads map to hardware—and how the hardware should evolve to support them. Your work will connect model and workload requirements with compute, memory, and specialized acceleration capabilities to maximize performance, efficiency, and scalability across current and future generations of AI silicon.

You’ll partner closely with ML research, compiler, and silicon architecture teams to jointly develop software approaches and hardware capabilities. From kernel mapping and quantization to new data structures and specialized IP, you’ll evaluate hardware and software tradeoffs to improve performance, efficiency, and utilization across large-scale AI workloads. Through performance modeling, simulation, and hands-on optimization, you’ll guide architectural decisions and validate improvements on representative workloads.


IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Drive hardware/software co-design across ML research, compiler, and silicon teams, jointly shaping kernel implementations and hardware capabilities to meet workload performance and efficiency goals.

 - Partner with ML research to translate model and workload needs into kernel performance targets and compute, memory capacity, and bandwidth requirements, feeding hardware constraints and opportunities back into model and algorithm choices.

 - Map and optimize ML kernels for architecture, using insights from data movement, memory hierarchy, and execution efficiency to guide both software improvements and hardware design.

 - Co-design support for new data structures and quantization formats across kernels, compilers, and silicon, balancing model quality, numerical behavior, performance, power, and implementation cost.

 - Define and help develop specialized acceleration IP, working with compiler and silicon partners to determine the right division of functionality across software, instructions, and dedicated hardware.

 - Drive ML performance modeling and simulation with the compiler team to compare hardware/software design options, expose bottlenecks, and quantify end-to-end benefits on representative workloads.

 - Partner with the Silicon Architecture lead and silicon team to specify and validate new IP, using kernel and simulation results to refine requirements and prioritize architectural improvements.


YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:

 - Have deep experience with ML accelerator architecture and how compute resources, memory systems, and data movement shape workload performance.

 - Can translate model-level behavior into concrete kernel requirements and hardware design decisions.

 - Have built or used accelerator performance models and simulators, and know how to validate their assumptions and interpret their limitations.

 - Have hands-on experience optimizing ML kernels, including identifying bottlenecks and improving utilization, locality, and execution efficiency.

 - Understand quantization and numerical formats, including their implications for model quality, memory bandwidth, compute efficiency, and hardware support.

 - Have experience with hardware/software co-design and can reason about whether a capability belongs in a kernel, compiler, instruction set, or dedicated hardware.

 - Work effectively across research, compiler, and silicon teams, bringing clarity to ambiguous requirements and building alignment through technical evidence.

title: Silicon Design Lead
description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops AI-native silicon and system-level solutions for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. Building on efforts like Jalapeño, the team is developing future generations of AI-native silicon and tightly integrated systems to power the next generation of frontier models. By co-designing chips, systems, tools, and methodologies, the team helps deliver faster, more efficient, and production-ready hardware for OpenAI’s supercomputing platform.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Silicon Design Lead to drive architecture, microarchitecture, and implementation of key IP and subsystems for our AI hardware platforms. You will translate functional, performance, and security requirements into efficient silicon designs, owning technical decisions from architectural definition through implementation and integration.

Part of this role will focus on hardware security implementation in close partnership with OpenAI’s Security team. While the Security team owns the overarching security architecture and requirements, you will translate those requirements into silicon microarchitecture and implementation, balancing security capabilities with performance, power, area, and design complexity. The other part of this role will focus on driving general silicon architecture/microarchitecture. 

In this role, you will:

 - Own architecture, microarchitecture, and implementation of silicon IP and subsystems, from requirements and design specifications through integration and validation.

 - Define hardware interfaces, data flows, and microarchitectural tradeoffs to meet functional, performance, power, and area requirements.

 - Partner closely with OpenAI’s Security team to translate security architecture, requirements, and threat models into implementable hardware capabilities.

 - Design and integrate hardware security mechanisms, including encryption, key management, access controls, isolation, and data protection across silicon subsystems.

 - Evaluate architectural and implementation tradeoffs to ensure security capabilities meet functional and performance requirements.

 - Collaborate with silicon architects, RTL, verification, firmware, and software teams to drive subsystem design, integration, and validation.

 - Review and contribute to RTL implementations, ensuring designs align with architectural intent and system requirements.

 - Evaluate existing and third-party IP, identify architectural or implementation gaps, and drive solutions across subsystem boundaries.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have strong experience in silicon IP or subsystem-level architecture, microarchitecture, and implementation.

 - Have owned hardware IP or subsystem designs from architectural definition through implementation and integration.

 - Have experience implementing hardware security features such as memory encryption, key management, access controls, isolation, or secure boot.

 - Understand how to translate functional and security requirements into hardware architectures, interfaces, and microarchitectural specifications.

 - Have working knowledge of RTL design and coding proficiency in Verilog or SystemVerilog, with the ability to read, review, and contribute to RTL.

 - Can evaluate performance, power, area, and complexity tradeoffs across silicon designs.

 - Work effectively across security, silicon architecture, RTL, verification, firmware, and software teams to drive designs from concept through execution.

title: Staff Backend Engineer, Financial Engineering
description:
About the Team

Financial Engineering (FinEng) builds the financial systems behind ChatGPT, Codex, and OpenAI’s API platform. These products serve people, developers, and businesses around the world. We make them easy to buy, use, and pay for. Our systems support everything from individual subscriptions to usage-based billing and complex enterprise agreements.

We also build the foundations for how products are packaged, accessed, and used: product catalogs, SKUs and bundles, workspaces, entitlements, and usage metering. These systems connect what customers purchase to the capabilities they can access and the usage they can manage.

That reach creates challenging engineering problems. We build services and data pipelines that handle large volumes of usage and transactions, keep payments, product access, and financial records consistent across systems, and adapt as products and pricing change. The same foundations must support a simple checkout and the detailed spending controls a large business needs.

Your work will help teams launch new products faster and give customers confidence in what they are paying for. The work spans customer experiences, backend services, and data systems, with opportunities to influence technical design and see your work through to production.

We’re hiring Staff+ engineers with strong backend experience. Experience in payments, billing, or financial systems is a strong plus, but not required.

In this role, you will:

 - Design and build systems for purchasing, payments, subscriptions, and billing across OpenAI products and global markets.

 - Build product catalogs, SKUs, and bundles that let product teams launch new offerings and evolve how products are packaged.

 - Develop workspace and entitlement systems that connect purchases and subscriptions to product access for individuals and teams.

 - Keep charges and product access correct when requests are retried, updates arrive late, or another service fails.

 - Build metering systems, data pipelines, and APIs that turn large volumes of usage into accurate bills, timely spending information, and records that are easy to trace and verify.

 - Create reusable building blocks that let product teams launch new offerings, pricing, and payment options without rebuilding the foundations each time.

 - Make complex financial workflows simple for customers and internal teams, using customer feedback and experiments to improve the experience.

You will combine technical judgment and program leadership to connect capacity planning with the deployment, scheduling, and optimization systems that make allocated compute usable.

description:

Our award-winning products help our global community gain a deeper knowledge of their readiness, activity, and sleep quality by using their Oura Ring and its connected app. We've helped millions of people understand and improve their health by providing daily insights and practical steps to inspire healthy lifestyles.
Empowering the world starts with living our values and empowering our team. As a quickly growing company focused on helping people live healthier and happier lives, we ensure that our team members have what they need to do their best work — both in and out of the office.
We’re looking for a Director, Quality to lead quality strategy and execution across Oura’s global engineering organization and supply chain.
What You Will Do:
In this role, you will ensure that quality and reliability are designed into our products, components, suppliers, and manufacturing processes from concept through development, launch, ramp, and sustaining operations. You will lead a global team of quality professionals and partner closely with Product Development, Hardware, Software, Reliability, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Customer Experience, and external suppliers.
You will connect customer and field needs to engineering requirements, component controls, supplier capability, manufacturing performance, and product reliability. Your team will help Oura identify risks early, make evidence-based decisions, prevent defects, and resolve complex issues with durable corrective actions.
This is a broad, highly cross-functional leadership role for an experienced quality executive who can set strategy, develop talent, influence engineering and operations leaders, and engage deeply in both product and supply chain quality when needed.
Set the quality strategy: Define Oura’s quality vision, operating model, standards, metrics, and priorities across product development, components, suppliers, manufacturing, reliability, and the field.
Lead and develop a global quality organization: Build, mentor, and manage a high-performing team across product quality, component quality, supplier quality, manufacturing quality, reliability, program quality, and sustaining quality.
Embed quality across the product lifecycle: Establish effective quality gates and decision criteria from concept and architecture through EVT, DVT, PVT, launch, ramp, and sustaining.
Partner with engineering and product leaders: Influence product architecture, design decisions, materials, specifications, interfaces, validation plans, and manufacturability to prevent quality and reliability issues.
Strengthen component and supplier quality: Translate product requirements into component specifications, supplier quality requirements, qualification plans, control plans, inspection strategies, and process controls. Drive supplier capability and performance across the global supply chain.
Drive manufacturing readiness and performance: Ensure production processes are validated and controlled, with appropriate PFMEA, process capability, measurement systems, yield targets, traceability, reaction plans, and continuous improvement mechanisms.
Lead risk-based quality planning: Establish disciplined use of DFMEA, PFMEA, reliability planning, design reviews, tolerance analysis, GR&R, SPC, DOE, and risk-based verification and validation.
Own complex problem solving: Lead containment, failure analysis, root-cause investigation, corrective action, preventive action, and verification of effectiveness for product, component, supplier, manufacturing, reliability, and field issues.
Build strong field-quality feedback loops: Use warranty, returns, customer support, field failure, reliability, manufacturing, and supplier data to identify systemic risks and drive improvements that reduce member impact and cost of poor quality.
Lead launch and ramp readiness: Review product and component qualification, supplier capability, manufacturing readiness, validation evidence, yield, open risks, reliability results, and corrective actions before launch and ramp decisions.
Govern quality-related changes: Ensure design, material, component, supplier, process, software, and manufacturing changes are evaluated for quality and reliability impact and implemented consistently through ECR/ECN and change-control processes.
Establish a data-driven quality operating system: Define leading and lagging indicators across development, suppliers, manufacturing, and the field. Improve data quality, traceability, dashboards, and escalation mechanisms.
Drive continuous improvement: Reduce defects, escapes, returns, warranty claims, rework, scrap, and other sources of cost of poor quality while improving product reliability, supplier performance, and customer experience.
Influence cross-functional decisions: Provide clear, risk-based recommendations when quality, schedule, cost, performance, capacity, and supply continuity priorities compete.
Communicate with senior leadership: Present concise assessments of product risk, supplier and manufacturing performance, launch readiness, field quality, and improvement priorities.
Build a culture of prevention and accountability: Make quality a shared responsibility across engineering and operations, with clear ownership for requirements, validation, supplier controls, manufacturing execution, and sustained performance.
This is a hybrid role out of our San Francisco office.
What you'll bring
15+ years of experience in product quality, supplier quality, manufacturing quality, reliability, operations quality, or a related engineering discipline, including significant people leadership experience.
Demonstrated success leading quality for complex, high-volume consumer electronics, wearable, medical-adjacent, or similarly reliability-sensitive products.
Experience leading and developing teams across one or more of the following areas: product quality, component quality, supplier quality, manufacturing quality, reliability, program quality, or sustaining quality.
A track record of establishing quality strategy, operating mechanisms, and measurable improvements from early product development through launch and sustaining.
Strong understanding of product development, design verification and validation, component qualification, reliability engineering, supplier quality, manufacturing processes, and production ramp.
Strong command of quality and problem-solving methods, including FMEA, 8D, CAPA, SPC, GR&R, DOE, root-cause analysis, control plans, and process capability.
Experience using engineering, field, warranty, customer support, supplier, and manufacturing data to identify systemic risks and drive corrective action.
Demonstrated ability to influence engineering, operations, suppliers, and executive leadership without relying solely on direct authority.
Experience with engineering change control, supplier changes, component qualification, process validation, manufacturing readiness, or production quality improvement.
Strong understanding of DFM/DFA, GD&T, Lean and Six Sigma principles, measurement systems, and quality management systems.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate complex technical risks into concise decisions and actions.
A self-directed, pragmatic, and resilient leadership style, with a willingness to engage deeply in details while maintaining a strategic perspective.
Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Industrial, Systems, Manufacturing, or a related engineering field required; advanced degree or quality certification is a plus.
Preferred qualifications
Experience with both product quality and supplier or manufacturing quality, or demonstrated ability to operate effectively across both domains.
Experience with batteries, electronics, sensors, RF systems, precision mechanics, adhesives, miniaturized assemblies, or other demanding product technologies.
Experience leading quality for products that combine hardware, firmware, software, and cloud-enabled member experiences.
Experience building or scaling quality management systems during rapid company growth.
Familiarity with product safety, regulatory, compliance, traceability, and risk-management requirements relevant to wearable technology.
Experience with supplier development, APQP, PPAP, SCAR processes, multi-source strategies, capacity expansion, or major manufacturing transitions.
Experience working across multiple countries, engineering sites, suppliers, and manufacturing partners.

description:
ABOUT QUINCE
Quince is a destination for builders, creators, innovators, and operators who want to come together and challenge the status quo. Our mission is simple: make really high quality essentials for really low prices, fairly and sustainably. We deliver on that mission through a unique manufacturer-to-consumer (M2C) model eliminating the layers of traditional retail that add cost and result in consumers paying more than they need to. We find, build relationships with, and work directly with the manufacturing partners behind some of the world’s finest products. From there, our teams design smart, efficient operational processes  and build and deploy proprietary technology, AI, and analytics to help us scale fast.
What began with a small assortment of elevated basics has quickly grown into a cross-category brand spanning apparel, accessories, home goods, and more. Today, tens of millions of people across a growing number of countries come – and return – to Quince because they trust us to deliver.
OUR CULTURE
Quince is a culture built for builders by builders. Our way of working starts with a blank sheet of paper.
